content.text: Internet law: A practical introduction. The Internet is becoming increasingly important in business and society and is no longer a matter of thought in many areas. A flood of laws and the case law that has not yet been consolidated in many areas of Internet law sometimes creates great uncertainty among users. Internet law introduces easily understandable and at the same time in all important topics: - disputes about domain names - Internet offers and copyright - advertising in the net - contracts in the Internet - e-commerce - computer crime and criminal law - data protection - procedural issues The author places particular importance on a high practical relevance. Using many examples, a concrete insight into the application possibilities and fields of application is given. All current legal reforms are taken into account. Internet law is aimed at students and lecturers in the fields of business administration, business engineering, computer science and law at universities, colleges of applied sciences and professional academies.
content.title_en: Internet law : A practical introduction

content.text: Pervasive Gaming as a new way of influencing thinking and acting: An application in the learning context. Pervasive Games are new game formats in which the real world merges with the virtual. If these game concepts are used in conjunction with mobile phones as interaction and communication media to support learning processes, this results in a high intrinsic motivation especially among young people. Francika Edegger describes the design, development and practical application of the Pervasive Game "Digital Economy" which is intended to lead to the transmission of learning content in modern teaching. To this end, she first designs a useful game mechanism and then checks the practical suitability of an empirical study in terms of learning success and learning efficiency. The author shows that the Pervasive Gaming with mobile phones as an interaction and communication medium results in increased energy activation, a more positive attitude towards learning content and a more efficient knowledge transfer. Problem definition and approach -- Information systems in the learning context -- Potentials of Pervasive Games -- Pervasive Learning Game "Digital Economy" - Information System -- Behavior Scientific Evaluation of the Pervasive Games
content.title_en: Pervasive Gaming as a new way to influence thinking and action : An application in the learning context

content.text: The measurement of the success of internal communication processes: Effectiveness and efficiency measurement of face-to-face meetings. The measurement of the success of internal communication processes in meetings, in which many managers spend a large part of their time, is a task of controlling. In order to optimize the processes, communication trainings are carried out over and over again, but there is usually no systematic control of the success of such communication-contributing measures. In the sense of the performance measurement, Alexandra Rausch designs a model of indicators based on the extended 3-level concept, which serves as a measuring instrument for determining success-relevant factors in meetings as well as effectiveness and efficiency. Through the successive modification and optimization of the model in the course of an empirical longitudinal analysis (SPSS, PLS), the author demonstrates the relevant success factors and demonstrates the importance of the measurement instrument for the optimization of the meeting culture in companies.
content.title_en: Controlling of internal communication processes : Effectiveness and efficiency measurement of face-to-face meetings

content.text: Quality of software systems: A pattern-based knowledge model to support the design and evaluation of software architectures. The basics and frameworks of the design of software architectures -- Software architecture assessment -- Patterns in the context of the design and evaluation of software architectures -- Development of a pattern-based knowledge model -- Final consideration. The use of software-intensive systems is increasingly shaping processes in companies and administrations, and the dependence on these systems is increasing. The development of IT systems that meet requirements therefore requires more resources and is often associated with major risks that need to be efficiently controlled and controlled in the context of the software development process. Stefan Malich develops a pattern-based knowledge model that allows the relationships between the design decisions regarding software architecture and the resulting effects on the quality of the system to be determined and documented. The applicability of his model is demonstrated by the classification of patterns from selected pattern catalogs. The mapped patterns can be evaluated and evaluated more efficiently by the resulting, expandable model in terms of quality impact.
content.title_en: Quality of software systems : A pattern-based knowledge model to support the design and evaluation of software architectures

content.text: E-commerce business models in the German tourism market. Theoretical basics -- Market-specific basics -- Conceptualization of empirical analysis -- Case studies -- Cross case analysis -- Refinement of typology -- Market outlook -- Theoretical findings -- Final remarks and further research needs. The Internet has changed the German travel and tourism industry in a relatively short time. Over the years, dominant distribution structures and ways of customer addressing have been questioned and adapted. At the same time, a high industry dynamics and competitive intensity developed between a large number of companies, which are characterized by different origins and resources. The question arises which companies have the best chances of asserting themselves in the long term and which strategic adjustments are necessary for individual business models to improve their future prospects. Based on a comprehensive case studies of selected e-commerce business models in the German tourism market and using methods of strategy teaching Philipp Wohland examines competitive advantages of individual business models and thus explains their success. With the help of a cross-case comparison, he works out the compatibility advantages and evaluates the sustainability of the business model.
content.title_en: E-commerce business models in the German tourism market

content.text: Environmental innovations through cooperations: Using the example of a voluntary industry agreement. Promoting innovation through environmental-oriented cooperation -- Basics and framework conditions of environmental innovations -- Conceptual foundations and design possibilities of environmental-oriented cooperations -- Theoretical cooperation approaches and their contribution to innovation promotion -- Conceptual and methodological considerations for the analysis of the cooperation contribution to environmental innovations -- Analysis of environmental innovation potentials in environmental-oriented cooperations: impact and conditions -- Implications for environmental-oriented industry innovation systems and summary. Environmental-oriented cooperation is considered an appropriate form to stimulate and support company change processes in environmental protection in order to improve innovation and competitiveness in this way. Maria Urbaniec investigates the contribution of environmental-oriented cooperations to environmental innovations. On the theoretical basis of environmental innovation and cooperation research, she develops a heuristic analysis framework for the empirical analysis of environmental-oriented cooperation.
content.title_en: Environmental Innovations through Cooperations : Using the example of a voluntary sectoral agreement

content.text: Media policy in the 1980s: Power policies of the parties in the course of the introduction of the dual broadcasting system. Media policy mutated in the 1980s to power politics and the control of public television significantly influenced the agenda of the People's Party. In order to assess the overall problem, the author had access for the first time to the complete confidential media policy documents (committee protocols, correspondence etc.) of SPD and CDU/CSU. Hermanni shows in this basic work the power policies and influence possibilities of the parties in the struggle for a dual broadcasting order in detail and assesses them. The analyses also support a survey among the former decision-makers of the People's Party (especially former prime ministers) about their motivations pro or contra New Media/Private TV. Open and detailed, the respondents reflect their power policy attitudes.
content.title_en: Media policy in the 1980s: political strategies of the parties in the context of the introduction of the dual broadcasting system

content.text: Ageing and time: The influence of demographic change on time structures.The influence of demographic change on individual and social time structures Current social time structures are economically permeated and will experience a profound change with demographic changes.This work examines life in old age as well as the goals and developments that could become important as life ages progress.The challenge for the design of a "good" life in old age lies in the reflections on how and what elements could become important for this. And one thing is very clear: Active ageing is only "good" if it reaches beyond being busy and can create new meaningful relationships to one's own life. Dr. Christine Meyer is a university assistant at the Institute of Social Pedagogy at the University of Lüneburg.
content.title_en: Ageing and Time : The Influence of Demographic Change on Time Structures

content.text: Islam as a field of discourse : Images of Islam in Germany. The book analyses the current discourse on the integration of Islam into German society. It shows how different actors establish certain images of Islam in public, in order to support positions and represent interests. On this basis, the perspectives that German Islam has under these discursive conditions are discussed. The book analyses the current discourse on the integration of Islam into German society. It is shown how different actors establish certain images of Islam in public, in order to support positions and represent interests. On this basis, the perspectives that German Islam has under these discursive conditions are discussed.
content.title_en: Islam as a field of discourse : Images of Islam in Germany

content.text: Urban security and participation: the importance and function of civic participation in municipal crime prevention. Since the early 1990s, civic participation has been presented as an important resource for urban security policies in the course of community policing in the USA and municipal crime prevention in Germany. The work empirically answers the question whether participatory project forms could be established permanently in the field of security policy and whether these had an effect on the public life of cities. The situation of criminal preventive committee work in twelve German cities is examined empirically and deepened by means of two case studies on Berlin and Stuttgart. The situation in the USA is analysed in more detail by means of a case study on Chicago.
content.title_en: Urban security and participation: the role and role of civic participation in municipal crime prevention

content.text: Aesthetics of pleasure : Urban spaces between professional aesthetics and amateur taste. Architects have different aesthetic ideas than lay people. Moreover, they are also deceived by the amateur taste and this the more their professional aesthetic ideas differ from the amateur taste. This discrepancy between professional aesthetics and amateur taste is the subject of this study. On the one hand, it is intended to determine the aesthetic demands of the population on urban spaces, on the other hand, to what extent and in what extent they differ from the professional aesthetics of landscape architects. The thesis is that these differences have become more pronounced in recent decades.
content.title_en: Aesthetics of Pleasant : Urban spaces between professional aesthetics and amateur taste

content.text: The authors from various scientific disciplines and practice show important topics of intensified district research under the focus of 'theoretical perspectives on the district', 'processes, control and governance in the district context' and 'quartiere im sozialdemographical Wandel'. Dr. Olaf Schnur is a research associate at the Humboldt University of Berlin's Geographic Institute. His main areas of work are urban and social geography, urban development in large cities and social urban development. Residential districts, urban districts, neighbourhoods: For residents, they are no more and no less than the local anchoring in the (large) city and the globalized world. In science, there are now diverse discourses about the local neighbourhood, not least in the context of spatial theory debates. But as a strategic planning category, the district is also important? It has as a meso-level between regional, city and individual levels in recent years virtually made careers: urban development programs such as "social city" or "urban construction east/west" and also as a strategic planning category of residential areas, the district industry is increasingly focused on more on the topic of the district industry and more on the district industry.
content.title_en: Quarter research : Between theory and practice

content.text: Holistic innovation: Concept, methodology and examples. Innovations can shape our future. But in practice, many challenges arise: How can one think a complex future ahead? How can one simultaneously take risks and take care of value creation? How can one effectively combine different interests and competences? And how can one organize innovation processes in such a way that they are systematically acted upon and yet remain room for visions and creativity? In this book Eckehard Fozzy Moritz gives answers to such questions. Using various examples he develops a holistic methodology that helps to generate innovations with diffusely formulated objectives. As a basis he has chosen sport, especially in sport, because the need and potential for innovation are particularly great. In the introductory chapter, the phenomena of sport and innovation and their interactions are discussed in greater detail. In the second chapter, Moritz brings together the various building blocks for his methodology to present in the third and fourth chapters the development and application of the methodology. This book addresses all practitioners, managers and students who want to be innovative or need to be innovative! Innovation is not equal to innovation: About a phenomenon and its chosen application field of application – Holistic development – The approach to the approach to the development – The approach to the approach to the approach to the approach to the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of practice.
content.title_en: Holistic innovation : concept, methodology and examples

content.text: The brown coal mining industry: meaning, planning, operation, technology, environment. "The brown coal mining industry" deals with the overall complex of the extraction of brown coal in opencast mining at present in theory and practice. There is currently no monograph of this kind. Therefore, the editors have set themselves the goal to work on and compile the necessary overall view of the topic and this in particular against the background of a much greater importance of brown coal mining in the united Germany. The present book is aimed at people who want to obtain a comprehensive overview of this sector of raw materials production and the energy economy. In particular, it is intended to serve employees who are already working in the relevant companies, in the supply industry or at licensing authorities. Moreover, it is intended for students of engineering and especially of raw materials sciences and thus future managers in mining or related industries. The focus of the study is on the large field of operation in Germany, which is the production of brown coal, including the production of the brown coal.
content.title_en: The lignite mining industry : importance, planning, operation, technology, environment

content.text: Exam preparation for IT professions : The really important exam content, sorted by learning fields — exercise tasks with commented solutions. The operation and its environment -- Business processes and operational organization -- Information sources and working methods -- Simple IT systems -- Technical English -- Development and provision of application systems -- Networked IT systems -- Market and customer relationships -- Public networks and services -- Supervision of IT systems -- Accounting and controlling. This book is written for prospective IT specialists, IT system electronics specialists, IT system merchants and IT merchants who are just ahead of the exam and offers a clear, compact guide to exam preparation.
content.title_en: Exam preparation for IT professions : The really important exam content, sorted by learning fields — Exercise tasks with commented solutions

content.text: Performance Management : Performance acquisition and management in companies and public administrations. Performance acquisition and management in private companies -- Performance acquisition and management in public administrations -- Public performance management presented in the field of application of fire brigade -- Summary of results and outlook. Sustainable financial bottlenecks in households and changed requirements for government and administrations require a radical rethink in the management of public resources, processes and services. Therefore, private management methods are now also used in public administration. Dennis Hilgers examines methods and concepts for performance recognition and management in the private sector as well as in the context of public administrations. Performance Management, a generic term for instruments for efficiency and efficiency management, also stands for the strategy-oriented management process of performance and impact-oriented management with regard to citizens' needs. The author shows that the reform of accounting is of particular importance. Finally, the author refers the findings to the concrete example of the fire brigade.
content.title_en: Performance Management : Performance acquisition and management in companies and public administrations

content.text: Tour planning in road freight transport. Especially in the distribution of goods, but increasingly also in the return transport of valuable materials, in operational practice tour planning problems of different structures occur, as industry or even company-specific conditions have to be taken into account. Competitive pressure and rising costs force better planning with higher requirements on the quality and feasibility of tour plans. Claudius Ohrt examines the requirements for real tour planning in road freight transport. The author develops a procedure that is characterized by general applicability and maximum flexibility. It is applicable to different problem structures and also takes into account other marginal conditions. Moreover, with the help of the procedure solutions of very high quality for various academic and practical tour planning problems can be determined. Complex problems of the operational day-to-day business can be solved and directly feasible tour plans can be determined. Introduction -- Basics of tour planning -- Characteristics of tour planning in road freight transport -- Methods and models of tour planning - Modelling of tour planning problems in road freight transport -- Design of a route planning procedure -- Application examples of road freight traffic - Outlook.
content.title_en: Road freight road transport route planning

content.text: Supply management in the hotel industry: basics, success factors and design recommendations. Theoretical consideration of supply management and hotel industry -- Theoretical basis, research concept and investigation model -- Quantitative investigation -- Qualitative investigation -- Final examination and outlook. An efficient, process- and customer-oriented and timely supply management means for companies a strategic competitive advantage that increases company value. In the increasingly dynamic competitive environment, service companies such as the three to five-star hotels in Germany achieve decisive advantages through supply management, whereby current cases from theory and practice show the need for a professionalization of purchasing. Christine Schüffler presents the status quo and the success factors of purchasing and supply management in the three to five-star hotel industry. The basis for this is a large-scale empirical investigation as well as selected case studies of hotel chains and individual hotels in Germany. The author shows success factors and their impact relationships between supply management and provides valuable design concepts for the hotel industry.
content.title_en: Supply management in the hotel industry : basics, success factors and design recommendations

content.text: The way to virtual management -- analysis of public administration processes -- modelling of e-government processes -- the Rhine-Neckar Metropolitan Region (MRN) -- modelling of e-government processes and their integration into the structures of the MRN -- modelling of different e-government processes in the MRN -- harmonisation of e-government processes in the EU and the MRN -- final analysis. E-government summarizes the efforts to improve processes within and between state institutions and between these institutions and citizens respectively companies using information and communication technologies. Unlike the many successful business models in the private e-business, however, many e-government projects fail. This is due, among other things, to the question of legal certainty and the obligation of public business processes. Sebastian Olbrich develops a methodology model that explicitly validates the business modeling method. The practice process is legally based on the practice process.
content.title_en: Modelling of legal framework conditions for e-government administrative processes

content.text: Network Analysis and Network Theory : A New Paradigm in Social Sciences. In network analysis and network theory, patterns of relations are at the heart of research. Network research, although it is based on classics of sociology and on various theoretical directions and well-known methods, has in recent years been the result of the new paradigm of network research, but a variety of theoretical and empirical research has been initiated, which has led to the emergence of this field into perhaps the most dynamic field in social research. This is due to the fact that network research can provide answers to numerous questions that have not yet been or are not yet sufficiently clarified. In the volume, important theoretical strands and methodological approaches are discussed, both in an introductory and in the form of the latest research results.
content.title_en: Network Analysis and Network Theory : A New Paradigm in Social Sciences

content.text: The role of brand personality for the communicative management of a brand: An analysis from a system-theoretical perspective. The personality-oriented brand understanding is a much discussed topic of strategic brand management. It is now an integral part of large parts of current brand research and experiences special upturn especially in consulting practice for some years. Nicolas Schindler examines for the first time the importance of the concept of brand personality for the communicative management of a brand from the perspective of Luhmann's system theory and thereby places the brand personality in a communicative and societal context. Furthermore, he underscores the theoretical framework and the findings of a systemic analysis with examples from the practice, in order to derive on this basis recommendations for the strategic brand management in the field of marketing. The work was awarded the Horizon Award 2008 with the funding prize of the Horizon Foundation. Nicolas Schindler studied journalism and communication sciences, business economics and psychology at the Freie Universität Berlin and the University of Sorbonne, Paris.
content.title_en: The role of brand personality for the communicative management of a brand: An analysis from a system-theoretical perspective

content.text: Right-wing populism as a "citizen movement": campaigns against Islam and mosque construction and municipal counter-strategies. Campaigns against Islam and mosque construction are considered to be 'success-related' issues in Europe in the extreme right-wing. Under the label 'Citizen movement pro NRW/Germany', a new group of right-wing outsiders tries to gain influence in this country with right-wing populist agitation against mosques and Muslims. In this book, this form of agitation of anti-Islamic right-wing populism is being comprehensively analyzed for the first time and placed in the context of social and communal political debates about the topics Islam and integration. Campaigns against Islam and mosque construction are considered to be 'success-oriented issues' in the extreme right-wing Europe in this book. Under the label 'Citizen movement pro NRW/Germany', in this country, a new group of right-wing outsiders tries to gain influence with right-wing populist agitation against mosques and Muslims.
content.title_en: Right-wing populism as a "citizen movement" : campaigns against Islam and mosque construction and municipal counter-strategies

content.text: New risk Terrorism: Disintegration, ways of dealing with terrorism, alternatives. Terrorism has been a risk since its inception. But since when has it been one of the new risks? Are the existing concepts for dealing with risks to the social management of terrorism sufficient? Where can alternatives be used? The present work shows that the existing concepts for dealing with risks do not fully meet terrorism, which is considered a new risk since the attacks of September 11. Therefore, alternatives are being developed that in turn aim to address the functioning and effects of terrorism and strengthen the protection of the social psyche.
content.title_en: New risk Terrorism : delimitation, possibilities of dealing with it, alternatives

content.text: Trading in balancing energy and spot markets: methods for decision support for grid and power plant operators. To support the complex trading decisions of grid and power plant operators, Derk Jan Schwer develops new methods and models from the field of energy-economic system analysis and decision theory. Their basic character allows them to be transferred to comparablely designed markets in other sectors of the economy. Dr. Derk Jan Schwer is a scientific employee at the Institute for Energy Economics and Rational Energy Application at the University of Stuttgart and heads the Department of Energy Application and Energy Management. After the deregulation of the electricity markets in Germany, the grid and power plant operators are facing new planning tasks under uncertain conditions. In addition to the change from cost minimisation to profit maximisation, the adequate handling of risks is particularly important. Accordingly, the trade planning is focused on operational business activities. Derk Jan Schwer develops new methods and models from the field of energy-economic system analysis and decision theory to support the complex trading decisions of grid and power plant operators.
content.title_en: Trading in balancing and spot markets : methods for decision support for grid and power plant operators

content.text: SAP for Java developers: Concepts, interfaces, technologies. Introduction to SAP -- Introduction to SAP -- Overview -- ABAP -- Development environment and process -- Integration of Java and SAP -- Integration of Java and SAP -- Overview -- RFC interfaces and Java Connector -- IDocs -- Netweaver -- Netweaver -- Overview -- Development environment and process -- Web Dynpro -- Backend access -- Persistence -- Exchange Infrastructure -- Netweaver — Resume. SAP has recently been pushing the spread of Netweaver technology and thus initiates an equalization of Java and ABAP as languages for SAP programming. This book provides an experienced Java programmer with the necessary help when starting the SAP world. Introducing the architecture and terminology of SAP R/3 is discussed. This is done at a sophisticated technical level in the language of a Java developer. Afterwards, two different approaches to connecting the conventional SAP R/3 to Java are explained and compared. Using representative interface examples, the implementation of the web interface diagrams are discussed in different ways.
content.title_en: SAP for Java developers : Concepts, interfaces, technologies

content.text: The thesis of double disadvantage is the fundamental assumption in the literature on the effects of the contextual effects of poor or disadvantaged residential areas on the inhabitants. This thesis is examined in a representative survey of German and Turkish residents of Cologne-Vingst/Höhenberg, supplemented by qualitative interviews. First, the internal differentiation of the area is examined and then the strategies of the daily management of the German and Turkish residents as well as their networks and social capital are examined. Further, the question of the extent to which different behaviour is perceived is also addressed. Numerous hypotheses are tested for the individual areas of behaviour. German respondents can prove double disadvantage. For the Turkish population it is only limited. Turkish residents of a disadvantaged area can apparently cope with crisis situations better.
content.title_en: Double disadvantaged? : Living in a German-Turkish district

content.text: Performance assessment of computer systems: Practical performance analysis of computers and their communication. Preliminary remarks on the load with performance -- Simple performance measurements -- The laws of Amdahl and Gustafson -- The laws of Little -- Benchmarks or the load with load -- Measurable performance laws -- Simple stochastic model concepts -- The Chapman-Kologoroff equations -- The desire to model -- Performance analysis on a model basis -- Concepts for analysing communication systems -- Model and reality -- The validity of laws. The performance of computer systems is the decisive factor for their use. To measure performance, the benchmark method is often used as a standard tool, although it is generally known that the corresponding results have only a very limited significance – this is of course the case for their strong orientation to practice. Model-forming techniques are often rightly perceived as "mathematical-heavy" and also suggest an accuracy beyond reality. It is obvious that both positions complement each other and allow for a much better measurement, analysis and evaluation.
content.title_en: Performance evaluation of computer systems : Practical performance analysis of computers and their communication

content.text: Digital ecosystems: Service orientation in dynamically networked companies. Introduction -- Basics -- Service orientation paradigm -- Security -- Mobile computing -- Ambiente Intelligence -- Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing -- Smart Spaces -- One.world -- Digital ecosystems -- Ecosystem Oriented Architecture -- Digital biology -- Evolutionary environments -- Self-healing -- Identity management -- Transactions -- Peering tactics -- Epilog -- Attachment: -- System theory -- Ultra Large Scale Systems -- Viable System Model -- Metrics -- Pi-Calkul -- XMI -- Glossary -- Directory of subjects. Services as basic building blocks of organizations, corporate worlds and technical environments generate completely new and partially unpredictable properties. At the same time, the tax and feasibility of such digital ecosystems is considered as well as the pervasive computing, ambient intelligence on the one hand and virtual organizations from many partners in the field of software are changing the future of the systems.
content.title_en: Digital Ecosystems : Service orientation for dynamically networked companies

content.text: Innovation systems: technology, institutions and the dynamics of competitiveness. Innovations are created in the context of interactive learning processes of systemically networked actors. The focus is on structurally and institutionally embedded innovation networks, which are involved in the generation and diffusion of innovations. They primarily cooperate with public and private research institutions, educational and training institutions as well as with financial service providers. Historically, innovation systems were first developed at the national level. However, globalization leads to the differentiation of local, regional and supranational arrangements. The collection volume is divided into three blocks. The first block contains German translations of basic texts of the innovation system approach. In the second block, individual theoretical aspects are analysed in depth. The third block contains studies on the differentiation of the German innovation system.
content.title_en: Innovation systems: technology, institutions and the dynamics of competitiveness

content.text: Young people in the off-side: The situation in French and German marginalised urban districts. To understand the developments and manifestations of the exclusion processes in France and Germany, a detailed analysis of the different framework conditions of the two countries is required. The topic implies not only an international but also an interdisciplinary view of social work: not only the youth topic, but also gender, migration, social space orientation and the role of the media are directly involved. Dr. Markus Ottersbach is Professor of Sociology at the Cologne University of Applied Social Sciences, Faculty of Applied Social Sciences. Thomas Zitzmann, graduate teacher, is head of a refugee advisory and teaching officer at the University of Cologne. In order to understand the developments and manifestations of the exclusion processes in France and Germany, a detailed analysis of the different framework conditions of the two countries is required. The topic implies not only an international but also an interdisciplinary view of social work: not only the youth topic, but also gender, migration, social space orientation and the role of the media are directly involved.
content.title_en: Young people away: The situation in French and German marginalised urban districts

content.text: Health reform 2007: After the reform, the German health policy is like an ever-lasting construction site. Health reform 2007 not only forms another stage in this process, but also has brought about changes in the constellation of actors. Because like no other field of social security, health policy is characterized by a diverse and complex structure of competing actors whose respective enforcement opportunities can be strongly promoted or reduced by government influences. The present volume aims to identify the strategies of the individual actors in order to illustrate and understand how, in the example of the health reform 2007, state-organised action, the power resources of the actors change. In these analyses, it is also clear that the lobbyists are after the reform before the reform. In this sense, it is also examined whether and how the reform responds to the challenges of the health system and what this means for the interests of the individual actors.
content.title_en: Health reform 2007 : After the reform is before the reform

content.text: Integration of immigrants in Italy: Legal foundations, political actors and the implementation of integration policies using the example of Emilia Romagna. Migration is one of the most important factors for social change worldwide. Its effects and consequences pose immense challenges for societies and politicians. Maren Borkert examines the legal and programmatic foundations of Italian integration policy and its implementation using the example of two key areas: the integration of children with a migrant background into the state primary school and language courses for adult immigrants.
content.title_en: Integration of immigrants in Italy: legal basis, political actors and implementation of integration policies, using Emilia Romagna as an example

content.text: Crime in everyday life: An action-theoretical analysis of opportunities. Why do actors gain benefits at the expense of others? Why do they take or retain valuables that do not belong to them or are not entitled to them when the opportunity spontaneously arises in the context of everyday action? The present study investigates this question and pursues the aim of explaining such activities as criminally designated activities in the light of favourable opportunities and understanding them from the social situation of actors.On the basis of the model of frame selection, the most important criminal-shociological theories are integrated into the frame of reference of a macro-micro-macro model of sociological explanations and related to the selection of criminal actions. Using opportunities for detection and unjustified areas, this integrative approach is subjected to empirical analysis.The study, in which a sample of the general population was polled post-examined, results in the conclusion that criminal action can be seen as rational action in the face of opportunities, which is less structured by instrumental incentives than by non-instrumental incentives in connection with cognitive strategies of justification.
content.title_en: Crime in everyday life : An action-theoretical analysis of opportunities

content.text: The subject of public debt has been one of the main themes of German domestic policy over the past 25 years, but also decisive in discussions of many other nation states and in the introduction of the EURO. If the focus was on the causes of public debt in many scientific analyses, the perspective has changed for some years. Meanwhile, it is increasingly being asked by what means a high level of public debt can be reduced. Some Western industrial states have shown great success in this regard. Thus, the Irish managed to generate budget surpluses for the Belgians or New Zealanders and thereby significantly reduce their government debt ratios. These developments, which are contrary to Germany, are the focus of this study on budget consolidation in international comparison.
content.title_en: Budgetary consolidation

The existence of modern societies would be practically impossible without reliable computing systems, e.g. in air traffic control, in nuclear power plants and in automotive construction. As complexity increases, it becomes increasingly difficult to ensure the reliability of such systems. Bernhard Fechner develops several innovative error tolerance mechanisms in this work, which are characterized by their simplicity and extraordinary efficiency in terms of space, time and energy consumption. These mechanisms are validated by implementations for FPGAs, standard cells and by software error injections.

content.text: Privacy by the delegation of rights. Personalised services, such as those offered by bonus programs of Customer Relationship Management (CRM), require the transfer of personal data between service providers. Current practices to comply with data protection agreements implement a trust model in which users have to issue a proxy for the transfer of their personal data and trust that they comply with the data protection agreements. Sven Wohlgemuth proposes with the delegation of rights an improvement of the trust model in favour of users. He presents an identity management system, which allows users to enforce and control the agreed rules for data collection and transmission. Thus, a controlled data transfer is realized and the user does not have to trust the provider of his data but the data consumers only. The presented system is examined according to the legal and functional requirements of CRM and the functioning and protection effect of the protocols. Privacy: A question of trust? -- Delegation of rights using the example CRM -- Multi-sidedness of current security systems -- THRESAM: Identity management system with the delegation of rights -- Evaluation of THRESAM - Potentials of THRESAM.

The methods presented here apply to both standard and adapted or newly developed software and take account of ITIL and other IT process standards. They have proven themselves in practice. Initially, the organizational requirements required for successful acceptance are described, then all preparatory work that must be carried out. Organisational interface areas that are affected by the identification of technical and technical requirements are also considered. The author presents the acceptance process in detail. content.text: Business process management. Business process management (BPM) is constantly enhanced, especially in the context of the more popular service-oriented architecture (SOA). A formal description of the business processes is also an important prerequisite for the depiction of business processes in the course of reorganisation and compliance measures. This book familiarizes with the basic principles of process modelling in a compact presentation and shows how they can be implemented in modern IT systems. In this process, modelling concepts bridge the way to technical presentation forms, standards (e.g. UML, BPMN, WS-BPEL, XPDL) and their implementation. In addition to the basics, practical examples show how companies can use the means of process-controlled process management and model-driven software development in their projects, and which tools are available for this purpose. A book for architects, developers and project managers. Importance of business process management -- Procedures in business process management -- Formal documentation of business processes -- IT-technical implementation of business processes -- Technology overview -- Summary and outlook.
content.title_en: Business process management

content.text: Maritime container logistics: Performance comparison of container ships in intermodal transport chains. The book focuses on today's and future container shipping, including ports and their hinterland connections. The reason for the book is the seemingly unlimited growth of container ships. The news about new size records of container ships is almost overturned. Massive infrastructure investments are made in the next few years for large container ships in the port regions without the hitherto methodical and plausible approaches to the efficient use of these relatively few super-sized ships. There are virtually no critical, economically oriented discussions with the future design of container sea transport and the impact of ship size increase on the entire transport chain. The book simply ignores the opportunities, risks and new requirements that arise from the growth of the container ships in the 70s and 80s. The book uses a transparent, pictorially oriented representation and quantitative evaluation of the processes in container sea transport to illustrate the parallels with the death of super tankers in the 70s and 80s. New innovative and practical design options for the shipping ship's shipping model as a benchmark for the container ship's container logistics. The summary of the container ship's model of container logistics are presented in terms of the container logistics.
content.title_en: Maritime Container Logistics : Performance comparison of container ships in intermodal transport chains

content.text: Optimization of auxiliary aggregates : Measures to reduce CO2 emissions from motor vehicles. and target definition -- CO2 emissions -- state of the art -- optimization of auxiliary aggregates -- meaningful combination of optimization measures -- conclusion and outlook. In order to exploit the entire potential of reducing CO2 emissions from motor vehicles, the influence of the auxiliary aggregates on fuel consumption must be taken into account in addition to the optimization of the basic engine. Marco Lunanova describes in his book the current technical state of the most common auxiliary aggregates and characterizes them in terms of their influence on fuel consumption. The optimization potential of the individual auxiliary aggregates and their interconnection is presented. Various combinations of measures taking into account the resulting costs show that a significant saving in fuel consumption can be realized by optimising the auxiliary aggregates.
content.title_en: Optimisation of auxiliary aggregates: measures to reduce CO2 emissions from motor vehicles

Journalism on the Internet loses its monopoly as a gatekeeper, because everyone can publish there without much effort. But communication between communicators and recipients remains necessary. But who channels the information flood on the Internet? Who sorts out the information waste? Are professional journalists still? Or do Internet users themselves take over the task of selecting and examining information? Can these processes be technized? In the research project that the band presents, the triangle relationship between profession, participation and technology was first investigated.
content.title_en: Journalism on the Internet : Profession – Participation – Technisation

content.text: Climate Change and Society : Perspective Adaptation Communication. Dr. Harald Heinrichs is a junior professor for Sustainable Development and Participation at the Institute for Environmental Communication at the University of Lüneburg. Heiko Grunenberg is a research associate at the Institute for Environmental Communication at the University of Lüneburg. Global climate change also has regional and local consequences in Germany. In addition to strengthening climate protection to mitigate climate change and its consequences, the need for forward-looking societal adaptation to itself is growing. This requires communication and participation processes that adequately inform and involve the affected population. In the book, the approach of adaptation communication is first developed theoretically conceptually. In the case of climate change and floods, empirically current communication processes are analyzed in the areas of Bremen and Hamburg that are affected by the trend.
content.title_en: Climate change and society : Perspective Adaptation communication

content.text: Corporate Risk Climate Change: Managing Risks and Using Opportunities strategically. 0 -- Basics of Risk and Sustainability Management -- Overview of Risk Management -- Overview of Risk Management -- Overview of Sustainability Management -- Compatibility of Risk and Sustainability Management -- Designing a Climate Risk Management Approach (CCRM) -- Overview of Current Research on Climate Risk Management (CCRM) -- Ideal-typical design of a climate risk management approach -- The steps of climate risk management process -- Summary, conclusion and outlook. The economic and financial consequences of climate change are becoming increasingly obvious: already today, but especially in the near future, companies will be affected by direct risks and costs, e.g. extreme weather events. This will have implications for other areas: companies, for example, must expect consumer purchasing power losses and demand shifts, with policy regulation of CO2 emissions and with legitimating and reputation losses. Companies will be affected regardless of their industry affiliation and size. Many companies will be confronted with risks, advanced companies can even benefit from climate change management – This involves strategically identifying new climate risk risks.
content.title_en: Corporate Risk Climate Change : Managing Risks and Using Opportunities strategically

content.text: Key works of Cultural Studies. This volume introduces in a double sense the "key works" of Cultural Studies with a focus on their media analysis approach: its first part presents fundamental theoretical reference fields based on authors who are central to the development of Cultural Studies. In the second part, key areas of Cultural Studies are presented using the works of central representatives. Thus, the book "Key Works of Cultural Studies" opens a comprehensive introduction to this current and critical access to media, communication and cultural research.
content.title_en: Key works of Cultural Studies

content.text: Tables in Germany: Aspects of a social movement between food redistribution and poverty intervention. The volume provides sound background information on a constantly expanding mass phenomenon in Germany: food tablets. Most volunteers now provide food for almost a million people from the overproduction of the food industry. The contributions gathered in this volume lay the foundation for the new research field "Interdisciplinary Table Research". Tables are analyzed and classified from sociological, social, political, nutritional, historical and board-internal perspectives.
content.title_en: Tables in Germany: Aspects of a Social Movement between Food Distribution and Poverty Intervention

content.text: Complex Regions - Regional Complexes : Multi-perspective approaches to describing regional and urban dynamics. Location competition and regionalization, participation and social capital, knowledge networks and creative industries, socio-political practice chooses one-dimensional descriptions of interdependent and multi-variate developments of locations and regions. To analyse these profound transformations, a view that exceeds the boundaries of individual political departments and individual scientific disciplines is needed.Therefore, this richly-spective volume explores the multi-layered phenomena that are important in connection with developments of locations and regions. In the foreground are predominantly qualitative dynamics that have only a secondary impact. Based on contributions to theoretical backgrounds, general developments, as well as specific case studies, the volume shows the theoretical complexity of current fields of action and outlines their challenges for application. Marissa Hey is a communication and cultural scientist and currently deals with intercultural communication in the healthcare sector. Research focuses: Media and cultural theory, cultural sociology, intercultural research. Korneliaert is a research associate at the Institute for Communication and Sociology of the University of Mainz.
content.title_en: Complex regions - regional complexes : multi-perspective approaches to describe regional and urban dynamics

content.text: The management of conscience in organizations: ways of dealing with corporate social responsibility. Companies are increasingly required to orient their decisions not only on economic but also on moral criteria. But how realistic are these demands on economic organizations, both in scientific and public discourse, to train a conscience? (How) are organized social systems able to differentiate between two distinctions (economic/moral) and these two distinctions themselves (costs/benefits, good/evil)? (How) are they able to observe themselves when this distinction is made or when they are applied in decision-making situations? (How) can organizations ultimately deal with the tensions that necessarily occur? The result presented is confident and at the same time shows consequences or limits of organizational morality. The book is addressed to lecturers and students of social and economic sciences, especially in the fields of organizational theory and economic ethics. Persons who deal with morals and management responsibility receive valuable information.
content.title_en: Conscience management in organizations : ways to deal with corporate social responsibility

content.text: Methodical development of technical products: applying methods flexibly and in a situation-oriented manner. The development of technical products is far more than design and design, mechatronics, customer requirements, corporate design, number of variants - only a few keywords that indicate the complexity, for which work methods are indispensable for mastering. This book focuses on the description and networking of working methods in product development. The methods are described in their structure and mechanisms of action, not as "recipes", but as a meaningful chain of questions and alternative ways of answering these questions. Thus methods of less complexity are brought to the fore, thereby supporting the necessary application flexibility. For the selection of methods and adaptation, the effects and side effects of the method application are addressed. More complex methods such as scenario technology, QFD, TRIZ and FMEA are described in a specific application situation and resulting adaptations. In the 3rd edition, besides updates, new research results are also integrated.
content.title_en: Methodological development of technical products : Methods flexible and appropriate to the situation

content.text: Simulation of tube amplifiers with SPICE : PC simulations of vacuum tubes in audio amplifiers. Tube amplifiers are developed and produced again. Those who own one or even more appreciate them because of their sound properties. The book combines the universal simulation program SPICE with audio tube amplifiers in theory and practice. This serves not only the developer but also the amateur and the interested person who can support his ideas of good circuit technology with the help of simulation. The circuit simulation quickly conveys knowledge about the tube amplifier without complex and expensive laboratory setups. The book presents new concepts that can be analyzed with SPICE and realized in a short time. NF tube amplifiers in times of digital audio technology -- Simulation of electronic circuits with SPICE -- SPICE implementations for PC -- SPICE analyses using simple passive networks -- Amplifier tubes, amplifiers and SPICE models -- Spice simulations of tube circuits in examples.
content.title_en: Simulation of tube amplifiers with SPICE : PC simulations of vacuum tubes in audio amplifiers

content.text: Hierarchical production planning in the event of uncertainty. Production-based research has been concerned for some time with the questions of hierarchical production planning, the treatment of uncertainties in planning and the approach of robust planning methods. Accordingly, a large amount of research on the individual subject areas is found. Marina Gebhard proposes to systematically combine these sub-areas. The author shows how the approaches of robust planning can be integrated into a hierarchical planning system, which can achieve significantly better and above all more stable planning results if uncertainties exist. Against the background of the increasing use of concepts and methods of advanced planning (AP) in operational practice, this approach is particularly important. The concepts show for the first time that the approach of robust optimization can be used in AP systems as well. The author deals with an open research question, which has not only scientific significance but has enormous practical relevance. Hierarchical production planning -- uncertainty in planning -- Robust optimization -- Development of a model for robust hierarchical production planning -- Case study -- Summary and Outlook.
content.title_en: Hierarchical production planning in the event of uncertainty

content.text: Lasers in production : beam sources, systems, manufacturing processes. Introduction: laser beam tool -- The tool -- Basics of interaction laser beam/workpiece -- Methods. This textbook introduces, on the one hand, laser technology and laser radiation generation, but clearly focuses on the application of laser radiation in manufacturing technology. Starting from the properties of laser light and the various beam sources, laser types and systems, individual manufacturing processes such as cutting, drilling, welding, soldering, hardening or also alloying are considered from the perspective of how laser radiation can be used as a technological manufacturing tool. For the second edition, the book was re-designed and written based on research and development. Thus, all lasers relevant to manufacturing technology are now addressed. The content focuses on the treatment of manufacturing processes, for which a detailed chapter on the physical basis of interaction laser beam/workpiece is to create the basis of process understanding.
content.title_en: Lasers in production : beam sources, systems, manufacturing processes

content.text: The book presents a new form of data collection: the telephone survey on the mobile network. This method is becoming more and more relevant due to the increasing distribution of mobile phones and the simultaneous absence of fixed network connections. This is the first book that represents the method and its implementation. It was developed as a result of a project funded by the German Research Foundation, which focuses on the integration of mobile telephone connections into telephone samples and the survey in both networks. The project is a cooperation between the Technical University of Dresden and GESIS - Leibniz Institute for Social Sciences. In addition to the development of a sample design, the survey (each of 1,000 interviews on fixed network and mobile) examined possible fashion effects in greater detail and the general willingness to conduct surveys on mobile communications in general.
content.title_en: Telephone surveys on the mobile network : concept, design and implementation of a data collection strategy

content.text: Swarm Branding : Brand management in the age of Web 2.0. Dr. Stephan Sonnenburg is Professor of Marketing and Communication at Karlshochschule International University in Karlsruhe. The phenomenon "Web 2.0" is becoming increasingly a decisive factor for brand management. Web 2.0 is significantly changing the understanding, design and communication of brands. Especially through the new technical possibilities consumers are really meeting the companies at eye level. They are increasingly demanding equal brand dialogue. The authors are concerned with the question of how consumers can be involved in brand management in a meaningful way. Based on theoretical considerations, practical models are presented that can be helpful for brand design and communication. Using case studies, it is shown how brands develop positively under the conditions of Web 2.0. The book addresses lecturers and students of social sciences and business administration with a focus on marketing and advertising. Employees in marketing and advertising agencies receive valuable suggestions for brand management.
content.title_en: Swarm Branding : Brand management in the age of Web 2.0

content.text: Patenting of business processes : Monitoring - Strategies - Protection. Business processes serve the implementation of the corporate goals. They range from eBanking and Internet auctions to ordering systems for books and digital media to booking travel. Business processes are an important field for innovation and targeted profiling towards competitors, which also involves patenting. The book describes the basics and perspectives of patenting business processes. It shows design options for companies and provides guidance for monitoring business processes and relevant patent research. The search results can be clearly presented with patent maps, which can be used to derive recommendations for strategic management of companies. This approach is applied to two exemplary business processes. The summary formulates perspectives for management to develop and secure their business processes.
content.title_en: Patenting of business processes : Monitoring - Strategies - Protection

content.text: Linear algebra and analysis elements. Linear algebra -- Linear equation systems and vector spaces -- Linear images -- The scalar product -- Determinants -- Affine figures -- Curves and second order flats -- Projective geometry -- Linear optimization -- Analysis -- Consequences of real numbers -- Differential and integral calculations -- Potency series -- Curves and surfaces. The book is aimed at students of mathematics in teaching school courses of all levels and polyvalent Bachelor courses. It provides the basics of linear algebra and analysis, i.e. those mathematical areas which are of central importance for applications and on the other hand for further development of mathematics. The relevance of the topics covered is demonstrated by numerous examples. Linear algebra and analysis are presented in two independent parts. However, linear algebra uses simple examples of the analysis to motivate the conceptual formations and inversely, some of the concepts being used in the linear algebra and the analysis are also used in a more detailed manner.

content.text: Climate science: Climate research in the 21st century — challenge for natural and social sciences. Climate research – introduction to a "mega science" Climate science has undergone a significant change in recent years. It has become a global "system science" of the climate system – or even of the earth system as a whole –: highly interdisciplinary, extremely problem-driven and increasingly embedded in international contexts. Natural science studies combine here with socio-scientific questions, basic research with political frameworks. The present introductory textbook addresses this development. It consists of three interconnected parts: I: Climate science as science II: Climate change and Global Change III: Interactions: Climate – people, society and politics The chapter "Basic knowledge and basic laws of climate science" provides a detailed overview of the highly topical topic "Global Change" and illustrates the societal relevance of climate research. For the necessary understanding of the natural scientific context – in particular on the physics and chemistry of the atmosphere – the chapter "Basic knowledge and basic laws of climate science" is also used to illustrate the topic of the "global change" of the social spectrum of the global climate science.
content.title_en: Climate: Climate research in the 21st century — challenge for natural and social sciences

content.text: Strategic IP management – more than just patents: Protect intellectual property and use it as a competitive advantage. Product piracy and price dumping from low-cost countries pose a serious threat to many European companies. Protecting an enterprise's intellectual property (Intellectual Property – IP) and its management are therefore of high strategic importance, increasingly also for medium-sized companies. Patents, trademarks and other property rights can play a decisive role in increasing and sustainably safeguarding the competitiveness of a company. However, intelligent management of intellectual property proves to be a major challenge. Competitive advantages in the form of monopoly positions can be achieved by linking all intellectual property rights with corporate communication and integrating both areas into the overall strategy. A profitable book, especially for non-lawyers such as managers in medium-sized and larger companies, marketing managers and corporate communications managers, shows in this book for the first time how to sustainably increase marketing strategies, increase the scope of protection rights, especially in the field of industrial property protection, especially in the field of trademark, competition, taste and patent law, and in this book, based on numerous examples, how to achieve all-decision-making strategies for the protection of rights and in the context of communication.
content.title_en: Strategic IP management – more than just patents: Protecting intellectual property and using it as a competitive advantage

content.text: Internet and migration: Theoretical approaches and empirical findings. The information and interaction of migrants is now increasingly taking place via the Internet. This is partly creating new ethnic, diasporic or transnational online communities. Overall, the Internet and its possibilities for use thus assume an important role for the social participation of migrants in the host country and also for the development of their countries of origin. Dr. Uwe Hunger is a scientific assistant at the Institute for Political Science of the University of Münster and spokesman of the Working Group 'Migration Policy' in the German Association for Political Science (DVPW). Dr. Kathrin Kissau is a senior researcher at the Swiss Foundation for Social Sciences Research (FORS) at the University of Lausanne and works in the field of participation and online research. The information and interaction of migrants is now increasingly taking place via the Internet. This partly creates new ethnic, diasporic or transnational online communities. Overall, the Internet and its possibilities of use thus plays an important role in the social participation of migrants in the host country and also for the development of their countries of origin.
content.title_en: Internet and Migration : Theoretical approaches and empirical findings

content.text: The power of parliaments: functions and performance profiles of national popular representatives in the old democracies of the world. The study first works out how the functional spectrum of modern parliaments varies worldwide. The subject of this comparative analysis is the popular representatives of 23 "old" democracies, i.e. consolidated and at the same time rich in tradition. Secondly, it analyses how the respective parliamentary function profile (government formation, legislation, control, representation and communication) is influenced by certain context variables (government system, party landscape, political vetoes etc.). Third, it examines which specific parliamentary current accounts (guarantee of government stability, effective legislation, budgetary discipline, citizen confidence) result from the respective power equipment. This then allows conclusions to be drawn as to whether certain functional profiles and context conditions are attainable to optimal parliamentary achievements.
content.title_en: The power of parliaments: functions and performance profiles of national popular representatives in the old democracies of the world

content.text: Flexibility through self-control in logistic systems : Development of a real-option-based assessment model. To be able to assess new technologies in the logistics industry, e.g. the use of RFID, in terms of economic functionality and feasibility, an economic evaluation is needed. Christine Wycisk develops a valuation model for rational decision support for logistics management, which illustrates the use of self-control concepts in terms of their economic value-adding potential. The author answers the following questions: How can the degree of self-control be measured in a company? What additional flexibility effects can be identified by self-control? What influence does the concept of self-control have on the company's value? Introductory considerations -- Flexibility requirements of logistic systems and self-control as a solution approach -- Evaluation requirements and approaches for self-controlling logistic systems -- Economic assessment model for self-controlling logistic systems -- Final considerations.
content.title_en: Flexibility through self-management in logistical systems : Development of a real-time option-based assessment model

content.text: Electronic Knowledge Markets : Trade information and knowledge about digital networks. Basics -- Electronic Knowledge Markets -- Semantically-annotated digital knowledge goods -- Infrastructure components of electronic knowledge markets -- Summary and outlook. Knowledge is the central resource of companies that need employees to develop innovative products and services. Documented knowledge, such as patents, strategy models, best practices or benchmark descriptions, can be efficiently stored in digital form and exchanged via digital networks. Such knowledge values can be traded within and between companies via electronic markets. Wolfgang Maass develops the concept of digital knowledge, integrates it into a reference model for electronic knowledge markets and presents technical implementation possibilities.
content.title_en: Electronic knowledge markets : Information and knowledge trading via digital networks

content.text: Credit risk modelling: A multi-functional approach to integrating credit risk analysis into value-based overall banking management. Risk identification and quantification based on current state of theory and practice -- Risk concept -- Market risk quantification – Introduction of approaches and procedures in theory and practice -- Credit risk quantification – Introduction of approaches and procedures in theory and practice -- Multi-functional model for credit risk quantification (MMKRQ) -- The approach to developing a multi-functional model for credit risk quantification (MMKRQ) -- Pre-module of the Multi-functional model for credit risk quantification (MMKRQ) -- Main and Construction Module of the Multi-functional model for credit risk quantification (MMKRQ). Jan Zurek presents a new credit risk model based on established methods of market and credit risk modelling, which is characterized by four central characteristics: the universal applicability of the model, the credit borrower and credit institution's in-house execution of credit risk analysis, the flexible assessment of any risk assessment, the risk assessment of the different types of risk and the portfolio.
content.title_en: Credit risk modelling: a multifunctional approach to integration into value-based overall banking management

content.text: Transfer of a capital company from a tax perspective : A tax advantage comparison between the share deal and the asset deal. Introduction -- Methodical basis for determining the tax-advantaged implementation route -- Abstract Determination of the tax-advantaged implementation route taking into account the existing tax-based factors -- Derivation of the tax-advantage of the share deal or asset deal by means of exemplary quantification -- Final summary. The transfer of a capital company can generally be done by means of a share deal or asset deal. If a non-decision-neutral tax system exists, a conflict of interest arises in the case of the transferee and the acquirer in respect of the execution route. Simone Jüttner develops a general analysis tool, which can be used to determine the tax-advantaged implementation route for each individual case. An exemplary quantification of various transactions shows the application for the individual case and allows a derivation of general trend statements.
content.title_en: Transfer of a company from a tax perspective : A tax advantage comparison between the share deal and the asset deal

content.text: SOHO IN OTTAKRING : What's up? What's going on here?. "SOHO IN OTTAKRING sums up the first ten years of the art project of the same name and provides a richly illustrated insight into the diversity of the projects. The venue, the Brunnenviertel in the Vienna district of Ottakring, is an exemplary area of global social transformation through migration and economicization. The main theme of the publication is the possibilities and effects of art in the field of tension between the different interests in the public urban space. SOHO IN OTTAKRING has become an internationally respected art project in recent years. The festival is open, low-key and tests an art concept that is in permanent engagement with the dominant players in public space. This form of "public artistic work" opens up new fields for art, but always includes the possibility of failure.
content.title_en: SOHO IN OTTAKRING : What is up? What is going on here?

content.text: The mass psychology of the financial market crisis: US real estate bubble, subprime disaster, debt bubble and its effects. Almost daily new Job's messages come from the economy and financial markets. Shares are dramatically losing value, banks are collapsing, companies from all sectors are losing employees. The current financial market crisis has triggered the biggest and most serious recession since the Great Depression in the 1930s. However, market prices are not driven by fundamental data, but by the investor sentiment that drives the players. Explanations for this irrational investor behaviour are provided by economic psychology. This book brings together the insights about financial markets and mass psychology research results. After an introduction to the dynamics of euphoric booms and panic reactions on the markets and an assessment of the current situation, it provides an explanation of the connections of the phenomena to be observed on the international markets and opens up a current insight into hidden mass psychology developments.
content.title_en: The mass psychology of the financial crisis: US real estate bubble, subprime disaster, debt bubble and its impact

content.text: Thermodynamics of the combustion engine. General basics -- Combustion -- Idealized engine processes -- Analysis and simulation of the system Combustion chamber -- In and out system, charging -- Analysis of the working process of executed motors -- Application of thermodynamic simulation. Building on the compilation of relevant basics of thermodynamics and the presentation of idealized engine processes, current zero, quasi, single and multidimensional methods for the analysis and simulation of the real engine process are discussed, discussing questions of heat transfer, combustion, pollutant formation and charge change including charging. The close connection to practice is given, among other things, by the analysis of the working process of a series of characteristic modern combustion engines. The book is suitable as a textbook for students and prospective engineers as well as as as a reference work for experts in practice.
content.title_en: Thermodynamics of the combustion engine

content.text: The ongoing debate in everyday life and in the sciences shows that this task is still not easy to accomplish, because identity still needs to be built, preserved and defended. The volume includes the most important contributions of the 20th century debate on identity from Sigmund Freud to Homi K. Bhabha. The theorists of identity research present here provide the necessary analytical and programmatic tools for working on the self. These 'key works' are a book for all social and cultural scientists who want to theoretically and practically deal with identity questions and concepts from a pedagogical, sociological, psychological and philosophical perspective. Prof. Dr. Jörg Zirfas is working at the Chair of Education at the Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg. Dr. Benjamin Jörissen works at the Chair of General Education at the Otto-von-Guericke-Universität Magdeburg.
content.title_en: Key works of identity research

content.text: Media analysis and media criticism : Research fields of a constructive sociology of the media. A socially scientifically viable media critique presupposes a powerful media analysis. From the point of view of a constructive sociology of the media, the foundations and fields of application of such media analysis in the areas of media criticism, media socialization, inclusion and integration by the media as well as interactivity of new media are presented. A socially scientifically viable media critique presupposes a powerful media analysis. From the point of view of a constructive sociology of the media, the foundations and fields of application of such media analysis in the areas of media criticism, media socialization, inclusion and integration by the media as well as interactivity of new media are presented
content.title_en: Media Analysis and Media Critics : Research Areas of Constructivist Sociology of the Media

content.text: Media literacy and Web 2.0. Against the background of the current discussion on the developments of Web 2.0, the current definition of media literacy from different perspectives is under review. In view of new techniques and applications in connection with social software, the contributions of the volume discuss theoretical and conceptual provisions, specific competences, standards in media education, empirical recording of media competence and practice within different educational contexts.
