content.text: Powder metallurgy - the main concept of powder metallurgy is a wide variety of processes and products, of which the structural materials in the technology have the greatest value added and application width. To this end, very different processing and forming processes have been developed, which are based on the processing properties of the respective powders. A selection of these processes with greater technical significance is described. For powders that develop under pressure green strength, the matrice pressing has the greatest economic importance at room temperature or low elevated temperatures for the shaping of components up to about five kilograms mass by far. For this there are numerous variants for special geometrical requirements, e.g. back-cuttings, which are described more extensively. In the pressed state, the green strength of the strength of chalk is comparable. For technical application, a metallurgy consolidation by sintering is required, which for economic reasons runs into protective gas-filled continuous furnaces under atmospheric pressure. The sintering conditions and in the case of carbon-containing alloy steels the cooling conditions are determined by the structure and together with the density of the strength properties.
content.title_en: Powder metallurgy manufacturing technology

content.text: Spaces in transition: Empirie and politics. Spatial change has accelerated. In the interplay of persistence and path dependencies on the one hand, as well as technically, economically, ecologically and socially induced development dynamics on the other, spatial weights shift and lead to new disparities. The explicitly spatially oriented policies such as spatial development policy, urban planning and regional economic policy attempt to regulate these processes normatively at national level. The present volume is deliberately multi-disciplinary and brings together spatial development policy, urban planning, administrative economic and philosophical-historical perspectives on spatial change. The content growth motors outside the metropolises • Demographic change • Healthy communities • Urban change • New boundaries of communities The target groups spatial researchers and researchers; social geographers and geographers; in urban and spatial planning activities. The editors Prof. Dr. Martin Junkernheinrich and Dr.-Ing. Karl Ziegler teach and research at the TU Kaiserslautern.
content.title_en: Spaces in the Change : Empirical and Politics

Social Media Marketing Guide for hotel industry -- Specialist glossary and glossary -- Reader service: Extraction list of other guidelines on the market -- Appendix. Social networks such as Facebook or Twitter are not only constant companions in everyday life, but also increasingly an important part of the integrated marketing communication of tourism companies. Ongoing, new social platforms or tools for companies to use these platforms for their corporate purposes are being switched online. Often, it is difficult for the entrepreneur in the everyday business to evaluate these developments and make them usable, as he lacks time. The present practical guide supports the caterer and/or hotelier in optimising his online business marketing: self-tests facilitate his own location determination, management possibilities are being identified and the selection of the wealth of social networks is simplified. The content of practical definitions and explanations clarifying the relevance and error of marketing of online marketing tools is used by the business community in the context of business administration.

content.text: Rules in social systems. Structure of rule -- Are rules descriptions or prescriptions? -- Rules as forecasts.- Form of rule -- Rules and social systems -- Rules, conflicts and decisions. Janeta Kapitanova examines the role of rules in the organization of social systems when they are understood as observant-relative, communicative phenomena. It explores rules in terms of communication, form and system. The concepts of observers, form, border, contingency, self-value and self-organization act as basic thinking figures that open up an epistemological approach to the rules in social systems. The author also refers to the disciplines of philosophy, sociology and linguistics and their findings about the rules. The aim is to develop, in addition to the criticism of the ontological treatment of the rule topic, a well-founded treatment of the rules from a systemic perspective. The content · Structure of rule · Rules are descriptions or prescriptions? · Rules as forecasts · Rules and social systems · Rules, conflicts and decisions The target group is the doctoral and the student's sociology.

This book introduces the simulation of discrete processes. Typical application examples are manufacturing processes, street traffic situations, human flows and business processes. The author conveys the basic event-oriented simulation and its programming realization. Using many examples, the solution of special detail problems with basic character is shown. The new challenges arising from the optimization of business processes in this way are a focus of the simulation, a separate part is devoted to the theoretical foundations. The book's learning goal is to understand the ability to use discrete process-based tools to create a completely appropriate simulation software.

content.text: Food Safety Reports 2011 : Zoonoses monitoring. 1 Introduction -- 2 Legal bases and objectives -- 3 Materials and methods -- 4 Results of the BfR prevalence studies after pathogens -- 5 Results of the BfR on resistance tests after pathogens -- 6 Summary of results and conclusions. Zoonoses are diseases or infections that can be transmitted directly or indirectly between humans and animals by natural means. Food contaminated with zoonotic agents is an important source of infection for humans. Zoonoses monitoring collect, evaluate and publish representative data on the occurrence of zoonotic agents in food, feed and live animals. Furthermore, zoonoses monitoring is used to monitor antibiotic resistance in zoonotic agents and other micro-organisms.
content.title_en: Reports on Food Safety 2011 : Zoonoses Monitoring

content.text: The Green Genetics Debate : The Influence of Language on the Production of Knowledge. Using the example of the Green Genetics Debate, Birgit Freitag shows the power of language in the production of knowledge about a controversial issue. It describes the strategies pursued by the actors in order to enforce their position in the discourse, and thus illustrates that not only the knowledge that an actor passes on on a controversial issue, but also the way of mediation has a decisive influence on the knowledge generated about this issue.The content • Language science analysis of technical texts and media texts on green genetics • Strategies of the discourse actors in the struggle for knowledge • Expert lay communication • Linguistic discourse analysis The target groups • Lecturers and students of German studies, sociology, biology, linguistics, politics • Biologists, politicians, experts in industry and church The author Birgit Freitag has been working as a leader in the free economy since completing her doctorate at the Ruprecht Karls University Heidelberg.
content.title_en: The Green Genetics Debate : The Influence of Language on the Production of Knowledge

content.text: The European city under privatisation pressure: conflicts over the sale of municipal housing stocks in Freiburg. European city -- democratic crisis -- housing as a core area of public services -- housing policy -- privatization of municipal housing stocks -- citizen decision. The area of housing is a core element of public services of general interest in the European city. The privatisation of municipal housing stocks could therefore fundamentally challenge the model of the European city. Sebastian Klus shows, however, that in the debate about privatisation perspectives open up, which refer to the future viability of the European city. These refer to the possibility of the city to act under difficult conditions as an independent political actor and the potential of the civic self-government. This is demonstrated by the author's case study on the conflict over the (most recently failed) sale of the urban housing company in Freiburg and its effects. The content · European city · democratic crisis · housing as a core area of public services · housing policy · privatization of municipal housing stocks · citizen decision The target groups · social sociology and students of the city workers as social sciences and the field of social sciences in the field of social sciences and social sciences.

content.text: Internet Economics: Basics and case studies of the networked economy. Introduction -- Part I: Electronic platforms of the Internet Economy.- Part II: Principles of the Internet Economy -- Part III: Value-added in the Internet Economy -- Summary and Outlook. Innovative information and communication technologies, the Internet and mobile communications are now a fixed and intransigable part of our everyday life. The structural change to the knowledge society described decades ago is reality. The Web 2.0 changes the basic forms of economic performance creation and makes possible new types of interaction between companies and customers as well as the user. The book examines the principles of the Internet Economy and the impact of the Internet for basic forms of economic performance creation. These include buying and selling on electronic markets, exchanging, sharing and social interaction in social networks. The book develops a systematic and overarching approach to this. A variety of case studies and practice tasks offer a high degree of application relevance to the business community. The solution for case studies and practice tasks as well as about 300 Fig. are available as a download at http://www.springer.com. The content of the Internet Economy and Business Administration's interaction in Bonn.

The question is addressed to what extent the electric car can contribute to sustainable traffic development as part of a new mobility culture. In addition to the technical, cultural, political, social and aesthetic dimensions, it is also considered how the overall social framework conditions need to change in order to help the electric car succeed. content.text: International Logistics in and between different world regions. The knowledge about the logistical framework conditions in the individual world regions is a decisive prerequisite for international success with or through logistics. The collection volume aims to analyze and make tangible the global logistics and to develop the awareness for the special framework conditions in the individual world regions. The differences between logistics and transport markets are illustrated by, for example, topographical conditions, growth rates of the economy and legal regulations of the individual countries. In addition, the authors are looking at questions about the respective Modal Split, the largest ports, airports or handling centers. The 2nd edition was fundamentally updated and supplemented with "Logistics in Australia" by another interesting world region. The content · World-wide moving flows of goods and logistics services as well as general conditions of global logistics · Logistics in Western and Eastern Europe as well as in North and South America · Logistics in the Middle East and Asia The target groups · Lecturers and students of business administration with the focus on logistics, transport systems and supply chain management · Managers in the areas of logistics and supply chain management in industry, trade and service. The editorial team of the German Logistics Group is appointed as a member of the German Chair of the German Business Administration and Logistics.

Basic statistical concepts -- Data collection -- Data processing -- Data analysis and interpretation -- Frequency distributions -- Ratio and index numbers -- Time series analysis -- Regression analysis -- Correlation analysis. The focus is on the application and practical implementation of statistical methods. The author places particular emphasis on a clear, understandable and comprehensible description. To this end, all methods are presented in a clearly structured form, step by step and in detail. Exercise tasks and control questions for all chapters deepen the material. content.text: Hollywood in space: Were we really on the moon?. A millennium event - a technical triumph: people were on the moon! Or - and can that be possible at all? - are we under-perceived a deception? A politically motivated global staging whose pictures and films were created in a studio? (From the video trailer to the book) "Hollywood in space" is about the landings of Americans on the moon - and the doubts of many people who have been in existence for forty years whether these landings really took place. Eversberg deals with the most famous lies, conspiracy theories and threats and analyses them in four-colour detail shots and with many film sequences available from the book. He addresses both the oldest well-known but also the most recent doubts about the moon landing - and offers readers of all ages such an exciting crime from physics, politics and history. .
content.title_en: Hollywood in space: Were we really on the moon?

content.text: Basic course for software engineering with UML: The pragmatic way to successful software projects. Software projects fail for a wide variety of reasons. This book shows, based on the systematic analysis of opportunities and risks, how the paths to successful software projects look. Based on the basis that the interaction of all participants in a project is to be coordinated in processes, the path from the requirements to modeling to implementation is described with the help of UML (Unified Modeling Language). Situation-dependent alternatives are discussed and the entire process is accompanied by quality-enhancing measures. To round off the topic area important approaches for project planning and project implementation are described, which indicate the embedding of software development into the overall processes of a company. As an associative machine consists of associative plants and is not built around a computer from Neumann, special features arise for its programming. Numerous examples are introduced into the associated associative programming. The associative machine simulator VidAs is available for this purpose. All chapters are attached to the students' support and their solutions are attached to the book.

Natural-inspired optimization methods such as the Schwarm Optimization (PSO) particles are only partially distributed in parallel. Tjorben Bogon develops a significant improvement of PSO, which is based on an analysis of the autonomous adaptation and improvement possibilities of metaheuristics. The focus is on the autonomous dynamic control and integration of additional knowledge in the current optimization process. The author examines how to generate new knowledge from the optimization process and on the other hand how this knowledge can be disseminated and integrated into other optimizations. He analyses these tasks under the premise of a connection of an agent system and shows how the optimization can be performed more efficiently and how it can be carried out in parallel cooperatively. content.text: Organisational change through coalition formation: An incentive-contributory-theoretical explanation of the change processes induced by employees. Juliane Stahl adopts employee initiatives as a starting point for organizational change and provides a comprehensive organizational theoretical analysis of bottom-up change. The presented an incentive-contributory-theoretical concept is then transferred into an agent-based simulation model. With the results, it can show that it is important for successful change processes to be transformed and special constellations of the participants. content.text: Political union without European demos? : the lack of a European community as an obstacle to political integration; with the revision of the results of a youth survey on European identity at the European School Luxembourg. The establishment of European monetary union had counterproductive consequences: it has led to divergent economic developments in the euro countries and excessive indebtedness of the southern countries, which has triggered the biggest crisis since the Second World War. This book examines the deeper economic, social, political and cultural disparities between member societies, which are massively countering the emergence of a solidarity community of European citizens – a European demo. However, the historically successful cases of national state formation show that strong citizen movements for the establishment of national states have emerged on the basis of cultural and social affinities. Today, these are not found between the societies of North-West and South-East Europe. In comparing these strongly contrasting groups of countries, Greece, the "weakest link of the Euro-Kette" is particularly taken into account.

content.text: The efficiency of the association's administrative and municipal authorities The efficiency of the association's administrative and administrative reforms in Rhineland-Palatinate. content.text: Reports on food safety 2012 : Monitoring. Monitoring is a joint research programme conducted by the federal and state governments, which complements official monitoring of the federal states. While monitoring via mainly suspected and risk-oriented investigations controls compliance with legal regulations, monitoring is a system of repeated representative measurements and assessments of levels of certain undesirable substances in the products on the German market. This enables the identification of possible health risks for consumers early and is targeted by targeted measures. In addition to food, cosmetic products and commodities are also the subject of monitoring. Monitoring of food is carried out in two parts: On the one hand, numerous foods from a defined shopping cart are examined annually, and on the other hand, current material and food related issues are processed in the form of projects. . Summary/Summary -- Aim of monitoring and use of results -- History and organisation of monitoring plan 2012 -- Monitoring plan 2012 -- Investigation figures and origin of samples -- Results of the shopping cart monitoring -- Results of the project monitoring -- Overview of the products previously examined in monitoring -- Glossary.

content.text: The World Climate Treaty: Responsibility of the International Community in the fight against climate change. The anthropogenic climate change leads to profound ecological, economic and social changes worldwide. Janine Bentz-Hölzl develops the foundations for a global climate treaty that defines the rights and obligations of states in international climate policy and meets the demands of climate justice. Distributive and corrective justice claims of current and future generations are set against each other in order to develop a new approach to the solution. This provides for a fair distribution of the rights of use of the resource atmosphere and at the same time establishes a fair "burden sharing of the costs of climate change". For the realization of the world climate treaty, the creation of an international organisation for climate and environment as well as a global environmental court is justified.The content Ethical implications of climate change Political theory by Peter Singer and Thomas Pogge in comparison The world climate treaty Institutional climate policy The target groups Dozende and students of the political and social sciences, climatology and economic science are researching the economic, ecological and social consequences of climate change.
content.title_en: The World Climate Treaty: Responsibility of the International Community in the fight against climate change

content.text: Early information system for real estate portfolios: Integrative approach for marketable rental properties. Risk controlling in the real estate industry has gained in importance in recent years. A challenge is to identify market trends early and to estimate their impact adequately on a real estate portfolio. Rupert Späth uses a self-developed crawler to provide data on objects to be managed in relation to real estate properties. In addition, he expands the controlling base by transferring data from existing properties and by taking into account the forecasting of tenant behaviour by means of probabilistic simulation. Finally, the aggregation and interpretation with special attention to corporate liquidity is addressed. The content Analysis of data from real estate properties Simulation of tenant behaviour Integrated information processing Liquidity The target groups Dozierende und Studierende der Betriebswirtschaftslehre focuss on real estate risk managers, portfolio managers, project developers and consultants in the real estate sector The author Dr. Ruperth studied construction engineering and business information technology and received his doctorate at Prof. Dr. Arnold Tautschnig at the working area for construction, construction and construction management at the University of Innsbruck.
content.title_en: Early reconnaissance system for real estate portfolios : Integrative approach for marketable rental properties

content.text: The International Criminal Law in Cyberspace: Criminal Law Analysis of the Law in Germany, Russia and the USA. Never before in the history of civilization has the crossing of geopolitical borders been so easy and fast. The author concludes that the borderlessness of cyberspace and the limitation of the national criminal law application space is a dilemma for all who need solutions for criminal law jurisdiction in cyberspace. The comparative analysis of the legal situation in Germany, Russia and the USA with integrated case solution leads the author to the following conclusion: The national alone approaches are in the solution of the problem of criminal law "All-Response-in- Cyberspace" doomed to failure. An international solution is possible alone. It is possible that without the creation of internationally recognized jurisdictional regulations or corresponding international institutions, such as an International Cybercrime Court of Justice, an increasingly extensive extraterritorial application of national criminal law is the source of interstate tensions. The content of criminal law law in cyberspace is known in comparison to: Germany, Russia, USA case solutions and resolution scheme for criminal law conflicts in cyberspace The target groups Dozierde, practitioners and students of criminal law, especially criminal law, and criminal law.
content.title_en: International Criminal Law in Cyberspace : Criminal Law Analysis of the Legal Situation in Germany, Russia and the USA

content.text: Reforms of the welfare state in Germany: willingness to reform and acceptance of reforms of the citizens. Politicians and voters fear reforms of the welfare state in the same way today. For the citizens they can mean interventions in social possessions, for which politicians will be punished in the next elections. The present volume examines the attitudes of the German citizens to the reforms of health, pensions and family policy initiated by the Schröder government and the grand coalition under Chancellor Merkel. It describes the acceptance of these reforms in the public sphere, which reform options supported the population in these areas and on which factors these attitudes are based. In particular, it examines the role of values and ideologies, interests and political trust.
content.title_en: Reforms of the welfare state in Germany: willingness to reform and acceptance of reforms by citizens

content.text: Global environmental change: new drivers for resistance, crime and terrorism?. Global environmental change and environmental destruction are continuing to progress. At the same time, the dependence on dwindling resources is increasing, while knowledge and skills are growing in the environment. We are currently experiencing rapid development, particularly in the field of biotechnology. This knowledge can make an important contribution to sustainability – but it can also be used for criminal and other purposes. The authors of this collection investigate how environmental change and the political strategies and technologies developed in response to it can contribute to unrest, crime and terrorism. With case examples from Europe, North America, the Middle East and Africa, the chapters shed light on this change, its causes and consequences, as well as possible solutions.
content.title_en: Global environmental change: new drivers for resistance, crime and terrorism?

content.text: Management of industrial product piracy: basics and overview. The phenomenon of product piracy as an existential risk in general is today as undisputed as its factual influence on industrial competition in particular. Accordingly, the systematic management of this corporate risk must be the subject of strategic planning and management. While the lack of concrete protection measures and difficulties in their implementation could be introduced as a major cause of the lack of counter-effects, today a better understanding of the competitive problem of product piracy seems to be a key key to improving the planning situation. Oliver Kleine provides an introductory but holistic overview of the issues relevant to the management of industrial product piracy. The content - conceptual principles - economic and business relevance - legal framework - entrepreneurial scope of action The target groups - lecturers and students of business economics with the focus - strategic planning, production and logistics - executives working in these areas The author Dr. Oliver Kleine is deputy director of the Competence Center Industry and Service Play as well as head of the business administration administration department.

content.text: Integration of organizations: A contribution to theoretical foundation. Integration of organizations, i.e. the knowledge of their "right" integration into a new whole, is one of the central skills of organizations or their management. In the company practice integrations often do not lead to expected success. Michael Schuster argues that a major cause of the lack of success is a lack of understanding of the real problem of integration and the associated challenges. In order to understand the phenomenon of integration and to understand descriptively, he uses a rule-oriented access to organizations: Integration therefore means the integration of the various regulations of the affected organizations. In this view, the decisive feature of integration is the degree of coherence, i.e. the internal and external coherence of these regulations. On this basis, the author formulates implications for the practical design of integration processes.
content.title_en: Integration of organisations : A contribution to theoretical foundation

content.text: Dealing with heterogeneity in mathematics instruction: Adaptive teacher acting in modelling. 1 Introduction -- 2 Teacher interventions -- 3 Mathematical modelling -- 4 Aim and method of the study -- 5 Analysis of the modelling task "Tanks-- 6 Results of data analysis -- 7 Summary and outlook. The book deals with teacher interventions in mathematical modelling as a specific aspect of the handling of heterogeneity in school-specific teaching. The core of the work is the description of an empirical study in which process-related teacher interventions were examined in an explorative way in the monitoring of self-employment oriented mathematical modelling processes of pupils. Both qualitative case analyses and frequency analyses of observed teacher interventions indicate that educational intervention during self-reliance-oriented learning phases is a complex subject and that the teachers examined only partially have the differentiated repertoire of action, which appears necessary to support individual learning processes in heterogeneous learning groups adaptively.

content.text: Public Relations and Economic Journalism : Success and Risk Factors for a win-win. Press spokespersons and business journalists are dependent on each other. The two stakeholder groups interact between duet and duel. But how does the interaction between press speakers and business journalists really work? What expectations exist in certain situations? The core question is: What concrete success and risk factors are there in the cooperation of press speakers and business journalists in the course of time? Torsten Knödler illuminates with the help of an innovative research design (cross-double-Delphi) and an integrative theory model (including game theory, quadrant model, intereffication model) what business journalists expect of press speakers and vice versa. He analyses the phases of initiation, course and crisis and gives concrete recommendations for action.

content.text: The Hartz Acts on Labour Market Policy: a comprehensive evaluation concept. Main description: The changes in labour market legislation brought about by the Hartz reforms aim to speed up and sustain placement in work, to create new employment fields and to build more bridges in employment. The ultimate goal is to reduce unemployment. Each evaluation study has to be oriented towards this overarching objective. The authors of the present work present such a concept for the medium and longer term evaluation of the implementation of labour market policies. Guidelines are:The concept must be practical in view of the not optimal data situation and the short time available. Given the variety of objectives of labour market policy, it must focus on the employment situation of unemployed workers. It must provide a uniform analysis framework for guiding questions such as: What have the measures taken resulted in they were effective? What are the costs of the measures? What are the causes for the impact can be identified? It must therefore pursue an interdisciplinary approach that provides a balanced combination of theoretical analysis, econometric competence and know-how of the implementation research. The evaluation approach must be implemented in the light of the evaluation's objectives.

content.text: Nuclear energy exit 2011 : the 13th AtG-Novelle from a constitutional point of view. The nuclear exit 2011 is also a challenge for the legal system, especially for the constitution. In this volume the constitutional framework is analysed in three steps: Udo Di Fabio examines whether the nuclear exit 2011 and the way it is implemented is in line with the property guarantee of Article 14 GG. Wolfgang Durner discusses the requirements that the equality clause of Article 3(1) GG makes the legislator in the field of nuclear law. Gerhard Wagner's contribution is based on the premise that the restrictions on use for nuclear power plants should not have been imposed without compensation from the operators. On this basis, the fundamental requirements for a constitutionally compliant compensation system are developed. Thus, for the first time all constitutional key and follow-up questions of nuclear energy exit are negotiated in a factory closedly.

content.text: Digital Politics Mediation: Opportunities and Risks of Interactive Media. General forecasting techniques and forecasting errors -- Theoretical basics of time series -- Component models.- Linear models -- Volatility models. content.text: The Restrictability of the Patent Law Injunction Claim in Individual Cases. Purpose of the Patent Law Injunction Claim -- The eBay case law of the US Supreme Court -- Abuse of rights by means of patent law Injunction Claim.- Patent and antitrust law Compulsory license. The patent law injunction claim gives the proprietor a fundamentally unlimited exclusivity right. This causes difficulties if the injunction claim is used exclusively as a threatening agent to obtain the highest possible (license) release. In this case, the conflict between the patent as a transportable economic property and the other protection purposes of the legal granting of patent rights may arise. Marcus Sonnenberg examines problematic case constellations and explains under which conditions a restriction of the patent law injunction claim is added, also in terms of the purposes and functions of this right, according to international, European and national specifications.
content.title_en: The limitation of the patent injunction claim in individual cases

content.text: The predictive performance management in vehicle-board networks. Energy-board networks and voltage stability -- On-board grid test stand -- System design -- Environmental coupling and prediction -- Performance management -- Implementation. The strongly increased electrical requirements in vehicle-board networks can endanger voltage stability in critical situations. However, without new components there is still potential for predictive, active stabilization. In the system developed by Tom P. Kohler, critical situations are detected early on using the information available in vehicles. Power management then calculates the effects on the on-board network and carries out appropriate conditioning measures. The consistent application of cybernetic methods enables the author to master complex on-board networks with a slim management system. Local, autonomous functions and a hierarchical system structure ensure without costly calculations that the most effective measures are always carried out. At the same time, short response times are possible without time-critical communication. The system was implemented by the author on a real-time computer and tested at a board network test stand. The content Predictive, cybernetic performance management in vehicle-board networks.
content.title_en: Predictive performance management in vehicle in-vehicle networks

content.text: Theoretical approach, empirical investigation and implications. Technology transfer processes for integrating external technologies are of high importance for the innovative power of companies and economic regions. They require a targeted design in order to be able to transfer knowledge and technologies effectively. Stefanie Lohmann considers the quality of interactions in technology transfer relationships as a central variable for explaining the success of such relationships. She develops a theoretical reference framework for this, e.g. on the basis of relationship marketing and social exchange theory, which creates correlations between interaction quality, its essential determinants and effects. The author examines the hypotheses she has created by means of an empirical investigation of companies and universities as a supplier in a technology transfer. From this she derives implications, which can support the actors and thus positively influence them. The content of technology transfer relationships as part of innovation and business relationship management Interaction and interaction quality Structure equation modelling Management of technology transfer processes The target groups Dozierende and students of the economic sciences with the emphasis on marketing and management specialist and executives in the field of F&E, technology transfer and marketing respectively.
content.title_en: Interaction quality in technology transfer : Theoretical approach, empirical investigation and implications

content.text: Change Leadership : System Theory and Emotion Management as pillars of leadership work. Sabine Lehner focuses on the integrative orientation of a modern leadership approach, including the often excluded personal management components. Based on system theory, she develops an extended approach for executives, which focuses on the complex interplay of factual and emotional effects and consequences with diverse feedback loops. The author shows which solutions are open to leadership in the face of resistance to organizational change or fears of the affected parties. content.text: Text Mining in the Social Sciences: Basics and Applications between qualitative and quantitative discourse analysis. The analysis of language enables conclusions to be drawn on society and politics. In the age of digital mass media, language is available as a machine-readable text in a quantity that cannot be adequately mastered without tools. The machine analysis of text data can provide valuable new insights in the social sciences, which until now have generally been qualitatively and less quantitatively, i.e. linguistically, analyze text. Against this background, the volume introduces the use of text mining in the social sciences. Using exemplary analyses of a corpus of 3.5 million newspaper articles, it shows for concrete research questions how text mining can be applied. The content · Basics: Text and Social Reality • Blended Reading • Text Mining Applications for the Analysis of qualitative data • Text mining as a method · Applications: Neoliberalism and the Change of Justice Discourses • Scientificization of Politics • International Organizations in the German Public • Rescue Folters in Democracy · Perspectives: Towards of a Best Practice? The Target Groups Political Scientists · Social Science Professors of the University of Hamburg Linguism
content.title_en: Text Mining in the Social Sciences : Basics and Applications between qualitative and quantitative discourse analysis

content.text: (De) Standardization of educational courses and structures: new perspectives on educational inequality. Scientific and educational discourses have been characterized by contrasts for some time now, which are moving in the field of tension between the increasing standardization and destandardization. These dynamics, which are characteristic in particular of education systems and institutions, are embedded in an increasing pluralization of individual educational biographies. The present collection asks about the effects of these processes on the reproduction and transformation of social educational inequality. The tension field of standardization and destandardization is taken into account from macro-, meso- and microanalytic perspectives as well as in various fields of education: The cross-sectional dynamics at the level of educational structures and educational courses are of interest. The content - the concept of social inequality - current developments of educational courses and structures - (de-) standardization tendencies in the fields: early childhood education, school, university The target groups are academics in the fields of sociology, education, culture and politics.
content.title_en: (De) Standardisation of educational patterns and structures : new perspectives on educational inequality

Understanding this matter is an essential basis for successful working with DNA and RNA in order to ensure a qualitatively good result. content.text: Key works of media impact research. There are central works in every scientific field that one must know - mostly because they have provided particularly important insights or given decisive impulses to research. This volume presents 25 such central works from the field of media impact research, which were identified on the basis of a citation analysis study. Among the key works are both theoretically oriented works as well as empirical studies and both older and much more recent works. Thus, the volume not only provides an insight into the beginnings of media impact research, but also makes their development comprehensible over time. By presenting the complex contents of the key works in a comprehensible manner, it is particularly suitable as an introduction to this research area central to communication science.The content of important works on (meta)theories, hypotheses and models of media effects as well as influential empirical studies The target groups Dozierende und Studierende der Medien- und Kommunikationswissenschaft The editor Dr. Matthias Potthoff is a research associate at the Institute for Media and Communication Science of the University of Mannheim
content.title_en: Key works of media impact research

content.text: Statistics for economic scientists: A real data-based introduction with SPSS. This textbook introduces comprehensive and practical concepts into statistical methodology. In its conceptual and content-based annex, the textbook is ideally suited as a lecture-accompanying and self-study-supporting compendium for students in economic and social science courses. All SPSS data files used in this textbook are available free of charge under the Internet address specified in the annex. content.text: The Ssymmetries and Groups in Particle Physics. This book provides a didactic introduction to group theory considerations and methods that allow a deep understanding of the interactions between elementary particles. It is primarily aimed at students of the Master's degree program in physics, but is also suitable for students of mathematics who have an interest in the concrete application of group theory. The first three chapters deal with the mathematical aspects of group theory, which are underlying the formulation of symmetry principles and their phenomenological application. In the following chapters, concrete physical applications, such as the extremely successful standard model of elementary particle physics, are addressed. The book is suitable for self-study as well as for additional reading on lectures in this field and offers the reader the opportunity to independently examine and deepen his understanding of matter using far more than 100 exercise tasks. The author Prof. Dr. Stefan Scherer (*1961) is academic director of the Institute of Nuclear Physics at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz. His research focus is on the theory of strong interaction, above all its chiral symmetry. In the teaching award he received the lecture for the teaching of the teaching discipline.
content.title_en: Symmetries and groups in particle physics

content.text: Square Numbers: An Introduction with Many Examples. The theory of square numbering bodies is the first step towards a general theory of algebraic numbering bodies. Furthermore, we go into the history of algebraic numbering theory in detail and discuss some important examples for the development of this discipline. Here, especially, diaphane equations play a major role. The book is rounded off by numerous exercise tasks and a short introduction to arithmetic with Pari and Sage. The author Franz Lemmermeyer, after his doctorate in Heidelberg and his habilitation in Bonn, has taught at universities in the USA and Turkey, and since 2007 teaches mathematics at the Gymnasium St. Gertrudis in Ellwangen. content.text: Alternative drives for automobiles. The fourth edition of this plant presents, based on the latest research and development results, as well as prototype and series versions, pioneering drive systems for automobiles – from electric drives with batteries or fuel cells to plug-in hybrid systems. The drive concepts are analysed according to the implemented processes and functions and are evaluated according to uniform criteria such as specific power, torque flow, specific fuel consumption and exhaust emissions. The alternative fuels are compared in terms of availability, production, technical complexity of on-board storage, costs, safety and infrastructure. The book contains summaries of the previously created electric cars, hybrids and plug-in vehicles. The future drives for automobiles will be characterized by diversity – from the solutions for compact urban vehicles, medium-sized cars, vehicles with range extension and SUV-s to inexpensive multi-purpose vehicles. Mobility – conditions, requirements, scenarios - thermal drives -- alternative fuels -- electric drives -- combinations of drive systems, energy carriers, and storage systems -- energy management in the automotive as a complex system.

content.text: Media Crisis and Media War: Do we still need journalism at all?. The media are in a permanent crisis – and that is not only the fault of the Internet. They suffer from the ‘American illness'; commercialization of content, reduction of investments and minimization of journalistic staff are the consequence. For years, it has been neglected to modernise their old business model. Moreover, professional inability and ethical failure of journalists have shaken the confidence in the reporting. Meanwhile, a US president and German ‘citizens' are even leading a war against the media. This book reconstructs how this situation has arisen and legitimises that a democratic society (good) journalism still needs to be. Autonomy of economic constraints and competence of the actors are the prerequisites for its functioning. The author Dr. Siegfried Weischenberg taught – after years of professional journalism – as a professor at universities in Germany and abroad. He published more than 20 books on media communication and conducted numerous empirical studies on journalism. content.text: Studies of the causes and effects of cow poxes. Studies of the causes and effects of cow poxes Wolfgang U. Eckart, Director of the Institute of History and Ethics of Medicine at Heidelberg University, comments on the first German translation of Edward Jenner's work "An Inquiry into the Causes and Effects of the Variolae Vaccinae" which was published here in 1799 under the title "Eduard Jenner's investigations into the causes and effects of cow poxes: a disease that has been noted in some western provinces of England, especially Gloucestershire". Edward Jenner is the inventor of modern smallpox vaccination. Vaccination with realpox viruses was already practiced earlier, but was very risky. Jenner realized that people who had infected with cow poxes (e.g. milking women) almost never contracted the actual smallpox. On this basis he developed a protective vaccination for people who eventually – even against oppositions of some time-companions – were able to obtain protection.
content.title_en: Investigations into the causes and effects of cowpox

content.text: The potential of numerical flow calculation for forecasting particle emissions in petrol engines with direct injection. Fabian Köpple presents a consistent approach to the 3D calculation of internal motor processes in petrol engines with direct injection. He was able to show that using the developed modeling concept the effects of different parameters affecting the mixture formation and combustion on soot emissions can be evaluated. Since the delayed evaporation of the fuel deposited on the wall is an essential source of soot emissions, the special consideration of the modeling of the spray wall interaction was an important aspect of this dissertation. In particular, the surface temperature of the piston has an important influence on the spray wall interaction, which is why the author carried out surface temperature measurements on the piston of a single cylinder aggregate. Overall, the modeling of the particle emissions could be significantly improved by means of numerical simulation. The content of large-scale research on spray modelling of experimental and numerical fundamental investigations on the spray wall interaction results of surface temperature measurements on the piston of a single cylinder aggregate.
content.title_en: Study of the potential of numerical flow calculation for forecasting particle emissions in petrol engines with direct injection

content.text: The burning cathedral: a history from the First World War. The cathedral of Reims is a coronation church, national monument and masterpiece of Gothicism, an important place of French history and identity. When this unique monument was bombarded and severely damaged by German troops during the First World War, this led to a radical break in Franco-German relations.The attack on Reims in September 1914 had far-reaching consequences and triggered an unprecedented propaganda war in which France denounced the destruction of the house of God as a deliberate act of barbarism. Thomas W. Gaehtgens impressively presents the cathedral's symbolic, architectural and historical power, thus raising awareness of the political significance of cultural monuments. Moreover, he is knowledgeable about issues of protection and restoration of monuments. The book ends with the difficult approach of France and Germany after the end of World War II. Through the engagement of Charles de Gaulle and Konrad Adenauers, the cathedral of Reims finally became a "peace church" to commemorate the reconciliation and European unification.
content.title_en: The burning cathedral: a history from the First World War

content.text: Historical landscapes of Italy: walks between Venice and Syracuse. Whether on the trail of the last inhabitants of Ostia, in search of the Sibylle on the magic mountain of the Apennines or on walks on water through the lagoon landscape of Veneto, Arnold Esch dives deep into the history of the country on his hikes across the diverse landscapes of Italy and lets the reader participate in it alive.On abandoned Roman roads, on ancient pilgrimage paths, through Etruscan gorges and on the tracks of cattle drive Arnold Esch roams his terrain ? from antiquity to the 20th century. The results of historical and archaeological research, the different perceptions of Italian landscape in painting and literature are included in the landscape experience and give the historian decisive clues in his search for traces: history that is in the landscape in front of his eyes. Arnold Esch masterfully understands how to re-enact the changes of the landscape from the past to the present, and takes us on a fascinating journey into often unknown areas. Thus, many, very different landscapes come together, which convey an atmosphere of his own time and an impression of his own exploration.
content.title_en: Historical landscapes of Italy : Hikes between Venice and Syracuse

content.text: Investigations of residual load-bearing behaviour of fractured glazing: Investigation of the residual load-bearing behaviour of fractured glazing. In this volume, the Through-Cracked-Bending (TCB) Test and the Through-Cracked-Tensile (TCT) Test are described as central test methods for assessing residual load behaviour of composite glass such as VSG and TVG. Both allow classification of the intermediate layer of VSG by comparison with the PVB film normally used in construction and are superior to the adhesion tensile and adhesion shear test and the currently used test methods such as the pumble test. For residual loadability, the delamination behaviour of the intermediate layer in the broken VSG, which is to be interpreted as the release process of the film from glass, is of particular importance. This is evaluated using PVB films with different adhesion levels in detail with the TCT test for different pathway rates of determination of their respective energy release rate.
content.title_en: Investigations on residual capacity of broken glazing : Investigation of the residual load-bearing behaviour of furnitured glazing

content.text: Customer Relationship Management : Profitability-oriented bonding of apartment tenants. Friederike Sperl examines loyal tenant behaviour in order to identify effective bonding measures for housing companies and derive a profit-oriented bonding approach. The aim is to sustainably increase the chances of institutional housing providers through an effective and efficient tenant loyalty strategy. This happens against the background of the change from a landlord to a tenant market. Therefore, customer orientation in the sense of Customer Relationship Management gains increasingly in importance also in the housing industry. In order to be able to exist on competitive markets, it is important to take into account the wishes and needs of the demander of housing services and to bind the tenants to institutional landlords in the long term.
content.title_en: Customer Relationship Management : Profitability-oriented bonding of apartment tenants

content.text: The IT-Information Technology in the Financial Services Sector: Ways to Process and Cost Optimization with ITIL & Lean. Lean Information Technology in the Financial Services Sector The importance of IT has been constantly changing since its inception. The desire for the latest technology has given way to the need to reduce costs. One way to do this is to increase efficiency. Management frameworks such as ITIL serve as a tool for this purpose. In the manufacturing industry, however, lean management is found to increase efficiency. This book now also offers a symbiosis useful for the financial sector from Lean and ITIL. In the second step, he sets a fundamental direction for the desired efficiency increase in the financial services sector based on the strategic orientation in the financial services sector and the resulting objectives and guidelines for the IT sector. Finally, he identifies possible weaknesses of the ITIL concept and makes a selection of the lean ideas for improvement. The strategic orientation of the IT-Information Management and the IT-Management-Management-Management-Management-Management-Berichtung.

content.text: The new German state: Report on the implementation of Federalism Reform I. The report contains the results of a research project, which from 2008 to 2012 observed, analysed and evaluated the implementation of Federalism Reform I in the federal and state states. It turned out that the most extensive reorganization of the federal authority distribution, which had been made 25 amendments to the Basic Law, is better than its reputation. The aims of the reform were achieved in essence. The number of laws required for approval in the Federal Council has greatly decreased. The state parliaments have been strengthened. Common tasks and responsibilities of the federal and state governments have been "unbundled". With the so-called deviation legislation, the countries have been created a unique instrument that allows them to modify federal laws and to take their own paths in the areas of nature conservation, water budget and spatial planning. In the fields of school education, culture and broadcasting, the countries can even send their own representatives, appointed by the Federal Council, to the meetings of the EU councils, of which many have been used.
content.title_en: The new German state : Report on the implementation of federalism reform I

content.text: Sports Interest and Mobile TV: An empirical analysis of the factors of usage behaviour. In practice, it is often observed that the introductions of media innovations are linked to sports events and sport-related advertising. However, the connection between the sports interest of consumers and the dissemination of new media has been insufficiently investigated scientifically. Reinhard Kunz develops a model for explaining the use of mobile TV and checks this empirically by means of structural equation analyses. As a central result of the study, it is evident that, in addition to mobility and media-specific innovation readiness, the sports interest is the largest factor of influence in the use of mobile TV. Moreover, the travel situations and quality and alternative related use barriers also prove to be relevant to the mobile TV users. content.text: Tourism and Nature: An empirical study in Hawaii and in the English Garden. Michael Höhne examines the tourist understanding of nature and examines the questions of how nature looks like and how nature is practically produced and processed in a communicative way. He undertakes an interdisciplinary historical and systematic reconstruction of natural semantics and applies them to tourism as a medium of nature's life. The content On the culture of nature Art of nature and the nature of art Travel and nature experience Natural recovery in practice Natural semantics as a contrasting means The target groups lecturers and students of social sciences, in particular with interest in the topic tourism, as well as in the natural sociology of practitioners from the field of tourism The author Michael Höhne studied sociology at the Ludwig-Maximilians-University of Munich and received his doctorate in February 2014 with the study.

content.text: Statistics and intuition: Everyday examples critically questioned. This non-fiction book shows with entertaining and entertaining examples how statistical thinking can succeed and lead to more competence in dealing with uncertainty. Deeply anchored thinking habits make us intuitively look for truths and patterns in everyday life – not for probabilities as statistics provide. The book clarifies by means of a variety of everyday examples from the departments of politics and world affairs, business and business, knowledge and technology, health and nutrition, as well as society and life about how thinking patterns of statisticians and non-statisticians differ, what misunderstandings arise from it and what statistics have to do with truth. Thus, it promotes active and mature handling of statistics and shows how to interpret and communicate statistical statements correctly. In this context, both formulas and the pre-conditions are largely no longer used for the data journal.

content.text: The crisis of European sciences and transcendental phenomenology: an introduction to phenomenological philosophy. content.text: The question of trust: the crisis of today's parliamentarism. No institution has been declared dead as often as the parliament in Germany. Populists despise it and dream of a plebiscitary democracy. Is parliamentary politics only there to legalize decisions of the federal government afterwards? The jurist Florian Meinel analyses with a sharp measure how the German government system became what it is, and what storms it must survive today. The success of the AfD puts the political certainties of the Federal Republic into question. The end of the old competition of the People's Party has captured all constitutional organs. Disruptive politics today seems to go without parliament: abolition of the compulsory military service, Euro rescue, refugee crisis, marriage for all. What is often attributed to Angela Merkel's government style has much deeper causes. The misunderst understanding of parliamentarism is the most vulnerable achievement of the old Federal Republic. How can it be developed today? What political opportunity would be in minority governments? Or do we have to build up the two-chamber system in order to make Germany regulated? Meinel's book is a defense of parliamentarism and at the same time a loss balance of the great coalition.
content.title_en: Question of confidence : the crisis of today's parliamentarism

content.text: Business Model Innovation in the Age of the Fourth Industrial Revolution: Strategic Management in Mechanical Engineering. The book examines the extent to which the potential of the fourth industrial revolution can be used to maximize machine and plant engineering in the context of the development of new, innovative business models. The chapter of the evolutionary business models assumes that the development of the state of the art in mechanical and plant engineering is being continuously pursued in an evolutionary manner. The second part of the book explores possibilities for disruptive business models. The content Theoretical principles Evolutionary business models: Data acquisition and processing, Cyber-physical systems, Networking and integration through cloud computing Disruptive business models: Value as a Service (VaaaS), Modules as a Service (MaaS), Planning as a Service, Software/Platform/Infrastructure as a Service Interpretation of the results The target groups of experts in the areas of development, logistics, production, and plant management.

content.text: Challenges for the automotive trade through electromobility. The insufficient demand for electric vehicles, lower value added and high investments play an important role in the development of the status quo of electric mobility in the automotive trade and for the assessment of future developments in individual sectors. This book analyses the business models, the structure and financial situation of brand dealers and multi-brand dealers, in which higher levels of entrepreneurial freedom are assumed. The results are based on scientific work on the trade, an analysis of the 100 largest German automobile dealers with the help of company documents, on discussions with 30 multi-brand dealers and a written survey of 114 brand dealers.The content Traditional business models in the automotive trade Electromobility: status quo and future developments Service innovations in the transition to electromobility The target groups Students, teachers and scientists in the economic sciences with the focus on automotive management and automotive trade Managers in companies and corporate consultants The authors Prof. Dr. Heike Proff and Gregor Szybisty, M. Sc., Chair for General Business Economics & International Automotive Management, University of Duisburg-Essen. Traditional business models in the automotive trade -- electromobility: future status quo and service developments in the transition.

content.text: Concepts of Untruth: Copernicus, Kant and the methodological atheism of the natural sciences. The old question of how people want to live together must be re-established according to Copernicus. Anthropology and cosmology refer to one another, and yet they do not fit into a common framework of explanation. This is evident, among other things, in the discussions about free will and the possibility of morality attached to it. In the conviction that truth-capable knowledge can only be obtained in the natural sciences, one exceeds their limits. This book, following Kant's criticism of the dogmatic mode of thinking, wants to contribute to overcoming these restrictive precepts foreword -- I. Copernican's turn -- facts-fixing -- circuits of reason -- church resistance -- abolition of the aristotelian blockade -- the end of the circular movement -- the path to truth -- the transcendantial -- ontological difference -- II. Kant: the skeptical method -- the transcendental idealism -- the primacy of practical rationalism -- the ultimate religion - the necessity - the truth - the inconsclusion - the indisciprelation - the inconception - the inconception - the inconception - the inconvention.

content.text: Plural Social Structure Analysis : An Actual Theoretical Reconstruction of the Basic Concepts of Social Structure Analysis. The book develops a theoretical link between the classical resource-oriented concepts of vertical social inequality on the one hand and the more culturally sociologically inspired concepts of lifestyles and social milieus on the other on an action-theoretical basis. Beyond the low-yielding confrontation of these concepts, a path to a plural social structure analysis is thus to be opened up.
content.title_en: Plural Social Structure Analysis : An Actual Theoretical Reconstruction of the Basic Concepts of Social Structure Analysis

content.text: Leadership, communication and team development in construction: Basics – Application – Practical tips. Introduction -- Management and leadership -- Team management -- Communication -- Communication methods -- Conflict and conflict management -- Change Management -- Fair Management. If a construction site fails to meet schedules, breaks up or exceeds the budget, this often has interpersonal causes. In addition to technical knowledge, the management style of construction managers, architects and farmers decides on the success or failure of a construction enterprise. The correct management behaviour improves the cooperation with clients and subcontractors, resolves and avoids conflicts and leads the team to the greatest possible success. In practice, this book provides the relevant basics of management, communication and team development and prepares students of the construction sector for their future management tasks. The content Introduction - Management and leadership - Teams lead to success - Communication - Communication Methods - Conflict Management - Fair Management The target group construction engineers and architects in study and practice Building expert object supervisors Executives in construction companies The authors Dr. Brigitte Polzin is a PhD social scientist, independent company manager and civil engineering engineer.

content.text: Key works of migration research: Pioneering studies and reference theories. The volume includes contributions that provide an orientative overview of classical key works of migration research. The contributions explain the idea-historical and theoretical location of key texts, their research perspective, central empirical findings as well as their interdisciplinary reception and current fields of reference. The volume is divided into two sections. The first focuses on pioneering studies of cultural and social-scientific migration research in the first half of the 20th century; the second section deals with reference theories and concepts of critical migration research. The volume is essentially designed as an entry-level lecture for students and as a textbook for lecturers who deal with the topic of migration from a scientific perspective. The content Pioneering studies of migration research • Reference theories of migration research The target groups Migration scientists • Students and lecturers Education, Social and Cultural Studies The editor Dr. Julia Reuter is Professor of Education and Cultural Sociology at the University of Cologne. Dr. Paul Mecheril is Professor at the Institute for Education at the University of Carlky Oldenburg.

content.text: The public space fulfils important functions for young people as a place of socialization and identity development. But public space is fought over, because expectations and interests of different user groups meet here. While young people lack the influence of the planning and design of their living spaces, actors in youth work and planning react to the contested public space with different, not always contradictory approaches to action. The book highlights the connection between the development and effects of the contested public space and shows ways of involving young people in the planning and design of public spaces. With reference to concrete approaches and projects, the perspectives of different actors (youth work, urban planning, politics) are taken. The content · About the importance of lived interdisciplinarity · Introduction basic principles: construction collaborations and effects of the contested public space · Basic contributions · Discipline perspectives The target groups · social workers from the field of youth work · Urban planners · Policymakers The editor Raimund Kemper is the managing director of the Social Infrastructure and Habitats Department for Switzerland, University of Applied Sciences and Sciences, University of Applied Sciences and Sciences.
content.title_en: Challenges for planning and youth work

content.text: Using methods in product development: Better products, faster development, higher profit margins. Marc Graner examines the use of methods in product development. Based on a comprehensive empirical study with 410 projects, he shows that and how the use of methods in product development can have a positive impact on product success. In addition, concrete recommendations on the use of certain methods are derived. Individual particularly effective methods are presented and it is shown which combination of different methods is promising. Thus, decisive steps can be taken in product development to systematically increase the success rate of new products. The content Impact of the use of methods in product development on product success Detailed examination of individual, particularly effective methods Recommendations for action on the use of methods in product development The target groups Lecturers and students with a focus on innovation management and product development Scientists as well as specialists and managers in product development and innovation management The author Dr. Marc Graner studied economics at the universities of Mannheim and Hong Kong. He is involved in an international leading company consulting.
content.title_en: Methodical use in product development : Better products, faster development, higher profit margins

content.text: Heat protection and heating technology: An overview. Heat protection bases -- Minimum requirements for heat protection in winter according to DIN 4108-2: 2001-3 -- Systems and components of heating technology -- Individual heating -- Central heating. In the heat protection in building buildings, measures are taken to create a comfortable room climate for people in heated buildings. The basic reason for this is the heat movement by components that it is necessary to calculate. Minimum requirements for heat protection in winter are regulated according to DIN. In the area of heating technology, individual heating devices for living rooms, larger rooms and halls are distinguished. For central heating there are different systems depending on the heat carrier. Heating bodies and heating surfaces occur in various versions. In addition to the necessary pipe network, valves and mostly circulating pumps are required. Heat generation is carried out in heating boilers, possibly supported by heat pumps and solar collectors. Remote heating systems have also been established in some places. The content of heat protection bases minimum requirements for heat protection in winter according to DIN 4108-2: 2001-3 Systems and components of heating technology Single heating central heating The target groups of students The authors Prof. Dr. m. Erölen was Dr.
content.title_en: Thermal protection and heating technology : An overview

content.text: Complexity Management: Psychological insights into a central management task. This essential analyses how complexity affects the reality of companies and what implications it entails for leadership and management. From a psychological point of view, complex requirements create a particular challenge for the organisation of actors and decision-makers. Individuals, teams and companies are oriented towards dealing with complex requirements, above all on the guiding principle of reducing complexity. The authors refer to typical errors resulting from these. Against this background, they formulate requirements for good complexity management, which requires a complexity-recognising corporate culture and an extension of the traditional management profile. The content complexity and uncertainty requirements and competences for successful complexity management Complexity requirements are addressed to "good" leadership elements of a new corporate culture The target groups lecturers and students of economic psychology and economics executives and managers, especially in innovative companies The authors Dr. Elke Döring-Seipel is a scientific employee at the Institute of Psychology at the University of Kassel. Prof. Ernst-Dieter Lantermann was the holder of the chair for social and personality psychology at the University of Kassel and is a employee of the practice for organisational development. Complexity Management - Elements of Management of Complexity - Management of Management.
content.title_en: Complexity management : Psychological findings on a central management task

content.text: This is how we create this - a civil society in the process of departure : 90 pioneering projects with refugees. German civil society has re-established itself in its struggle with flight. Between 2015 and 2016, around 15,000 projects were created, in which creative answers to the many challenges of immigration were found. They form an alternative to panic reactions, which see the only way to deal with flight in controls and deterrence. This volume presents 90 exemplary projects. They show the strength to deal with social problems in the current civil society – and what potential for a new relationship is not only in the handling of immigrants but also within civil society. This publication was supported by the Federal Government Commissioners for Migration, Refugees and Integration.
content.title_en: This is how we do it - a civil society on the rise: 90 pioneering projects with refugees

content.text: Challenges in the implementation of school inclusion: opportunities for reflexive editing using social network. Inclusion -- Municipal inclusion -- School inclusion -- Cooperative learning -- Education policy -- History of the special school. Sabine Oymanns illustrates that inclusive teaching can be implemented with familiar concepts and existing resources. The author's theme is to sketch out the concepts and methodological approaches to uncover existing resources in the colleges and school teams. It is clear that the implementation of inclusion is a multidimensional, societal challenge that can be achieved with existing resources and changed ways of thinking in networks – networks that are reflexive. The content Inclusion Municipal inclusion School inclusion Cooperative learning Education policy History of the special school The target groups Dozierdeen and students of teaching offices, education science, psychology, cultural studies, sociology Teachers and referendars as well as practitioners from the municipal administration and the school office The author Sabine Oymanns works as a scientific employee in the field of education and research in the field of education and education in the field of media research.
content.title_en: Challenges in the implementation of school inclusion: opportunities for reflexive processing using social network
