content.text: Introduction -- State of the art -- Development tools -- Impact of tyre parameters on vehicle air resistance -- Results of tyre optimization -- Transferability of results to model scale -- Conclusions -- Annex. Felix Wittmeier gives a detailed overview of the geometric parameters of the tyre that can influence the aerodynamics of a vehicle and how an aerodynamically optimized tyre can be designed. This is important because, in addition to the classic characteristics of the tyre, such as rolling resistance or wear, the aerodynamic tyre characteristics are becoming increasingly important. The wheels of a vehicle are responsible for about 25% of the total air resistance. This leads to the fact that small geometric changes in the tyre can influence the fuel consumption of a vehicle. The content State of the art, development tools Impact of tyre parameters on vehicle air resistance Results of tyre optimization Transferability of the results in the model scale The target groups Dozierende and students of the vehicle technology field Praktiker in the areas of aerodynamics and tyre development The author of the research project, Wittmeier, is responsible for the driving force system of the Stuttgart Thermodynamics and the vehicle simulation system of the vehicle.
content.title_en: A contribution to aerodynamic optimization of car tyres

content.text: Construction company management-process oriented Volume 2 : Operational performance creation and support processes. Strategic and operational enterprise processes are the key to necessary lifecycle-oriented changes in the construction industry. In Volume 2 – Operational management, the processes as well as the operational processes and integral process responsibility for an interactive supply, execution, risk, supplement and quality management are explained in practice-oriented for a successful project and enterprise management. In addition, it is shown how one develops a learning and innovative corporate culture. All important sub-processes for operational enterprise design and management are presented in detail. They find recommendations for the systematic execution of their daily operational tasks and the future-oriented structuring of the enterprise processes. Larger companies can use this knowledge to improve their positioning in the aggressive, dynamic and complex environment and strengthen their own competitive position. Smaller growth-oriented enterprises find the methodology that should be used for their company structure. Modern management concepts are mapped to the construction industry. The target groups All managers of the construction industry, construction managers, project managers, project managers, job managers and technicians in the construction industry.
content.title_en: Construction company management process oriented Volume 2 : Operational performance creation and support processes

content.text: Smart green world?: Digitization between monitoring, consumption and sustainability. Biographical note: Tilman Santarius heads the research group "Digitalization and Social-Ecological Transformation" at the TU Berlin and the Institute for Ecological Economic Research. He is co-author of several books, most recently of "The Rebound Effect". Steffen Lange is an economist at the Institute for Ecological Economic Research and a member of the Concept Work New Economy as well as of Common Future. He deals with the connection between digitalization, growth and ecology. "Everything will change!" This prophetic reputation from the IT industry has become a common assessment of the significance of digitalization. But what brings digitalization to ecology and justice? Does it lead us into a smart green world in which everyone benefits from technological progress and at the same time we treat the environment more gently? Or do we steer into a digital capitalism in which money and power concentrate on few and where the economy grows even further beyond the planetary boundaries? Steffen Lange and Tilman Santarius analyze how digitalization has so far worked towards energy and resource consumption, and how digitalisation has made the world work sustainable and how digitalization has really worked.
content.title_en: Smart green world?: Digitalisation between monitoring, consumption and sustainability

content.text: Violence as a social problem in schools : investigation results and prevention strategies. The book includes an analysis and presentation of forms, extend and causes of school violence. In addition, the possibilities of violence prevention and intervention in schools are presented. The first edition (out of print) was published in 1998 by Leske + Budrich, Opladen. The book can be downloaded free of charge as a pdf file (www.budrich-verlag.de). It includes an analysis and presentation of forms, extent and causes of school violence. In addition, the possibilities of violence prevention and intervention are presented in schools. The first edition (out of print) was published in 1998 by Leske + Budrich, Opladen.
content.title_en: Violence as a social problem in schools : Research results and prevention strategies

content.text: Border crossing borders: German-Czech border organizations are making a »translational performance«. Europe is growing together - a common political slogan says. This study shows that in many cases, organisations are promoting concrete international cooperation in internal European border regions. In this book, a research team of linguists, educators and sociologists investigates how educational, cultural, social and administrative institutions in the border region between Bavaria and Bohemia manage to achieve cross-border cooperation. The researchers illustrate how organisations use humanities expertise to »translate« between cultures, languages and legal areas.
content.title_en: Limits of crossing the border : On the »translation performance« of German-Czech border organizations

content.text: Automation 4.0 : Object-oriented development of modular machines for digital production: with 10 tables. When is a processing machine fit for Industry 4.0? The fourth industrial revolution poses a number of additional requirements for the design and automation of processing machines. Thus, products and their manufacturing processes are not only more demanding but also more individual. In this textbook, the challenges are analysed and illustrated by meaningful examples of solution scenarios. A focus of the book is the projection of these requirements on well-known design principles. This results in functions that are illustrated by various examples such as the production of photo books or inmould labelling. This creates a roadmap for the development of a load book for the construction of a conversion-capable processing machine. The modular, function- and object-oriented design of individual machines and systems is presented as a solution approach for efficiency improvements in the entire life cycle as well as for practical examples. An essential process for the design of changeable machines is modularization according to function units. These diverse requirements are illustrated step by step and elaborated. The book is aimed at development engineers and engineers of the fields of automation and engineering.
content.title_en: Automation 4.0 : Object-oriented development of modular machines for digital production : with 10 tables

content.text: The optimal movement system – solving problems of movement technology systematically and practice-oriented! A comprehensive overview of all the essential steps to solve movement tasks that are part of the everyday problems of a product developer. Designing and designing movement systems of machines, equipment and devices in which work organs, tools, workpieces or processing material have to perform certain movements is a decisive factor in the overall behaviour of the machine. For this reason, a systematic, modern and above all practical solution of these tasks is of great importance for the product developer. The textbook discusses all the essential topics for this purpose and provides the respective work steps in a clear and practical manner exemplary and practical way using general, effective methods and procedures. The book is aimed at students of technical courses as well as practitioners, technicians and engineers from the industry. Various examples and exercises for self-study support the learning process and the understanding of the topic. The solutions of the exercise tasks can be called up at www.hanser-fachbuch.de/motionstechnik. In the second edition, the analysis methods selected for the analysis and the QR are available for use of the animation procedures.
content.title_en: Movement technology : Design and design of mechanical transmissions

content.text: The beginning of the present: The discourse of catastrophes. Terrorist attacks and wars, tsunamis, earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, climate change, oil spills, financial crisis - reports about »catastrophes« are long since medial everyday life.However, the question remains which intentions and consequences the increasing use of the concept of catastrophe by politics and the economy entails.The contributions of the volume therefore ask: Does the term really serve only the description - or should an atmosphere of the state of emergency be created that enables the application of otherwise non-consensible procedures? Where does it lead to the classification of events into comprehensive social processes if their perception as a consequence of the risks received remain?
content.title_en: Departure into the Insurable : The Discourse of the Present

content.text: Spaces and identities in border regions: Politiken - Medien - Subjecte. Biographical note: Christian Wille (Dr.), social and cultural scientist, is scientific project coordinator at the University of Luxembourg. Rachel Reckinger (Dr.), sociologist, is a scientific project coordinator at the University of Luxembourg. Sonja Kmec (Prof. Dr.) teaches history and cultural studies at the University of Luxembourg. Markus Hesse (Prof. Dr.), geographer and space planner, is professor of urban research at the University of Luxembourg. Space and identity research works with distinctions and relations. These are particularly profitable as heuristic instruments in border regions when social and geopolitical markings fall apart. The results of the volume are discussed here. Based on empirical surveys in Germany, France, Belgium and Luxembourg, they investigate spatial and identity constructions in cross-border relationships, as they manifest themselves in everyday, institutional and media practices. The results are discussed with sensitive views for cross-border spaces and identities and are linked to governmental questions of subjectification and normative.
content.title_en: Spaces and identities in border regions : Politics - Media - Subjects

content.text: Risk. The concept of risk, which is theoretically based on society, assumes that "risk" belongs to the class of problems of modern society, which is "cross" to its functional systems: risks cannot then be concentrated on a special functional system (economic, scientific or political), they are structurally linked to the system of modern society. As outlined in the volume focusing on system-theoretical risk research, research problems are essentially related to the possibility of understanding between decision-makers and those concerned, to the "rationalizability" of risky decisions and to the importance of non-dissolvable knowledge. In the ecological context, these aspects culminate in the insoluble problem of "self-hazardment of society".
content.title_en: Risk

content.text: Symbolic forms: the foundations and elements of a sociology of catastrophe. When disasters increase, fundamental questions must be addressed by 'modern', technologically and scientifically organized societies. How was it possible that more complex societies could stabilize relatively in an overall undetermined environment without exact sciences and instrumental technology? What is wrong if this seems to be less and less successful today? Can fundamental patterns be identified that make societies more vulnerable to disasters? With the category of symbolic form, these questions can be addressed and some elements can be derived to their answer. The symbolic is the moment by which man has always been attuned to his environment. The increase in catastrophe phenomena points 'in a horrific way' to this category that is replaced in modern times.
content.title_en: Symbolic forms : basics and elements of a sociology of catastrophe

content.text: Innovation. How does a catchword transform into a scientific concept? The volume by Holger Braun-Thürmann looks at this question and develops a »sociology of innovation«. The systematically structured text provides information on how innovations can be understood as phenomena of social change. For this purpose, the author integrates the basic concepts of innovation studies into a sociology of innovation. The volume examines the complexity of the phenomenon of innovation, which is usually only considered from the point of view of the competitive advantage and the increase in productivity.
content.title_en: Innovation

content.text: The self-sense of consciousness: the person - the psyche - the signature. It is no secret that what we call person, consciousness, psyche, individual, etc., seems to evaporate in the advanced theories of sociology and philosophy. It is becoming increasingly clear that the consciousness to which tradition had attributed an own value is overformed by social processes. It cannot observe itself without discovering itself as an individual generality. Peter Fuchs' instructive essay deals with this problem. Explores the terrain of the question of consciousness - in connection with important concepts of proximity such as person, psyche, individual - at the level and with the means of system theory, i.e. one of the theories that seem to be massively threatening the self-value of consciousness. The concept of individual signature and its counter-drawing is used in all its preliminality to open up the space of discussion of the problem.
content.title_en: The Self-Sense of Consciousness : The Person - the Psyche - the Signature

content.text: Information Security Management: Guide for practitioners and accompanying book on CISM certification. This book is a practical guide on information security management and at the same time a guide to the examination preparation for the "Certified Information Security Manager (CISM)" according to ISACA. After an introduction, the first part of the book prepares for the CISM exam in four chapters. These were structured in analogy to the structure of the ISACA - "Security Governance", "Risk Management", "Security Program Development and Management" and "Incident Response". The second part deals with the IT basic protection standard of the BSI and the implementation of security using a baseline approach. The third and last part finally takes up the pre-discussed aspects using practical examples and supplements them with current topics, such as the IT security law. A detailed index and an extensive glossary round off the book and make it a reference work in the field of information security management. . content.text: IGLU 2016 : Reading skills of primary school children in Germany in an international comparison. In 2016, Germany participated for the fourth time in the school performance study Internationale Grundschule-Read-Aussuchung (IGLU). IGLU has been investigating the reading understanding of pupils at the end of the fourth year. In this volume, the results of IGLU 2016 are reported in Germany in an international comparison. The results are presented against the background of topics that have changed teaching and learning at primary schools in Germany and have shaped the educational discourse of the last years. The reading skills of primary school children are analysed on the basis of key characteristics such as gender, social origin, migration status and design characteristics of the teaching and with regard to the transition from primary to secondary school I. With in-depth analyses and the classification of the results into the current research level, the volume presents a differentiated and connectable inventory of the performance of primary schools and describes developments since 2001.
content.title_en: IGLU 2016 : Reading skills of primary school children in Germany in an international comparison

content.text: Wilderness, Forest, Human: Research contributions to the development of a national park region using the Black Forest as an example. »Wildnis, Forest, Human« – these keywords represent the broad spectrum of topics in this book. Topics that were worked on by research teams from science and practice within the Reallabor »Wildness Dialogue North Black Forest« (WiNo) from 2015 to 2020 were the impetus for this by the establishment of the National Park Black Forest on 1 January 2014. Numerous debates preceded the establishment: How will nature react to this when forest land is being managed? Will adjacent forest stocks fall victim to the bark beetle? What if previous opportunities for locals to acquire the forest are eliminated? Could new opportunities arise, e.g. in tourism? To address these key issues for the development of a national park region and explore the potential of cooperation between science and practice in the search for answers and solutions is the concern of this book.
content.title_en: Wilderness, Forest, Human: Research contributions to the development of a national park region using the Black Forest example

content.text: Indeterminate signatures of technology: A new interpretation of the technological world. Not that a fundamental uncertainty has not always been part of life or a more or less constant and universal condition of human existence, appears as a problem, but that with the experience of an increase in uncertainty a technology connected with society is affected and involved in the uncertainty process;- that social freedom and option gains go hand in hand with after-sustaining loss of orientation;- that the technoscientific generation of knowledge brings forth novel zones of non-knowledge;- that we cannot know what we should actually do and- that dealing with this fact represents the starting condition for a contemporary-incontinuous philosophy of technology.The contributions of this volume (including Dreyfus, Dupuy, Hörning, Hubig, Nordmann and Willke) are not only based on the different aspects of this development. They also make an attempt to estimate the socio-technical determination and the radical strategies of union (the new task is always determined by the determination of a new person).
content.title_en: Indeterminability signatures of technology : A new interpretation of the technological world

content.text: Sustainability has become a guiding concept of social change, with which different goals are combined – whether it is a green capitalism based on ecological modernization or a social-ecological transformation that could herald a post-capitalist era.This program book by Sighard Neckel and his Hamburg research team highlights the social dimensions of sustainability, but also the paradoxes associated with sustainable development in global capitalism. Fundamental sociological perspectives on sustainability are also the topic as well as prospects for concrete fields of critical-reflective social research on social conflicts about sustainability.
content.title_en: The Society of Sustainability: Outline of a Research Programme

content.text: Un/Certain Futures : Roles of Design in Social Transformation Processes. What role does design play in social transformation processes? Can futures and social realities be sustainably shaped - or are the effects of creative interventions more or less accidental reactions of self-interested social systems to well-meaning interventions? How would the "better" be defined, especially in the context of sustainability and the debate about a necessary "great transformation"?In the spanning of a complex network of contributions from theory and practice, design is conceived in this volume outside disciplinary narrowness and takes social, ecological, political and economic challenges seriously.
content.title_en: Un/Certain Futures : Roles of Design in Social Transformation Processes

content.text: Evaluation of a treatment preparation station for drug addicts and abusers. Criminals have high prevalence rates of drug use compared to the general population and vice versa, problematic drug use is often the cause of crime. Conservative estimates suggest that about one fifth of prisoners in Germany are former or current drug users. Up to now, there are only isolated interventions and treatment programs tailored to this target group. Corresponding evidence of effectiveness is almost complete. The focus of the research documented in the book is the testing of a therapy preparation station (TVS), which was first evaluated in the Hamburg prison. The intervention includes a search-specific "feature training" in the sense of "dialectic behavioral therapy" (DBT) after Linehan, a training for relapse prevention, conversation groups as well as a therapeutic running group and an acupuncture offer.
content.title_en: Evaluation of a treatment preparation station for drug addicts and abusers of prisoners

content.text: Through the flower: gender narratives in museum nature representations. Nature, gender, identity – three concepts that long stood for immutability and promised a security associated with it. However, the ideas we have of genders, nature and (collective) identities prove to be social, social and historical-related constructions and are subject to change as such. Home museums also stand in the field of social perception for stability, permanence and intergenerational continuity: they collect, preserve, remember and mediate. At the same time, however, they are not detached from social change and act as discursive places of knowledge production. They are thus always in the field of tension between preservation and renegotiation. Against this background, the study investigates new home museums as institutions of knowledge production natural representations and the associated knowledge production about gender and collective identities in four regional museums. They seek shifts and irritations of dominant discourses about nature, gender and collective identities, works out new exhibition practices and discusses their potential for change and perceived security.
content.title_en: Through the flower : Gender narratives in museum natural representations

content.text: Key Works of System Theory. Kybernetics -- Communication -- Self-Organization and Autopoiesis -- Mathematics and Logic -- Management and Design -- Sociology and Political Science. System Theory is an attempt to find descriptions of phenomena that are neither so simple that they are causal, nor so random that they can be statistically described. System Theory is about phenomena of self-organization and the question of how the observer can be equipped with a conceptuality that allows him to understand that his descriptions are part of the world and do not operate in an imaginary outside. The second edition supplements the texts of the first edition with conceptual contributions from management and organizational theory as well as with further contributions from general system theory and cognitive science. Moreover, the texts are no longer chronologically arranged, but assigned to certain thematic groups. There are still contributions that appreciate key works of science, and contributions that draw conclusions from key works for his own work. The content · Kybernetics · Communication · Self-organization and Autopo Managementists Theology of Mathematics and Management Sociology and Sophotics Theology of Mathematics and Soology · SoroeInnenwissenschaft · SoroInnen.

content.text: Interaction: How principles of software change philosophy. In software-cast algorithms that defeat chess world masters or successfully exist against humans in question games, the radical changes in a software-driven world that requires bridges between computer scientists and technicians and philosophers to understand them. In this sense, the author argues for a technology pilosophie in which software plays a significant role. Terms experience new perspectives and meanings. The result is a modern form of the three-world model of Karl Popper, now summarized with a glossary of the second-world particle.

content.text: In search of the ideal turtle: Vitruv's description of the basilica in German translations — a semiotic adventure. In the last four centuries, Vitruv's work has been translated into German several times and has been interpreted in a new and sometimes contradictory way. Why is it seemingly impossible to describe architecture in such a precise way that a building can only be reconstructed precisely by the use of a text? Using the example of the various translations of the basilica description Vitruv's, the often superficially postulated context of architecture and language is investigated.
content.title_en: In search of the ideal turtle : Vitruv's Basilica description in German translations — a semiotic adventure

content.text: The incomparables: The change of school systems in the German Länder since 1949. The educational opportunities and school systems differ considerably in the German Länder. This finding has changed little since the founding of the Federal Republic. In "The Incomparables" the attempt is made to compare the seemingly incomparable school policies of the Länder since 1949 (for the East German Länder since 1991) along selected indicators. Here, historical developments, school policy trends and debates are described and analysed. Furthermore, school law types are identified and the Länder are assigned to these types over time. The book presents for the first time a historically comparative systematic overview of the development of school policy in the Federal States. The authors rely on the analysis of about 8,000 legal texts from the last six decades. The data collection thus provided is the basis for further projects of educational research and an indispensable follow-up work of German school policy. This title is deposited in the open access document server pedocs of the DIPF.
content.title_en: The Incomparables : The Change in School Systems in the German Federal States since 1949

content.text: Doing Space while Doing Gender : Networking of Space and Gender in Research and Politics. Doing Space while Doing Gender - this volume opens up new perspectives on the interdisciplinary research field on the relationship between space and gender. In a first book section, articles present central concepts such as "Exposure", "Materiality" and "Visuality". A second book section gathers studies - for example on queer bodies in New York around 1900, the poetry Gloria Fuertes', or on masculinity in the structural change of urban transport. The volume, which can also be used as a manual through the content-related networking of the contributions, shows how dynamics of space and gender are reflected not least in political questions of the present.
content.title_en: Doing Space while Doing Gender : Networking space and gender in research and politics

content.text: Governance of the creative economy: Diagnoses and options for action. This volume discusses current and future control options of the creative industry. International experts from research and practice present the orientation knowledge on new institutions, knowledge management and networked transnational forms of work and problematize the question of the controllability of this emerging field of action.For the first time in the German language area substantial, tailor-made and sustainable understandings and perspectives for the promotion of the creative economy are presented, critically evaluated and placed in a higher-level technical and socio-political context.
content.title_en: Governance of the creative industry: diagnosis and options for action

content.text: Social Urban Policy: Institutions, Networks and Discourses in Political Design. Since the late 1980s, a planning approach has been established in Europe, which uses quartier-related strategies to counteract social-spatial segregation in the big cities. The study reconstructs the development of this policy from early discourses to political decisions and implementation in funding programmes and projects. It shows how the political process has resulted in the respective coupling of problem interpretation and instrumentation. Examples are the EU community initiatives URBAN I and II, the federal-state programme "Social City" and the "Social-Oriented Urban Development" in Berlin.
content.title_en: Social Urban Policy : Institutions, Networks and Discourses in Policy Design

content.text: Optimise websites - The manual. How is a website successful – for companies, associations, associations or private individuals? With easy-to-understand examples and tried-and-tested practical tips, the reader learns how to optimize his website for search engines, improve usability and improve performance, so that visitors to the website enjoy and intensively use the offer.The planning of a website relaunch is presented in just as much detail as the possibilities to successfully market the website themselves. Content: Search engine optimization - Online and search engine marketing - Email and Permission Marketing - Social Marketing - Usability - Accessibility - Avoid security gaps - Performance optimization - Design optimization and relaunch conception - E-Controlling.
content.title_en: Optimising websites - The manual

content.text: WorldKnowledge : Development cooperation in the world society. »Development« is inevitably a reflexive communicative process under the conditions of the globalized knowledge society. After realizing that there is no king path towards sustainable development, new ways of cooperation are being developed, in which global and local knowledge are brought into a fruitful relationship.For the experts involved, this means that they primarily act as consultants, mediators and translators.The volume portrays development cooperation from many examples from practice (politic consulting, democracy promotion, good governance, environmental projects, etc.) as an area in which constantly new global-locally anchored world knowledge is produced and communicated.
content.title_en: WorldKnowledge : Development cooperation in the world society

content.text: Is Turkey part of Europe? : A Europe at a crossroads. Turkey's "Europeability" has been controversially discussed for some time in the European and German public. Many Europeans criticize human rights violations, the inadequate democratization and fear that Europe will be Islamized. Turkey, in turn, can refer to reforms and assert its geostrategic significance in the accession debate. Is Turkey "ready to Europe"? What is the relationship between Turkey and the European Union? Does Turkey belong to a united Europe? The contributions gathered in this volume are statements of speech in a passionate debate that also seeks answers to the question of a European identity. With contributions by Claus Leggewie, Herfried Münkler, Faruk Sen and Hans-Ulrich Wehler, among others.
content.title_en: Is Turkey part of Europe? : A Europe at a crossroads

content.text: Formal SQL tuning for Oracle databases : Practical efficiency - efficient practice. The goal of SQL tuning is to improve the existing execution plan. The method described in this book can be called "brake removal in the execution plan". Such "brake removals" or bottlenecks can be identified by a formal analysis of the execution plan. No data model knowledge is necessary for this. This is particularly beneficial for database administrators because they are usually not or insufficiently familiar with the data model. In the book numerous practical experiences with this method are presented. Introduction -- Oracle databases -- Data modelling -- Execution plans -- SQL tuning in brief -- Index.
content.title_en: Formal SQL tuning for Oracle databases : Practical efficiency - efficient practice

content.text: R compact : The quick introduction to data analysis. This book provides a compact introduction to data analysis with the free statistical environment R. The aim is to provide an overview of the basic scope of R and to enable a quick introduction to descriptive data analysis and the implementation of the most important statistical tests. These are explained in examples and graphically illustrated in many places. In addition, the book covers the many possibilities of creating diagrams, exchanging data with other programs and extending R through additional packages. Thus, the book is suitable for readers to get to know R and quickly use it in specific tasks. . First steps -- Import and export data -- Elemental data processing -- Data sets -- Tools for inference statistics -- Linear regression -- t tests and variance analyses -- Nonparametric methods -- Multivariate methods -- Create diagrams -- R as programming language. .
content.title_en: R compact : The quick introduction to data analysis

content.text: Integrated maintenance and spare parts logistics : Methods, methods, tools. This book describes the analysis and decision-making system for designing and improving production processes in the area of maintenance and spare parts logistics. It shows how the processes and organisation of maintenance and the associated spare parts logistics can be optimized taking into account their dependencies. The second edition covers various new approaches to the more efficient design of maintenance and spare parts logistics. Further development is also the topics for the distribution of maintenance tasks between production and maintenance as well as the outsourcing of technical services. New is the online fault management to support the order processing. A proposal for a total cost structure for maintenance, which can also be used as a basis for the potential determination and later analysis of maintenance processes, completes the new aspects of the second edition. Engineers of operating technology as well as employees and managers of maintenance and spare parts logistics will recognize and appreciate the special value of this work. For students of engineering and business engineering, the book serves as an excellent guide for the application of methods to improve the availability of machines and plants. Developments and trends -- foundations of "integrated maintenance" - goal and key figures system.
content.title_en: Integrated maintenance and spare parts logistics : procedures, methods, tools

content.text: Current legal issues concerning tobacco regulation in Europe. The new study in English examines the legal admissibility of an amendment to the Tobacco Product Directive
content.title_en: Current legal issues concerning tobacco regulation in Europe

content.text: State and Terrorism in Italy 1969-1982. In the 1970s and early 1980s Italy experienced the most intense confrontation between state and terrorism in all Western democracies. The liberal republic and its pluralistic society were put to a hard test by left-wing and right-wing terrorist violent criminals. How did the political establishment perceive this danger? Did the Italian state succeed in fighting terrorism without leaving the constitutional framework? Tobias Hof for the first time comprehensively analyses Italian anti-terrorism policy during the "leaning years" which had a significant influence on domestic political development. It not only promoted the rapprochement between the Christian Democratic and Communist parties, but also offered the Italian political system an opportunity to overcome its legitimacy crisis.
content.title_en: State and terrorism in Italy 1969-1982

content.text: Local talks: Space and Communication in the 19th and 20th centuries. Under the slogan of the spatial turn, 'Space' is currently experiencing an unprecedented renaissance in historical science. However, other disciplines have long been involved in what has quickly become fashion there. The interdisciplinary volume therefore prepares theoretical and knowledge offerings from various neighbouring disciplines for historiographic purposes and at the same time explores the relationship between space and communication in the 19th and 20th centuries using case studies.
content.title_en: Local calls : Space and communication in the 19th and 20th centuries

content.text: From monsters and humans: encounters of the other kind in a cultural-scientific perspective. If monsters emerge in the cultural history of man, they spread terror. At the same time they also represent objects of fascination - precisely because they seem to be different.The contributions of this volume deal with the respective historical form and conceptualization of monsters and illuminate the multi-faceted richness of the monster and the monstrous. Particular attention is paid to the functionality of these figures for the human being, which ranges from identity generator qua border drawing to non-more-human life up to the promise of a posthumanist future.
content.title_en: Of monsters and humans : encounters of the other kind in a cultural-scientific perspective

content.text: Discourse - City - Crime : Urban (un)security from the perspective of urban research and critical crime geography. (Un)security has become a megatrend of urban development worldwide. Public authorities and the private sector are establishing new security policies: monitoring and control techniques, urban planning changes, formalization of social control. However, with increasing crime this cannot be explained. The contributions from urban research and critical crime geography show that the differentiations of safe and insecure places are the result of social and discursive constructions and disclose strategies and mechanisms for the construction of (un)security. This allows new perspectives on the connection between (un)security and city.
content.title_en: Discourse - City - Crime : Urban (Un)Securities from the Perspective of Urban Research and Critical Crime Geography

content.text: Who organises the "needs"?: Quarter designers in disadvantaged urban districts. Even though civil society is often hardly visible in socially disadvantaged neighbourhoods, there are important exceptions: quarter designers are active in civic activity with tireless force.In the book, eight of these extraordinary people are presented in detailed portraits. How did they come to their role, what motives drive them in their commitment, what values they represent? The study provides detailed insights into the functioning of civil society in socially weak neighbourhoods. It identifies obstacles and difficulties for the active people - but also shows perspectives on how the participatory promise of modern civil society for socially disadvantaged people could be fulfilled. Civil engagement on the rings of society - this volume shows what brings people in socially disadvantaged urban districts to engagement in the civil society.
content.title_en: Who organizes the "necessary"? : Quarter designers in disadvantaged urban districts

content.text: The main topic of the project is the "Maturity Management in the Age of Knowledge Society": Trends: Knowledge Management and Resource Knowledge. This Essential provides a compact, up-to-date and practical overview of the importance of the megatrends knowledge society. The authors explain the knowledge management tools available and show examples from practice how they are used in the company. In addition, they present results from market research on the use of knowledge management methods and provide recommendations for action for companies, as knowledge as a new central resource requires a fundamental rethinking in companies, especially in industrially-intensive countries.The content The importance of resource knowledge Examples from practice How to deal with this trend in the company Results from market research and recommendations The target groups Dozierdeen und Studieren der Betriebswirtschaftslehre Mitarbeiter und Entscheider aus dem Personalmanagement Die Autoren Prof. Dr. Anabel Ternès ist Managing Director of the Institute for Sustainable Management and is head of the Bachelor's program International Communication Management at SRH Hochschule Berlin.
content.title_en: Capacity management in the knowledge society: trends: knowledge management and resource knowledge

content.text: The practical manual Social Return on Investment : Measuring the impact of social investments. Making "social return" measurable. How economic profit is measured is known. But how can the social added value of social projects be measured? The SROI analysis tries to assess the added value created by social organizations comprehensively. In this context, the non-economic effects are also taken into account. An example is the business kindergarten: not only the profits of the company, but also the profits of the parents and the municipality are included. The practical manual introduces the functions and prerequisites of the approach and illuminates the opportunities and benefits of this now much discussed calculation tool on the basis of case studies.
content.title_en: Practical guide Social Return on Investment : Measuring the Impact of Social Investment

content.text: The Encyclical Laudato si' : an interdisciplinary approach to sustainability?. Rarely has a papal social encyclical received as much attention and support as Pope Francis' letter Laudato si' about the concern for the common house. Members of the Center for Interdisciplinary Sustainability Research (ZIN) of the University of Münster have accepted the invitation of Pope Francis to respond to his 2015 Encyclical Laudato si', which is published in 2015 and to initiate a dialogue. They present with this volume disciplinary views on the Encyclical, which have emerged from an interdisciplinary discussion. The individual contributions in this volume are questions from theological, political, economic and legal and landscape-ecological perspectives to enrich and promote the statements and positions of the Encyclical Laudato si', in order to discuss the ways and approaches of an integral ecology, an environmentally and socially appropriate economic, policy and lifestyle orientation.
content.title_en: The Encyclical Laudato si' : an interdisciplinary approach to sustainability?

content.text: The system theory is an attempt to find descriptions of phenomena that are neither so simple that they are causal, nor so random that they can be described statistically. System theory is about phenomena of self-organization and the question of how the observer can be endowed with a conceptuality that allows him to understand that he is a part of the world with his descriptions and does not act in an imaginary outside.
content.title_en: Key works of system theory

content.text: School sport 2020 : current research and perspectives in the field of sports teacher education. The focal point volume "School sport 2020" provides an overview of current research results and practical perspectives that were developed in the project of the same name at DSHS Cologne. The project Schulsport 2020 is funded within the framework of the nationwide "Quality Offensive Teacher Education" (QLB). The background of school sport 2020 and the present volume is that sports teachers are not only confronted with known but also new challenges. Of these, the present volume takes up three essential issues, namely (1) an increasingly heterogeneous student community, (2) an ongoing lack of school-based children and (3) the high stress potential of sports teachers, which is due to increasing demands, but also to changing places of instruction and a lack of appreciation of the school subject. In all three areas conclusions for future developments are derived on the basis of new data.
content.title_en: School sport 2020 : current research and perspectives in the field of sports teacher education

content.text: Schooling and Organization : Shape and Problem of State School Regulation. Frank Ohlhaver reconstructs central organizational structuring and stress relations in German schooling (focus on curriculum work) from a structuralist, organizational analysis perspective. He uses an empirical basis of quantitative and qualitative data collected in four old and two new federal states within the DFG project "Secondary Curriculum Formations"
content.title_en: Education and organisation: the shape and problem of state school regulation

content.text: Europeanization of internal security: A comparative study using the example of organised crime and terrorism. The book examines whether and how much internal security policy is Europeanized at national level. Using two key areas of concern, organised crime and terrorism, the question is examined whether Europe's increasing political integration has an impact on the area of internal security, how open to integration this core area of state sovereignty is, whether national specifics, historical and cultural peculiarities affect the political debate and institutional developments, and whether Europeanisation, as it is evident in this field of policy, will hold on to the borders of the European Union. The EU founding members of the EU, Germany, France, Italy, the Netherlands, the later members of the United Kingdom, Spain and Poland, as well as the non-EU countries Norway (Schengen-Land), Turkey (EU candidate country) and Russia, serve as "strategic partners" of the EU.
content.title_en: Europeanisation of internal security: A comparative study of organised crime and terrorism

content.text: The political order of the world is a topic that scientists have been dealing with for more than two thousand years. However, in recent times, the topic has made a career since the US asserts its claim to world hegemony more clearly than before. Europeans torment the idea of an empire of America, which, according to its own decision, is waging wars and which, depending on its usefulness, only uses the former allies in a "coalition of the willing". Two developments must be taken into account: isolation and terrorism. Their cooperation represents a deadly threat to state sovereignty. The states of the Westfälische Ordnung could be crushed in the long term between transnational networks on the one hand and new forms of domination, such as empires and large areas on the other hand. Against this background, eight chapters examine what the world order of the 21st century could look like and what options the European, especially German politics has in this regard.
content.title_en: World governance

content.text: Communication via communication : Theories, methods and practice Festschrift für Klaus Merten. The authors of this publication problematize communication as a basic building block of social systems. According to Merten, the most important definition criterion for communication is its reflexivity in temporal, factual and social terms. This knowledge is characterized by all contributions divided into three blocks: theory, methods/methodology and PR/communication practice. In the theoretical part, important basic concepts are defined and applied; in the methodological part, current developments and critical reflections of the common empirical research methods are discussed. In the practical part, theoretical, critical and empirical findings are compiled into the field of public relations.
content.title_en: Communication about communication : theories, methods and practice Festschrift für Klaus Merten

content.text: Co-integration concepts for credit risk modelling: Systematic credit risks and macroeconomic theory formation. In recent years, the measurement and management of credit risks have become a focus of interest due to the deterioration of the macroeconomic framework and the resulting increase in insolvency. This development is reinforced by the new rules on the capital adequacy of credit institutions developed by the Basel Committee for Banking Supervision. The modelling of credit portfolio risks using mathematical and statistical analysis methods is gaining importance against this background. Matthias Wagatha develops a conditional model framework for credit risk analysis, which establishes an explicit link between systematic credit risks and international macroeconomic systems. To this end, macro-economic theories are established and reviewed using vector author-gressive models in conjunction with co-integration concepts.
content.title_en: Co-integration concepts for credit risk modelling: systematic credit risks and macroeconomic theory building

content.text: Time-consuming modeling of price processes on financial markets : To interpret and need the Usual Conditions. The importance of derivatives for investors on financial markets is increasing. At the same time, it is becoming increasingly important to take into account the uncertainty of future price developments when deciding on the purchase and sale of such titles. However, the assumptions underlying the models used in the analysis of such decision situations have not been questioned and "proven". Stefan Klößner presents in detail the state-preferential approach of Arrow and Debreu, one of the standard models for analysing decision situations on capital markets. In its assumption catalog, the so-called Usual Conditions are of central importance. It is clear that this is only unsatisfactoryly harmonised with the other model assumptions and their application is ill-justifiable.
content.title_en: Timely modeling of price processes on financial markets : On the interpretation and necessity of the Usual Conditions

content.text: Expectation management for innovative communication services : An institutional economic analysis. When introducing innovative communication services, providers are faced with the task of creating a market, because demanders are only ready to invest in communication technology when a satisfactory number of participants is reached. Building positive expectations regarding the future number of users is one of the key adoption factors in this context. Based on the Principal Agent theory, Christina Rabe develops a model for relevance and the conditions for positive demand expectations for innovative communication services. content.text: Overfalls and Weirs : Basics and Calculation Examples. In recent years, water protection has become more important in water management frameworks. The correct calculation of water level courses is of great scientific and economic importance. Rivers and water bodies are regulated with weirs and raids. A correct hydromechanical calculation of these water structures is particularly important for rivers and river courses. The author shows various new hydromechanical model approaches for the calculation of overfalls and weirs based on current, scientifically safe and already known research results. Calculation examples and extensive tables and overviews provide the practitioner with good templates to check existing overfall works and weirs and prepare necessary change plans if necessary. In urban drainage, overfalls and weirs are the most important special constructions in the sewerage system. Here you will also find the wide range of use of weirs.
content.title_en: Robberies and Wehre : Basics and Examples of Calculation

content.text: Development of open youth work in Wolfsburg : In the field of tension between users, social work, municipalities and organizational development. These new requirements for open youth work have been understood by the youth division of the city of Wolfsburg as a challenge, on the one hand, to re-examine the interests of users and on the other hand to initiate an organizational development in the youth division. The Wolfsburg model project "pro11 in wob" was scientifically designed and accompanied by Prof. Dr. Ludger Kolhoff of the Braunschweig/Wolfenbüttel University of Applied Sciences. The Wolfsburg model project represents an attempt, as in the context of social work, here in the example of open youth work, to respond to the new requirements such as market competences, youth work as service, competition with commercial offers etc., without any disadvantage for users and users.

content.text: Universities as filters for human capital: Education and career of high potentials in the USA, France and Germany. How do highly gifted applicants signal their above-average talent to potential employers? A prominent criterion is education, because universities can be interpreted as filter institutions that classify students in different quality levels. Christian Opitz examines three filter models, which can be ideally assigned to higher education systems in the USA, France and Germany, in the context of an organizational economic analysis. The educational and career processes of the top managers of the one hundred market-capital-strongest companies in these countries point to different validation mechanisms for training signals. While in the USA the credibility of certificates and grades is ensured by competition between universities, in France, more emphasis is placed on state control. In Germany, however, the individual reputation of teachers is primarily used as a basis for validation. The book addresses lecturers and students of business administration with the emphasis on management and personnel.
content.title_en: Universities as filters for human capital : Education and career of high potentials in the USA, France and Germany

content.text: Legitimateness and efficiency of administrative innovations. 1 Problem -- 2 Legitimacy and efficiency of administrative innovations -- 2.1 Administrative innovations -- 2.2 Legitimacy and innovation -- 2.3 Legitimacy and efficiency -- 3 Legitimacy bases and degree of legitimacy -- 3.1 Sources of legitimacy -- 3.2 Determining the legitimacy of administrative innovations -- 3.3 Legitimacy as a multidimensional construct -- 4 Legitimacy strategies -- 4.1 Symbolism and adaptation -- 4.2 Advertising and influence -- 4.3 Organization and conflict management -- 4.4 Choice of approach -- 5 Conclusion. The introduction of administrative innovations, i.e. new rules, processes and structures, is often associated with acceptance difficulties among employees and criticism from the business environment. As a result, the expected efficiency gains remain. Anja Tuschke traces the efficiency problems of administrative innovations to lack of legitimacy. A comprehensive analysis of regulatory, normative and cognitive determinants shows which legitimacy problems can arise in the introduction of new rules, structures and processes. Building on findings of the institutionalist approach, the diffusion and network research, and the development of strategies for the motivation and incentive of the author.
content.title_en: Legitimacy and efficiency of administrative innovations

content.text: The introduction of new products on the market is of central importance for the competitiveness of a company. In recent years, marketing measures in the pre-physical market launch phase have been particularly important. However, the advance announcement of new products has been neglected despite their considerable practical relevance by scientific literature. Meike Niedbal examines the way product announcements work on the basis of a model that reflects the reaction of the buyers and competitors. The focus is on the content and timing of product announcements. The author shows that advance announcements can positively influence buyer behaviour, but can also lead to disadvantages on the competitive side, e.g. by imitation. This result is confirmed by an empirical investigation in the medical technology market.
content.title_en: Preliminary announcement of product innovations : A market process theoretical analysis of buyer and competition reactions

content.text: Supply chain coordination in the competitive environment. Competition between companies shifts towards competition between entire value chains. This, in addition to the efficient cooperation of the companies involved in the performance process, gains in importance the interaction with the respective adjacent competition environment (procurement markets, sales markets and competitors). Michael Zimmermann evaluates different coordination mechanisms of a supply chain in a monopoly and in a competitive situation. He shows that counter-coordination and competition effects arise for competing value chains, and compares the advantage of different coordination mechanisms in a monopoly and a duopoly situation on the basis of detailed planning models of operations management. In the context of a numerical study, he shows that the coordination mechanisms preferred in the monopoly can differ from those in competition.
content.title_en: Supply Chain Coordination in the competitive environment

content.text: Preference-Based Recommender Systems : Individual neural preference modeling using the model of investment funds. Knowing customers' preferences is one of the most important prerequisites for successful product policy, and their measurement is a central topic of marketing research. Tobias Schneider presents a new type of recommender systems based on modeling preferences in experimental designs and which use neural networks as a new, flexible method of preference modeling. In an example application, he examines the suitability of his approach as a recommendation system for investment funds, with the focus on the return-risk trade-offs of investors. The results allow a separate segmentation of investors and provide important indications for the design of the marketing mix for investment funds. Further interesting aspects are also evident, e.g. the relationship between the preferences determined and the development on the capital markets.
content.title_en: Preference-based recommender systems : Individual neural preference modeling using the model of investment funds

content.text: Success in retailing through franchising: Increasing process efficiency through web services technologies. Traditional distribution systems such as branch or network systems are increasingly being replaced by aggressive franchising networks, because they are, in the prevailing opinion, very well suited to pursuing demanding expansion goals. A strategic success factor of franchising networks are the efficiency potentials in the value creation system that can be unlocked by information and communication infrastructure (IuK). Stephan J. Meier analyses whether franchising networks place specific requirements on the IuK compared to alternative stationary sales concepts, especially branch systems, and whether web services technologies actually have the efficiency potential attributed to them. The focus of the study is on the better integration of heterogeneous island solutions with the aim of finding flexible, process-oriented applications. The results are based on structuring theoretical considerations in connection with information flow analysis.
content.title_en: Success in retailing through franchising: Increasing process efficiency through web services technologies

content.text: Integration and volatility at emerging markets. Characteristic of emerging markets are high stock yields and a low correlation with the share yields of developed markets, so that diversification of investment investments can reduce portfolio risk. However, the increasing integration of international financial markets could largely nullify this effect. At selected emerging markets, Frank Herrmann examines whether empirical evidence can be found for the two developments mentioned above. He classifys already available ARCH/GARCH models for the adequate description of the volatility patterns of emerging markets and makes an independent model extension to adjust the mean equation. In the empirical test of six different models with regard to their estimation and forecast properties, the model of the author proves to be the most suitable model for the adaptation of the average equation.
content.title_en: Integration and volatility at emerging markets

content.text: Controlling in small and medium-sized enterprises: From business process model to controller profile. Customer orientation and controlling are among the most essential and valuable prerequisites for successfully managing a company. Unlike large companies, these areas of corporate management in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are still little established. Taking into account the specific characteristics of SMEs and the specificities of the target group, Börge Kummert develops an ideal business process model. On this basis, he works out the specificities of an SME controlling and creates the competence profile of an SME controller. Business process model and formulated theses are examined in an empirical survey. Finally, first solutions for a functioning controlling in some performance processes are presented. 1 Introduction -- 2 Definitions -- 3 Process management — Business model -- 4 The ideal typical undertaking -- 5 Controlling — Controller -- 6 SME controlling — SME controller -- 7 Empirical survey -- 8 Solution approaches and basic requirements -- 9 Summary and outlook.

In addition to the programming languages AWL, FUP, KOP, the book also covers program examples in GRAPH, SCL and HiGRAPH. The many sample tasks with very detailed solutions deal with linking and sequence controls, tasks with digital operations (word processing), analog value processing and operations with data modules. content.text: LabVIEW for beginners : with practical exercises. LabVIEW for beginners - From users to users! LabVIEW is a graphical programming language that is primarily used in the field of test automation in industry, especially in measuring, testing and testing systems. The textbook offers a compact introduction to the basic concepts of graphical programming using the data flow principle. In addition, it contains further design patterns and provides sophisticated best practice applications from industry. Numerous graphics and visualised code sections as well as exercises for each chapter enable the reader to quickly find his or her way around the development environment. The book takes into account the guidelines recommended by National Instruments as a LabVIEW manufacturer and provides the latest programming techniques. Written by users, the textbook is aimed at students of electrical engineering with the fields of control technology and automation technology as well as engineers and practitioners from industry.
content.title_en: LabVIEW for beginners : with exercises for practice

content.text: Elements of electronics — Repetitorium and exam trainer : A workbook with circuit and calculation examples. The present exam trainer is the successor book of the book Rechenpraxisen zur angewandte Elektronik of the same author, published in five editions. The book wants to accompany students with practical examples during the study of electronics and pave the way for them through the examination. With overview sheets to the components it provides the necessary basic knowledge and can thus also serve the often necessary knowledge refresher before an examination. According to a normal study process it is structured as follows: Part A Tasks with guidance on the solution Part B Test tasks for self-examination Part C Examination tasks
content.title_en: Electronic elements — Repetitorium and test trainers : A workbook with circuit and calculation examples

content.text: Success factors for a digital future: IT management in times of digitalization and Industry 4.0. Introduction -- What do we mean by information technology? -- What benefits does information technology have? -- How can an IT organization best be optimized? -- CIO -- Final word -- Literature -- Index. Companies need well-functioning IT organisations and powerful IT infrastructures to meet the challenges of digitalization and Industry 4.0. The author explains how successful IT management is possible today. He provides practical recommendations on optimal organizational structures, for the further development of employees and for the consistent business orientation as well as for the development of corresponding strategic goals. The development of tailored governance structures and IT architectures is explained. The necessary quality-enhancing IT standards and service level agreements are presented. An appropriate IT budget planning, continuous partner management as well as the consistent monitoring, control and optimization of important business processes are presented. The author also considers structured demand management, responsive performance calculation, asset and license management as well as the appropriate data management and data analysis factors for a comprehensive overview of CIO.
content.title_en: Success factors for a digital future : IT management in times of digitalization and Industry 4.0

content.text: China First: the world on its way to the Chinese century. China has changed from a Mao-look poor house to a high-tech nation in a few decades. Multi-lane highways and high-speed trains connect the centers. Often it is said that the technology is imported, indeed robbed, and the social and ecological problems are overpowering. But this is a dangerous deception, as Theo Sommer impressively shows. Anyone who has read his lucid book full of surprising facts and connections will see China and the West with different eyes. In ever more future-savings like renewable energies or electric mobility China takes over the lead. The Silk Road project puts important trade routes under Chinese control. Foreign policy is increasingly trumping China, in Asia too military. The new strong man Xi Jinping has secured a wealth of power as she did not even Mao. He perfects the surveillance state with digital face recognition and a "social credit system" reminiscent of Orwell. Here, too, China plays a fearsome pioneering role. The Chinese century has begun. It is now important to understand and maintain.
content.title_en: China First : the world on its way to the Chinese century

content.text: On the way to work 4.0: Innovations in HR. Introduction -- Employability Management -- Life Phase Orientation -- Diversity & Inclusion -- Strategic Human Resources Planning -- Career & Career Management -- Final View. Work 4.0 is probably one of the most commonly used keywords for the future of the world of work at the moment. The present book examines how we will live and work in the future. It shows a central area of tension: On the one hand, it is important to keep moving to keep pace with the diverse trends and rapid changes, but at the same time there is a need to keep balance. This is one of the greatest tasks of our time for employers and employees alike. Based on current empirical studies, holistic concepts and successful corporate examples, the authors from science and practice show that the path to work 4.0 is challenging, but quite designable. The editors Prof. Dr. Jutta Rump is Professor of General Business Administration, in particular International Human Resources Management and Organizational Development at the Ludwigshafen University, and the Institute for Employment and Employment IBE.
content.title_en: On the way to work 4.0 : Innovations in HR

content.text: Albert Einstein, Boris Podolsky, Nathan Rosen : Can the quantum mechanical description of physical reality be considered complete?. Can the quantum mechanical description of physical reality be considered complete?Original text and detailed historical commentary by Claus Kiefer The work of Einstein, Podolsky and Rosen (EPR) from 1935 is one of the classics of modern physics. In it the central characteristic of quantum theory is addressed for the first time: the intertwining. In general, systems in nature are intertwined, that is, they have only a common, non-divisible state. This fact is responsible for all the peculiarities that are commonly associated with quantum theory, which include the thought experiments with Schrödinger's cat and Wigner's friend. The intertwining of quantum mechanical systems plays a central role in experiments with atoms and photons (Nobel Prize 2012 for Haroche and Wineland) and the planned construction of quantum computers. The book brings the original work of EPR in German translation and a detailed commentary part, which focuses both on the quantum theory of the context and the context.
content.title_en: Albert Einstein, Boris Podolsky, Nathan Rosen : Can the quantum mechanical description of physical reality be considered complete?

The book helps the reader to develop economic solutions even for complex plants. It is an indispensable reference work for every planner and operator of industrial wastewater plants. The Hartinger Manual Wastewater Technology is the reprocessing of the classic. In the completely revised 3rd edition all important developments of the last 26 years have been taken into account. Seven authors together with a new editor have updated a lot of content and supplemented new topics and practical experience: new equipment, technologies and procedures for wastewater treatment; electrical engineering for industrial wastewater treatment plants with control and control technology, communication systems and maintenance; a detailed description of the mathematical foundations of process calculation, which is essential for precise plant planning; concrete instructions for selecting the necessary procedures, for measuring equipment and for organizing plant control; the changed legal provisions under EU law.
content.title_en: Hartinger Manual Wastewater and Recycling Technology : Complete in colour

content.text: Digitally networked. Transformation of value creation: scenarios, options and success models for smart business models, products and services. Networked production in the 21st century - inventory and outlook Each product is created in a value creation process from customer requirements to aftersales service to recycling. Companies produce in networked supply chains, no step happens without the exchange of digital data at all levels. The book shows the drivers, the status quo and the perspective of this revolutionary development. There are insights into success models that already exist in certain industries. - Find out what Industry 4.0 and the Internet of Things is today and what the future could look like. - Get a detailed insight into the networked digital value chain of real companies. - What does cyberphysical system, big data, social media, predictive analytics mean. Here you get a comprehensive understanding of these key concepts. The author team from over 20 experts from industry and research will provide a comprehensive and yet compact overview of the topic in this book. No manager should renounce this knowledge. The publishers are Prof. Dr. Patrikia Kraft (Munich Business School) and H.
content.title_en: Digitally networked. Transformation of value creation : scenarios, options and success models for smart business models, products and services

content.text: Statistics: Introduction for economists and social scientists. Verbal and easily accessible descriptions of the statistical methods used in economics characterize this textbook. The application-based presentation is divided into three parts, the descriptive and closing statistics as well as the probability calculation as a link between these two areas. content.text: Creative Communities: A success tool for innovation and customer loyalty. This book considers Creative Communities as a special form of crowdsourcing and shows how they can contribute to supporting the innovation process on the one hand and to increasing customer loyalty on the other. By systematically investigating existing Creative Communities best practice approaches are identified and the success factors analyzed. New insights from the neurosciences are also included and reveal interesting approaches for the optimal design of Creative Communities. Concrete recommendations for action from the practice as well as two case studies are particularly interesting for those companies who want to use Creative Communities as an instrument for innovation and customer loyalty. The content Basics of Creative Communities Success factors for the design of Creative Communities Recommendations for action for companies Future perspectives The authors Prof. Dr. Christa Seja teaches General Business Economics and Marketing at Hannover University of Applied Sciences and Arts. The focus of her research and teaching is on specific topics of Customer Relationship Marketing. In addition to the current challenges of referral marketing and neuromarketing, she is working on the topic of the topic of "Involving in the field of Business Marketing" in Hannover.
content.title_en: Creative Communities : A success tool for innovation and customer loyalty

content.text: The General Social Service under reform pressure: ASD's interaction and organisational systems are changing. For years, the General Social Service (ASD) – the core of the municipal social service network – has been under considerable pressure to develop: it has to cope with increasing case numbers and increased case complexity, flexibly address new technical trends and societal needs, follow the call for holistic, uniform and efficient support services, and carry out organizational reforms in accordance with a modern administrative understanding – all in the context of a persistently difficult municipal budget situation. This book focuses in a compact form on how this diversity of partially conflicting goals can be achieved. Based on a solid theoretical foundation and based on a broad qualitative empirical approach, the author and the author investigates which factors are decisive in order to ensure a "successful ASD practice". This creates a typology of reform approaches, which make it clear that there are viable and promising development paths. In addition to the perspective of the actors, those of the ASD's addressees are also reflected on language and achievements, as are contradictions and obstacles.
content.title_en: The General Social Service under pressure of reform : ASD's interaction and organisational systems in transition

content.text: The Department of Cultural Studies and the Department of Cultural Studies at the University of Dortmund is a research group on the subject of cultural planning: creativity and the cultural dimension of sustainable development. Experimental cultures -- From experimentation in cities -- Promotors and strategies of experimental culture The contributions of the volume deal with the constant processes of change to which cities are subjected. They are characterized by building and decay, chaos and planning. In these, the sociocultural and technical fabric of modern societies cumulates. Symptoms of increasing segregation or the desertification of inner cities are e.g.... On the other hand, social innovations, such as the do-it-yourself movement, in which creative artists and artists increasingly act as interface actors and intervene with their activities in public spaces. The resulting narratives, atmospheres and interpretations of these activities shape the body of a city as sociocultural expressions and trace the narratives of change.
content.title_en: The experimental city: creativity and the cultural dimension of sustainable development

content.text: Professional Lead Management: Step by step towards new customers: an agile journey through marketing, sales and IT. This realistic business novel describes how companies can systematically build a structured and functioning lead management and thus attract new customers. The main character in this story is Helen, marketing manager of a medium-sized company, who is supposed to introduce a professional lead management there. She embarks on an agile adventure journey with heights and depths, on a path full of administrative obstacles, mental blockades and established structures - with the aim of making all participants more successful and significantly increasing sales. An inspiring reading for marketing managers with numerous practical tips that can be implemented directly - packed into a sympathetic and personal history with high recognition value. content.text: The subject of the discussion is the following: education or outcome? : guiding ideas of the standardized school in discourse. Before PISA, school development was primarily thought of from the individual school: school development as the design of the respective individual school with the exploration of its respective strengths and special challenges at the respective location. Since PISA, school development is again centrally thought: education is qua cultusadministrative targets planable, that is, through standardization - can be produced and also over-examined via appropriate methods of performance assessment. The current development can also be called the empiric turn, as the thought, analog many other products of modern life can also be technically established according to normative specifications and the respective outcome can be controlled afterwards. The vocabulary of the current educational reform is also borrowed from industrial production: controlling, benchmarking, quality audits, empowerment, goal agreement etc. This is accompanied by a change of science policy, which according to which also qualitative educational reflection has to differ largely from quantified educational research. The contributions of this topic are critically discussed in the context of the current development.
content.title_en: Education or Outcome? : The guiding ideas of the standardized school in discourse

content.text: The German government's drug representative, the "Drug and Addiction Report", reports that the per capita consumption of pure alcohol in Germany is considered to be high at 10.1 litres per year in an international comparison. More than 10 million people drink alcohol in a risky way in health. 1.6 million people are considered alcohol-dependent. Over 40,000 alcohol-related deaths are reported per year. Against the background of numerous alcohol-related deaths among young people ("flatrate drinking"), the Federal Drug Officer appeals to young people to live up to a restrained, moderate consumption. With this 2nd updated and greatly expanded edition, editors and authors present a further contribution to the "alcohol prevention in education and teaching". Addressees are people concerned with educational tasks, especially teachers, who are offered a pedagogically-diagnosis-oriented perspective of educational-didactic activities. The topics complexes are devoted to the theoretical foundations that justify targeted alcohol prevention, the school-based alcohol prevention as well as extra-school educational learning places, such as family, kindergarten or the Internet. In the end, three examples are being found in the neighbouring preventries, and in Switzerland.
content.title_en: Alcohol prevention in education and teaching
