content.text: Ludwig Leo: Circular tank 2. The circulating tank 2 (UT2, 1967-1974) is an enigmatic landmark of Berlin, which was still under monument protection during the lifetime of its architect Ludwig Leo. Leo's intellectual and design approach is emblematic of the UT2. The iconic building is a laboratory for experiments in currents, for architectural expressions and after its restoration, now also for dealing with young monuments. The book is dedicated to the example of the UT2 of various topics: the today regarded as utopian planning approach of Ludwig Leo, the connecting lines of science, technology and aesthetics that are crossing here, the social conditions of architectural design, as well as the reception and role of monument protection for modern buildings. Architecture as an experiment - Ludwig Leo (1924-2012), Kirowwerk, Hall 9, Leipzig, 20 February to 22 March 2020 and architecture as an experiment - Ludwig Leo's circulating tank, Bauhaus use pavilion, Berlin, 27 March to 24 April 2020.Ludwig Leo (1924-2012), German architect who worked in Berlin.
content.title_en: Ludwig Leo: Circulation tank 2

content.text: CO2: Five to twelve: how we can prevent climate collapse. In a factually, but quite emphatic way, Swiss cultural scientist B. Previsic explains the dangers of climate change. His main focus is on CO2 emissions and its consequences. In the six chapters he criticizes the symbolic policy, which among other things relies on monetary compensation, and instead advocates carbon retention, e.g. in agriculture. The coloured illustrations illustrate Previsic argumentation and facilitate the understanding of the partly complex text. Greenly-underlaid text passages mark the most important findings. A register is not available, the reading notes are commented. Recommended before Lothar Mayer and F. Rademacher, who, unlike B. Previsic, use financial incentives for CO2 reduction. The title gives a good, factual overview of CO2 problems and shows solutions. Also suitable for students of the first semester and students of the upper level. (2, S)
content.title_en: CO2: Five to twelve: how to prevent climate collapse

content.text: The protection of "private" information in cloud computing: an investigation into criminal, data protection and occupational sanctions risks for doctors and lawyers when using cloud services. Cloud computing is hardly possible in the meantime in both private and professional areas. Professional secretaries – such as doctors and lawyers – often face major challenges. They are subject to special regulations that have undergone some changes with the "Law on the Reregulation of the Protection of Secrets in the Participation of Third Parties in the Practice of Persons with a Presence of Confidentiality" and the EU Data Protection Regulation not too long ago. To what extent do doctors and lawyers have to deal with the "new" legal situation, data protection and occupational sanctions risks? This question is addressed by Michael Busching in his investigation. Both the relevant sanction conditions and related problems are identified and systematically discussed as well as possible measures that can prevent sanctioning under circumstances.
content.title_en: The protection of "private" information in cloud computing: a criminal, data protection and professional sanctioning risk for doctors and lawyers when using cloud services

content.text: Politics in digital society: key areas of problems and research perspectives. The importance of digitalization for politics and society is a highly topical topic, which is increasingly being researched and taught in political science. The contributions of the volume therefore gather programmatic positions that represent and discuss central aspects and perspectives of social science digitization research. These include research fields from the fields of participation and party research, governance of digitalization, methodological reflections on computational social science and the analysis of democracy and the public under the conditions of digitalization.
content.title_en: Politics in the digital society: key areas of problem and research perspectives

content.text: Augmented spaces and maps: the design of map-based interfaces. With the convergence of space, media and design, not only design practices are radically changing, but also the surfaces that need to be designed: digital maps enable an interface to the physical world and allow novel forms of navigation and spatial experience. At the same time, internet companies as cartographers are launching discussions about inequalities and hegemonic demands. This book introduces into this field, outlines important influences, theories and approaches and explains with the help of current examples how map-based interfaces can work. However, the foundations developed in this way also provide inspiration for a critical and experimental approach that is relevant for designers, practitioners and a design-oriented audience.
content.title_en: Augmented Spaces and Maps : the design of map-based interfaces

content.text: Autism: Support ideas for German and mathematics : structured exercises for teaching with students in the autism spectrum. Students with an autism spectrum disorder have special features in their perception and thus also in their learning behavior. They need a learning promotion tailored to their individual needs in order to acquire the basic skills in the subjects German and mathematics. Do you want to support your students in a holistic way in learning the reading, writing and arithmetic? In this volume you will find a collection of functional funding possibilities for the subjects German and mathematics, with which you can promote the basic skills from these subjects with your students. In the area of German, students read images, situations and first words, in mathematics they capture quantities, different number spaces and practice addition and subtraction. All exercises are action-oriented and different materials such as plug-in blocks, pearls and picture cards are used. (Verlagstext)
content.title_en: Autism: Support ideas for German and mathematics : structured exercises for teaching with students in the autism spectrum

content.text: Electromobility: Basics and Practice. The IBM electric car of the future! The textbook provides the physical and engineering basics of electric vehicles compared to vehicles with combustion engines. Calculation bases and simulations are developed for core statements. The overall assessment shows under which boundary conditions electric vehicles make sense and what future development will look like including opportunities and risks. content.text: Digitalisation and the digital transformation of the financial economy. The financial economy is at the heart of the attention given to the sectors where the market changes associated with it can be experienced by various interest groups. The changes in financial business processes, not least driven by technology-based startups (so-called FinTechs), are not only noticeable within the industry, but also in the end customer through concrete digital innovations. This volume deals with some of the business models created in connection with the digitalization and digital transformation of the financial economy and considers them against the background of the question whether the financial economy is "only" wrapped in a more modern dress or whether it is about profound market structural changes up to a possible disintermediation within the financial intermediation sector.
content.title_en: Digitalisation and the Digital Transformation of the Financial Economy

content.text: The basics of orbit mechanics. Space travel and space applications play an increasingly important role, especially satellite navigation and communication. At the same time, research into the solar system and space is still a central content of current space programs. For each space mission, detailed orbit calculations are required, e.g. to determine contact times with ground stations or to calculate fuel requirements for maneuvers. This book illuminates this orbit mechanics on the basis of the two-body problem and then builds on it the multi-body problem, i.e. the consideration of several acting gravitational forces. With vivid examples, the application is deepened to enable the reader to perform feasibility analyses and initial assessments. For further calculations, instructions are provided and computation methods are presented, which are typically carried out by computers. The book is aimed at students, users in space travel and interested lay people.
content.title_en: Basics of Orbit Mechanics

content.text: Libraries and Information Society in Germany: an introduction. In the introductory volume Libraries and Information Society in Germany, the German library system of the present day is not presented from a library-based perspective, but from a societal perspective. From this perspective, services and functions of libraries are analysed and evaluated. The authors verify historical development lines, describe current trends and show options for action. Among the changes that libraries and the library system can address and have been partially addressed, in addition to functional changes and systemic networking, also the possible approach to other segments of the information system or even convergence with them. The third edition has been thoroughly revised, continuously updated and extended compared to the second edition. Completely new sections on ethics, law and digital information infrastructure have been edited. Other aspects that have been added or gained considerable weight are research data, specialist information services for science, library as a learning space, new acquisition models, embedded librarian, fake news, makerspaces, the concept of the Green Library or library as a third place.
content.title_en: Libraries and the Information Society in Germany: an Introduction

content.text: The present textbook offers students of the natural and engineering sciences a clear and vivid introduction to the use of measurement data and their interpretation using measurement uncertainty – often called error calculation. This book focuses on the understanding and the teaching of directly applicable knowledge. Long mathematical derivations are largely omitted. Based on some simple basic principles such as the distribution of measurement values or the mathematical model of a measurement, this book introduces into central topics: - the measurement itself, - the indication of measurement results, - the concept of uncertainty, - the evaluation of measurement data using different methods, - as well as the evaluation of the results obtained. All these topics are presented in detail using various examples and the application of abstract concepts based on concrete numerical examples. Questions about self-control and the deepening of the contents round each chapter. The authors Philipp Möhrke is working at the University of Konstanz as lecturer for subject didactics of physics. Bernd-Uwe Runge has illustrated the management of the physical beginner's internship at the University of Konstanz. For their outstanding results in the field of measurement analysis, the new results of measurement are presented in an innovative form.
content.title_en: Working with measurement data : a practical short introduction to GUM

content.text: 100 years of Gross-Berlin ; 5: Settlement Star : Perspectives radically radial. Berlin and its surroundings present themselves today as settlement star. Rail paths and down roads formed a memorable growing settlement form since the end of the 19th century. This radial structure was complemented by rings: the ring railway, the inner highway (part) ring, the (so far little-noticed) outer railway ring and the outer motorway ring. This special ring radial framework reflects both: the tradition of rail-bound public transport such as the - shorter - tradition of the car-friendly city region. The settlement star is not only a linear framework. It connects a multitude of medium, small and smallest centers, which give a distinctive face to the metropolis in their historical and cultural peculiarities and offer the best conditions for sustainable spatial development.
content.title_en: 100 years of Gross-Berlin ; 5: Settlement Star : Perspectives radically radial

content.text: Encounter with the material: perspectives from architectural history and sociology. Dealing with things and material structures has always been one of the central experiences of aesthetic production. At the same time, digital processes and ecological paradigms are currently opening up new perspectives. The contributors of the volume investigate how encounters with the material can be theoretically described in architecture, art and design, historically anchored and empirically sociologically analyzed. To what extent can these encounters be conceived as meaningful or sensual? Which forms of perception or experience are practiced or aspired? And how does the material relate to concepts of the social?
content.title_en: Meeting with the Material : Perspectives from Architecture History and Sociology

content.text: OECD Guide to Compliance with the due diligence to promote responsible supply chains for minerals from conflict and high-risk areas. Trade in mineral resources and investments in these resources offer great potential for generating income, growth and prosperity, for sustaining livelihoods and promoting local development. However, these mineral resources are found to a large extent in conflict and high-risk areas where they are largely mined. This can lead directly or indirectly to armed conflicts and serious human rights violations and impair economic and social development. The OECD Guide to Compliance with the due diligence to promote responsible supply chains for minerals from conflict and high-risk areas contains officially supported recommendations that guide companies step by step to responsible global supply chain management for all minerals in order to respect human rights and to avoid conflict by making decisions and practices in the procurement of minerals or metals. This Guide can be used by all companies that could obtain minerals or metals from conflict or high-risk areas. The objective is to create transparent, conflict-free supply chains and sustainable entrepreneurial engagement in the mineral sector.
content.title_en: OECD Guide to Compliance with Due diligence to Promote Responsible Supply Chains for Minerals from Conflict and High-Risk Areas

content.text: Annotating, commenting, explaining : aspects of media change. Annotating, commenting and explaining texts is one of the core philological tasks. In the digital context, the commentary work faces new and hardly to be underestimated challenges. While the directly text philological components such as text constitution or variant representation have been thoroughly addressed in recent years, the discursive parts (transmission, origin, comment, etc.) and their integration into digital edition concepts remain largely disregarded. Fundamental theoretical aspects of digital commenting concern both cross-media issues such as the possibilities of linking to external sources and the integration of standard data as well as media-specific issues of commenting such as the structure specific to text and/or genre.
content.title_en: Annotating, commenting, explaining : aspects of media change

content.text: School buildings: rooms for learning and for the community. School architecture and building details. School develops into a full-day model in many countries with homework support, canteen and leisure activities. Future-oriented pedagogical methods of teaching and learning bring with them changing planning requirements. Just as the classical teaching structure is broken down, the new rooms are flexible or become part of an open learning landscape with cuddly corners and movement areas for climbing or racing. This publication deals with different school concepts as learning, social and living space and presents 20 project examples from construction to detail. 1. Exemplary school buildings for forward-looking learning scenarios. 2. Flexible school rooms and open learning landscapes. 3. Current projects from all over Europe.
content.title_en: School buildings : rooms for learning and for the community

content.text: Modern app development with dart and flutter: a comprehensive introduction. Dart is a programming language developed from 2013 onwards, which Google has been using since 2018 to program the Flutter framework for developing cross-platform apps. The book here is a good addition to Reto Meier or Ralph Steyer, which deals with the development of Android or iOS apps. The author is looking at programmers interested in cross-platform programming of apps. Basic knowledge in object-oriented programming is provided by the reader, additional knowledge in Java or JavaScript is very helpful. The book begins with an introduction to dart and app programming with flutter. In a practical part, examples (including the Messanger app for connecting with the cloud, 2-D game "Chicken Maze"), the more special programming techniques of dart and flutter are explained. The well-structured book deals with Dart in version 2.7.2 and Flutter in version V 1.12. Many illustrations and graphically highlighted error notes. (1)
content.title_en: Modern app development with dart and flutter : a comprehensive introduction

content.text: "New Control" - Renaissance of cybernetics?. This supplement has three objectives: firstly, it should contribute to the question of whether technocratic control concepts prevail at the various levels of the school system or which more development-oriented models are applied at the different levels of control. Secondly, it should contribute to an overarching discourse on control questions and models in the school system by presenting positions on educational monitoring and on control practices empirically to be found in the school system. Finally, it should show possible "risks and consequences" of increasing "datedities" of the educational by "learning analytics" and thus enable the introduction into a technological assessment which is obvious in other areas of policy and technology. content.text: Software Engineering - compact. In the software engineering chapter, the most important topics relating to software engineering are explained, summarized and deepened with small practical examples. The software life cycle is of central importance for software engineering. This is the whole process leading to the creation and maintenance of a software system. This life cycle is carried out in both traditional and agile software creation processes. In practice, the division into so-called phases that follow the structure is proven. After a short introduction, in Chapter 2, the process is discussed in advance, such as diverging procedure models and project management. Chapter 3 deals with the planning phase; Chapter 4 is dedicated to the requirements engineering, in which the software requirements are creatively constructed, analysed and – traditionally or agile – documented. Chapter 5 follows the discussion of the procedures for the design phase of the software. Here, a structured orientation is called up to the requirements engineering, and in this case the implementation of the software is explained in a good manner.

Mathematics has always been a special fascination for many. content.text: Augmented reality in e-commerce: the advantages of technology for online retail. Folding text: Augmented reality is increasingly in the focus as technology for product presentations in the online store and as a means to secure company success. As the experience from practice and some studies show, the type of product presentation determines the customer experience, the perceived risk of buying and trust in the decision taken. The focus of this study is therefore an analysis of this cause-effect-fabrication when using Augmented reality for product presentation in the online store. Likewise, the interactivity and realistic representation as components of the technology are examined. In order to identify the importance of these factors, the postulated relationships were examined with the help of an empirical study. The results confirm the influence of the correct product presentation on the success of an online shop. Both the components realistic representation and the possibility of interaction, as well as augmented reality as a whole, influence the consumer's satisfaction with the online shop decisively.
content.title_en: Augmented reality in e-commerce : the benefits of technology for online commerce

content.text: 40 years of BORDA: Water, hygiene and living for all!: sustainable with BORDA from Bremen into the world. "Over two billion people still have no access to clean water. Almost four billion have no hygienic and environmentally sound disposal of their domestic waste water. Almost one billion have to do their emergency needs outdoors. Thus, they lack basic livelihoods to lead a healthy and self-determined life. Already in 1977, Bremer citizens committed themselves to better living conditions in poverty areas in the Global South and founded BORDA (Bremen Overseas Research and Development Association). Since then, this non-profit non-governmental organization has improved the living conditions and educational opportunities of future generations in Asia, Africa and Latin America through clean water and better sanitation. With the sustainability goals of the United Nations, the world community of water, hygiene and sanitation has given a key role for living together on our planet. BORDA and its partners are involved in more than 20 countries of the world in a civil society, state and private sector. For over 40 years, Bremen has been giving impetus to this community of 13 activists, bringing this kind of light to the world's inhabitants.
content.title_en: 40 years BORDA : Water, hygiene and living for all! : sustainable with BORDA from Bremen into the world

content.text: Probability and statistics: an introduction to understanding, intuition and overview. Beschr.: This textbook introduces the central concepts and concepts of probability calculation, descriptive and final statistics. The focus is on an intuitive understanding of the basic concepts, contexts and methods. Nevertheless, the material is presented mathematically precisely. Within each chapter you will find various didactic elements that make it easier for you to access and understand, but also to provide orientation: a brief overview of the most important concepts at the beginning of the chapter, visual explanations and examples, central facts and definitions, warnings of frequent misunderstandings, separate text sections on intuition, graphic or tabular overviews at the end of the chapter. At the end of most sections you will find short learning controls IBM here you can check your knowledge by classifying different statements as true or false. The solutions can be found in the appendix, depending on the degree of difficulty with a short solution. At the end of the chapter you will also find comprehension questions, which will ask the most important content and thus show your progress in learning.
content.title_en: Probability and statistics : an introduction to understanding, intuition and overview

content.text: In discourses about the professionalization of teachers for inclusive schools, casuistic approaches in teacher education are experiencing new economic conditions. The volume asks in what relation casuistics, teacher education and inclusion are (can). In the first part, fundamental questions of casuistic teaching are addressed and conceptualizations of different approaches of casuistics for an inclusive teacher education are discussed. In the second part, empirical studies on the implementation of casuistic events of teacher education are presented and theoretically discussed. In the third part, studies are presented which examine the yields of casuistic teaching with different data types. Overall, the volume discusses how casuistic teaching can be developed and researched and what contribution it could make to the professionalization (inclusive) pedagogical action.
content.title_en: Case Studies - Teacher Education - Inclusion : Empirical and theoretical relationship determinations

content.text: History for gluing: historical events in the mirror of German stamps. Stamps are bearers, symbols and ambassadors of the states that issue them and thus a remarkable projection surface of the respective historical policy. Of great interest here are the motifs of the stamps, which span a long time frame from the antiquity to the Middle Ages and the early modern era to the modern age. They show to what extent the interpretation of historical events and persons changed in a diachronic way. Stamps therefore also reflect the historical policy of the respective states in their time. This applies particularly to the two German states existing between 1949 and 1990. Their dispute over the interpretation of German history and the use of positive traditions also expressed itself in various forms in the stamp production. The authors examine by means of the example of the stamp motifs, which events and persons are remembered by stamps and in which connection this is with the respective historical policy.
content.title_en: History for gluing : historical events in the mirror of German stamps

content.text: The healing power of Christian rituals and symbols : find meaning, come to rest, experience healing. A teacher and speech therapist as well as the head of a religious pedagogical center examine the meaning of life-affirming symbols and rituals and span a bow from their general to their specific Christian understanding. They analyze their origins and meaning in everyday life, proverbs and customs and their beneficial and healing effects. Then they turn to Christian rituals and symbols in detail and question their meaning, biblical sources and healing powers in the daily routine and in liturgical celebrations. They also show how to trace the healing powers of life through the senses, interpret healing basic attitudes (accompaniment, love, trust and faith) and refer to modern brain research (e.g. on Gerald Hüther) to confirm their statements. With many quotations, poems, stories, Bible excerpts and interpretations, which provide access to a lived Christian faith. - Encouraging, sustaining, inviting to meditate.
content.title_en: The Healing Power of Christian Rituals and Symbols : Finding meaning, coming to rest, experiencing healing

content.text: Allplan 2020. The Allplan Practice Book for Architects and Civil Engineers This standard work in 9th edition is aimed at architects and civil engineers who want to realize their planning processes with Allplan. It describes functions and processes that are essential for optimal work with CAD software. The practical book is aimed at both beginners and professionals who want to learn or deepen the handling of Allplan. Using the consistent example project of a residential and commercial building, the individual planning steps are demonstrated: from the preparation of the location plan and the creation of the building model, through cuts, views and reports, to the layout and output on paper or as a file. The new and revised functions from Allplan 2020, which are discussed in this edition, include developments in the areas of 3D modelling, levels, associative dimensioning, visualization, BIM and UTM data import. The internet provides the data of all the examples and further information available in the book. On the Allplan website you can download a 30-day demo version of 2020 free of allplan.

Artificial Intelligence in Practice - Symbol Processing Artificial Intelligence and Neural Networks in a Book - Business Rules and Knowledge Networks - Convolutional Neural Networks and Deep Learning - Exercises in PROLOG as well as with JavaNNS and Python Artificial Intelligence has reached our daily lives: We use chatbots, talk to speech assistants, AI digitizes document processing, pattern, image or object recognition. content.text: Dealing with aggressive behaviour of children: practical competence for daycare. Aggressions are a natural part of human behavior. Yet – understanding them and dealing with them poses challenges for educational professionals every day. This book creates a change of perspective – away from "disturbing child" to "meaningfulness" and occasionally needing aggressive behavior. Conflicts do not therefore constitute an incident in daycare, but rather a field of learning and an opportunity for development. With practical explanations and lively examples, educational experts are taught about possible causes and the appropriate handling of aggression in everyday pedagogical life. (back page Book cover)

content.text: Living sustainability with children: the impulse for value-based education in the day care centre. In the sense of "Education for sustainable development" (e.g. promoting independent thinking and acting), the author aims to achieve nothing less than a paradigm shift in childcare: away from individual education to a life-spractical activity education. After an actual analysis (short excursion into the exploitation of nature) she presents her approach and then dedicates the values needed for it to a chapter: Responsibility for the future, mindfulness & care, economy & care, gratitude & humility as well as discipline. She defines these values and gives suggestions to implement this value-based education in everyday life. The book is aimed at educational professionals and certainly meets a nerve - even if it remains quite theoretical and content is probably not undisputed in professional circles (sirrespective understanding of nature). Similar basic ideas such as P. Ritcher or "Nature, Ecology and Sustainability in Kindergarten. After "Sustainability from small to small" and "Environmental Ethics for Children". (3)

content.text: Philosophy of Time: Fundamentals and Perspectives. This supplement contains three objectives: firstly, it should contribute to the question of whether technocratic control concepts prevail at the various levels of the school system or which models, which extend beyond cybernetic cycles and are more development-oriented, are applied at the different levels of control. Secondly, it should contribute to an overarching discourse on control issues and control models in the school system by presenting positions and views on educational monitoring and control practices empirically to be found in the school system. content.text: Language education in the subject-matter of primary school education: with the scaffolding concept on the way to the educational language. Publisher's info: In order to participate successfully in the teaching, pupils in all classes must continuously expand their technical content and linguistic skills. The concept of scaffolding meets this didactic challenge with a teaching arrangement, in which the teachers consciously plan and shape the transition from everyday to technical and educational language. Already in the primary school, increasingly complex linguistic requirements are placed on the pupils, which offer important opportunities to develop educational language skills and think about language. This hand-out introduces the linguistic and learning-heoretical contexts of the scaffolding concept in the subject-matter teaching of primary school. The corresponding 16-minute teaching film "A puddle in the sky is not called puddle!" supplements the text and illustrates the implementation of the scaffolding concept in a third class of a natural science teaching unit. It offers the possibility to observe the linguistic statements, which are available as a transcription, as well as the interactions and learning of the children directly to the teaching language. The hand-powering and teaching of teachers are interested in teaching and teaching.
content.title_en: Language education in the primary school's practical education: with the scaffolding concept on the way to the language of education

content.text: Complex organization: Digitization as the driving force of a changed working world. Digitization and the working world are in a complex relationship between each other. How work is organized and shaped has been strongly influenced by technological developments for several decades. In addition, digitalisation significantly increases the pace of these changes induced by technology and thus leads to a decisive increase in complexity. Nevertheless, it is ultimately human actors who decide how work is organized at the legal, cultural, political and social level. How can future-oriented organizations actively shape the "new world of work? How do platform-based business models change work organisation? And what social policy demands are connected with a "culture of digitality? The co-production of technology and society is a highly topical topic of science and research-oriented practice, especially with regard to the increasingly complex work organisation.
content.title_en: Complex organization: digitalization as the driving force of a changing working world

content.text: ICILS 2018 #Germany: Computer and information-related competences of pupils in the second international comparison and competences in the field of computational thinking. The IEA study ICILS 2018 (International Computer and Information Literacy Study) measures computer and information-related competences of eight-year-olds in the international comparison for the second time after 2013. The study thus provides a current picture of the state of digital education in Germany. In this volume, empirically based statements on developments over a multi-year period are presented. Also for the first time, findings on the competence area of Computational Thinking are presented in the context of an international additional module, which addresses the solving of problems and the competent handling of algorithmic structures. By means of the detailed assessment of the framework conditions at school, teacher and student level as well as from the perspective of school leaders and IT coordinators, the study provides an overall picture of technological and pedagogical developments in Germany in an international comparison. Results on central background characteristics of the students and on school forms complement the study of the study of digital knowledge and the study of the study of the study of the study.
content.title_en: ICILS 2018 #Germany : Computer and information-related competences of students in the second international comparison and competences in the field of computational thinking

content.text: Fear in disaster research: interdisciplinary approaches. Considering that only two institutions were involved in the conference from which this collection was formed, with the disaster research office of the Freie Universität Berlin and the Institute for Psychoanalytic-Ethnological Disaster Research at Sigmund-Freud-Privatuniversität Wien, the multitude of interdisciplinary approaches opened in the book is very considerable. – Florian Grafl, in: Zeitschrift für Volkskunde 116. Jahrgang 2/2020, S.286-289. While psychology and psychotherapy deal extensively with the phenomenon of fear, he is often given little attention outside of these disciplines. Even in disaster research, an explicit reference to fear is less likely to be found than could be assumed. In fact, however, earthquakes, storm floods or aircraft crashes act as triggers existential fears, because they threaten the need for security and consequently the identity of both individuals and collectives. In view of such a connection, the conference of the KatNet disaster research network at the Free University of Berlin and the Institute of Disasterology offers the topic of disaster research on the topic of "Thropology-Psychology".
content.title_en: Fear in disaster research : interdisciplinary approaches

content.text: In the 2018 IQB educational trend, the results of the second country comparison of the Institute for Quality Development in Education (IQB) in mathematics and in the natural sciences subjects Biology, Chemistry and Physics in secondary education are reported. In the above-mentioned subjects, the competences of 9th grade students are examined, which were recorded in 2018. In addition to the 2018 survey, the focus is on trend analyses, which show to what extent the competence level achieved by 9-year-olds in the subjects studied has changed since 2012. The basis for this report is the mandatory education standards of the Education Conference for all countries, which determine the subject-specific competences of pupils up to a certain point in their school career. In addition to the competences achieved by 9-year-olds in the countries, the report also analyses the relevance of the school-related, social and migration-related subjects in the German language and the extent to which these subjects have been analysed in the course of the year.

content.text: Digitalisation of the education system: Tasks and perspectives for teacher formation. As the essence of the digital transformation of education, the core competencies of educators become more important than ever. The more work of machines is done, the more important tasks become that specifically demand something human. For example: working with other people, working with relationships, understanding different positions and developing sustainable ideas for a human-oriented society – tasks that teachers already work on today. The conference "Diggi17 – Enter Next Level Learning" has described essential guidelines for a positive course of digitisation of education. In four chapters, the book combines knowledge, experiences and assessments of international authors from various areas of digital education. It addresses powerful developments connected with digital transformation and shows how the teaching profession can emerge strengthened from digital transformation.
content.title_en: Digitization of the education system : Tasks and perspectives for teacher education

Overrunn inner cities, intensified regulations, protests by residents – tourist processes are increasingly being discussed in ambivalent constellations: increased attractiveness, city conflicts and mass individual tourism lead to intensifying conflict situations and demarcation tendencies. Using the example of a city like Freiburg and a landscape like the Black Forest, the contributors of this volume also discuss exemplar touristic phenomena in contrastive tension between "Snibelichtung" and "Snibelen überbeit die Beziken.
content.title_en: Sightseeing / Sightfleeing : Experiments of ethnographic tourism research

content.text: Automation technology : Methods for monitoring and controlling continuous and event-discrete systems. This book provides a broad introduction to the tasks and methods of automation technology and illustrates them in numerous application examples. Topics range from modeling to predicting future system behavior, designing regulations and controls to process diagnosis. The fourth edition improves and expands the presentation of methods, examples and exercises
content.title_en: Automation technology : Methods for monitoring and controlling continuous and event-discrete systems

content.text: Access to the theory of literature : 17 Model analyses of E.T.A. Hoffmann's Der Sandmann. Literature theory is an important component of any philological or cultural studies. However, the field of theories often appears to many students uncontroversial and difficult to access. This volume provides orientation not only by presenting different theoretical approaches, but also by testing them in one and the same text in their practical application. After the complete print-out of E.T.A. Hoffmann's narrative "Der Sandmann", 17 well-known experts from the perspective of 17 different literary theories examine the text. Here, both classical approaches (hermeneutics, new historicism, reception aesthetics or structuralism/literature emiotics) as well as the latest currents (acteur network theory, biopoetics, trauma theory, space theory or visual/media studies) are discussed.
content.title_en: Accesses to the theory of literature : 17 Model analyses of E.T.A. Hoffmann's Der Sandmann

content.text: 45 electronic projects for the Raspberry Pi. The 3rd edition of the Raspberry Pi, which was last published in 2017, is not shown here, and with 45 practical experiments, the edition is now being updated and expanded. The comparison of the table of contents (via DNB Opac, 2nd edition was not available) shows that the author has completely revised and expanded the chapters two and three. New addition is chapter 13 "Bluetooth projects". This edition has 47 pages more, but is still five euros cheaper. In addition to a short introduction to the Raspberry Pi, the author gives a short introduction to the operating system Linux and programming with Bash, Python and JavaScript, with the emphasis on Python. The 45 projects can be easily re-built by the clear descriptions, switching plans and photos for the construction. The existing index makes it easy to find projects. Thus, the book is not only available as a textbook, but also as a reference work. (2)
content.title_en: 45 electronics projects for the Raspberry Pi

content.text: Pandemics: Corona and the new global infectious diseases. Pandemics, which spread across countries and continents of infectious diseases, are a dark side of globalization, especially international aviation tourism. Even before the emergence of the new Coronavirus, this has been the case with a whole range of infectious diseases; cholera, HIV (AIDS), influenza and SARS are prominent examples. Looking at the current situation, the band explains the strategies to contain pandemics and their impact on the economy, politics and participation in public life. Can a virus that has not been known yet be stopped at all, or is it only a matter of time until a large part of the population is infected? What can the individual do, or is he powerless? How far can a democratic state put the basic conditions of social life out of force to preserve the health of the population? (publisher text)
content.title_en: Pandemics : Corona and the new global infectious diseases

content.text: The vulnerable world: a hypothesis. Bostrom assumes that technological development inevitably moves towards a point where it becomes critical. Historically, this was almost the case, as he illustrates with a breathtaking thought experiment that is playing in the Cold War period. Then he develops some only too plausible scenarios that would most likely bring about the demise of human civilization IBM unless we take countermeasures in time. In the second part of this important book, which concludes with recommendations to politics, Bostrom discusses which of these could be. (Verlagstext)
content.title_en: The vulnerable world : a hypothesis

content.text: Are we in a situation similar to that of the Weimar Republic? Adam Przeworski is looking for answers by looking at states that have been slipping away in authoritarian conditions. He identifies three sets of causes: economic and prosperity, inequality, social, but also in the narrower sense of political. Today, the situation in many states is characterized by the fact that parts of the population no longer participate in the growing prosperity and have lost faith in a better future. But if people get the impression that they could no longer positively influence their lives through elections, the probability that they will turn against the system is increasing.
content.title_en: Crisis of democracy

content.text: The women's atlas : Understanding inequality: 164 infographics and maps. At a glance: How do women live worldwide? How big is gender inequality really? Where are progress made, where are there problems? Joni Seager's women's atlas gives comprehensive answers in 164 infographics based on the most important studies worldwide. Doubtless as many women as men can't read and nothing has changed in this relationship for over 20 years. In Germany, women only earn 79 percent of what men get. They do 4.4 hours of unpaid household work per day, men 2.7 hours. Internationally, the women's atlas has long become an important institution, in Germany it is urgently needed. (Verlag text)
content.title_en: The Women's Atlas : Understanding inequality: 164 Infographics and maps

content.text: Construction site Electromobility: Social science perspectives on the transformation of (auto)mobility. Our mobility is changing. Electric cars are on the rise and are being praised as a central solution for many transport problems. However, this change in drive technology is too short, because it brings with it new social and ecological problems for raw materials policy and the global value chain. But also mobility concepts around car sharing, autonomous driving and other approaches to the traffic turnaround leave many questions open. The contributors coming from different disciplines deal with these highly topical developments and provide orientation in the examination of the transformation and future of (auto)mobility.
content.title_en: Construction site Electromobility : Social science perspectives on the transformation of (auto)mobility

content.text: Heterogeneity in vocational education : in the field of tension between education, promotion and specialist education. How does the heterogeneous composition of the student community determine the teaching-learning processes in vocational education? In 14 articles the authors discuss opportunities and challenges of personality development and specialized training in vocational education. The topic of heterogeneity is reflected from the perspective of general pedagogy, teaching and resilience research as well as professional didactics. Other aspects are language development, multi-religious contexts and value education. A large part of the contributions were made in the working group "Inclusion and Handling Heterogeneity in Vocational Education", which belongs to the quality offensive teacher education (QLB), which is promoted by the federal government and the Länder.
content.title_en: Heterogeneity in vocational training : in the field of education, promotion and technical training

content.text: Post-growth city: contours of a solidarity-based urban policy. Cities without growth – a vision that has so far been hard to imagine. But climate change, waste of resources, growing social inequalities and many other dangers of the future fundamentally call into question the panacea growth. How do we want to live together today and tomorrow? How do we shape a good life for everyone in the city? While these questions are already answered in some niches, there is still a lack of comprehensive designs and transformation approaches that contemplate a fundamentally different, solidarity-based city. This attempt is ventured by the Post-growth City project. In this book, conceptual and pragmatic aspects from various areas of urban policy are brought together, which show and link new paths. The contributions discuss urban growth crises, transformative planning and conflicts about design power. Not least, the question about the role of urban utopias is also being asked anew. This is intended to initiate a long-due debate on how to realize necessary urban changes through social ecological reorientation on the spot.
content.title_en: Post-growth city : contours of a solidarity-based urban policy

content.text: Post-growth geographies: Spatial references of various and alternative economies. Geography of post-growth investigates the spatial references of various and alternative economies in the field of tension between growth-oriented institutions and multiple social ecological crises. The contributors of the volume take this approach up comprehensively for the first time and open up different perspectives with conceptual and empirical contributions from geography and its neighbouring disciplines on the possibilities, demands and criticisms of a social ecological transformation. In case studies and interviews voices from activism, civil society, planning and politics are gathered with current theoretical debates on post-growth economies.
content.title_en: Post-growth geographies : Space supplies of various and alternative economies

content.text: Media quality : Discourses from the Grimme Institute on television, Internet and radio. What quality do media have? Are they "worth" to be awarded? After being sensational in the 1960s to honour quality on television with the Grimme Prize, the Grimme Online Award was added as a major innovation 20 years ago to award high-quality internet offers - and for ten years the German Radio Award has been acknowledging the quality and strengths of radio programmes.The contributors of the volume are for the first time acknowledging the backgrounds of quality and media from the Grimme Institute's perspective, with a view to its jury and from a scientific perspective.
content.title_en: Media quality : Discourses from the Grimme Institute on television, Internet and radio

content.text: Image traces - language traces : Postcards as sources of multilingualism in the late Habsburg monarchy. As widely used short news carriers, which in a new way integrated visual and linguistic elements around 1900, postcards have a still hardly accessible potential for exploring multilingual communication spaces. The contributors of the volume use the multi-layered nature of this everyday medium to expose image and language traces from the multilingual Habsburg monarchy. How did postcards visually and linguistically shape public space? How did the self- and foreign images of the people living there shape? And what do the concrete forms of use of postcards tell about exchange and language practice? The postcard enables an illuminating view »from below« on multilingual societies.
content.title_en: Images - Language tracks : Postcards as sources of multilingualism in the late Habsburg monarchy

content.text: Prototyping society - the precipitating technologization of the future. Prototypes migrate from workshops to society. They are no longer considered to be deficient, because incomplete objects. Rather, the design of the materially provisional shapes and technologizes the social over-morrow. The production and reception of these artifacts transforms from an exclusive expert activity into a public social practice: prototypes are produced in publicly accessible Makerspaces and celebrated in urban event formats. Sascha Dickel shows that this can also involve a new form of criticism, which does not oppose the technologization of the social, but opens up ways to design alternative futures in a technologically installed world.
content.title_en: Prototyping society - for the advance of the future

content.text: Fragile values : Discourse and practice of the restoration sciences 1913-2014. »Fragil« we call fragile material as well as vulnerable social constitutions. Fragile oscillates between affirmative assessments and insecure connotations. Nathalie Bäschlin presents the thesis that the fragile has developed into a separate category of values that has a lasting influence on our view of art and the formulation of the conservation mission. She asks about the historical context, the motivations that have drawn our attention to the fragile, and how the examination of fragility permeates the practice and discourse of museum preservation.
content.title_en: Fragile Values : Discourse and Practice of the Restoration Sciences 1913-2014

content.text: Imaginations of sustainability: catastrophe, crisis, normalization. Klappentext: Imaginations of sustainability design different possibilities for a social-ecological change. As positive or negative worlds of imagination, disaster fears and end-time scenarios emerge, normality conjures up and ecological ignorance, technical belief and optimism of progress, but also utopian images of a good life in the consciousness of the present. What tensions and conflict lines arise when modern societies are guided by such contravening imaginations of sustainability? With contributions by Frank Adloff, Gerard Delanty, Benno Fladvad, Martina Hasenfratz, Eva Horn, Albrecht Koschorke, Sighard Neckel, Heike Paul and Peter Wagner.
content.title_en: Imaginations of sustainability : disaster, crisis, normalization

content.text: The epistemical images: the media onto epistemology of visualisation. If something becomes visible in scientific contexts, then often because it has been made visible in experimental processes. The operative »distinctization« allows new perspectives on the disjunctive interlinkage of scientific and media history. An archaeology of the visible - as it can be understood, for example, by the example of microphotographic processes of bacteriology - emphasizes the material-discursive configuration of knowledge production. The generated »epistemic images« thus act as relays between knowledge and visibility. Sebastian Scholz approaches this complex constellation with the aim of problematizing »the visible« and of showing the potential of an operative media onto epistemology.
content.title_en: The epistemical images : on the medial onto epistemology of visualisation

content.text: Study projects in the practical semester: Basics and examples of research students in music teachers' education in North Rhine-Westphalia. The volume responds from the perspective of the subject music to the introduction of the format of study projects within the practical semester in North Rhine-Westphalia and is aimed at both university teachers and students. Typical decision-making fields in the planning, implementation and evaluation of projects are presented to researchers learning. The theoretically guided statements on goals, methodological and methodological principles are linked with the presentation of exemplary questions, seminar concepts and music (education)-related study projects. The texts are designed in such a way that they support the conception of teaching events, but can also be used directly as basic literature or training material. In addition, the contributions aim is to open a discussion about the design of music teachers' education at the North Rhine-Westphalian locations as well as beyond.
content.title_en: Study projects in the practical semester : Basics and examples Researchers Learning in music teacher education in North Rhine-Westphalia

content.text: Fridays for Future – the youth against climate change: contours of the worldwide protest movement. With Fridays for Future, the climate protests have gained unprecedented social breadth and political attention. But who is actually involved in this social movement, what motivates people to protest and what attitudes do the participants have? Several surveys among protesters from 2019 form the starting point of the analysis of Sebastian Haunss, Moritz Sommer and 26 other authors of this book. In twelve chapters, they provide insights into decision-making and mobilization structures of local Fridays for Future groups, analyse the reactions to the protests in the media, politics and society, and examine the attitudes of young people and young adults to climate change issues. The individual chapters are written in such a way that they provide a wider audience with access to the first research results on Fridays for Future.
content.title_en: Fridays for Future – the youth against climate change : contours of the worldwide protest movement

content.text: Seeing the world with different eyes: a physicist encourages more spirituality. The author of this work is a physicist and holder of a chair for medical technology. He was awarded for his research on laser medicine. He is therefore standing with both legs in life, but he is also a believer who says: "We have to look at correlations from several perspectives to understand." He verifies this in six examples, so-called challenges: What comes first: space or time? Being or becoming? Good or evil? Chicken or egg? Creator or creation? Love or understanding? From a higher point of view, it is evident that all this is deeply connected. In addition, he addresses many questions of man, e.g. after eternity, free will, happiness and all concepts, there are clean definitions in the text and in the appendix. His goal is to "promise love and knowledge in the world without wanting to convince politically or religiously". Thus, a work has emerged that describes the world from a holistic view. It is easy to understand that the work can be recommended to all libraries (1).
content.title_en: Seeing the world with different eyes: a physicist encourages more spirituality

content.text: Fair trade? : how our consumption behaviour divides society. In seven detailed chapters, the doctoral sociologist and urban planner discusses what different types of consumption there are and she shows how and why what type of consumption is chosen and what consequences this has on society. Review (ekz): The doctoral sociologist and urban planner E. Currid-Halkett notes that in recent years a new cultural elite has emerged, which tries to distinguish itself from the rest of society through "conscious consumption" or stressed consumer renunciation. This part of society is concerned with the right decision, not the most advantageous or expensive. The author shows how and why what type of consumption is chosen and what kind of consumption is chosen and what kind of effects, even until the division that has occurred to society. Even if the descriptions refer to the USA, this inventory nevertheless reveals inconvenient results.
content.title_en: Fair trade? : how our consumption behaviour divides society

content.text: The experiment is us: our world is changing so rapidly that we are going from crisis to crisis: we have to learn to steer this enormous acceleration. Three of the crucial developments that will determine our future in the 21st century - those of the world population, those of climate change and those of digital hardware - have something in common. They are phenomena of exponential growth and so-called great acceleration. The bad news: We humans have always been hard to think of these developments. The good news: we are a learning species... Christian Stöcker's book is a panic-free and precise analysis of the great experiment humanity and a call to open up new knowledge now and to direct the Great Acceleration. (Verlag text)
content.title_en: The experiment is us : our world is changing so breathtakingly fast that we are reeling from crisis to crisis : we must learn to steer this enormous acceleration

content.text: "... that it was over with us": East European Jews in the old town of Hanover in the first decades of the 20th century. "In the dark evening, night and morning hours of the last days of October 1938, the East European Jewish families, who had been living in Hanover for decades, were "scattered out of their homes without any preparation". The police and SS forces drove the frightened and sometimes only needy-clothed people to local collection points, where they were forced to sign identification documents. Only rarely did they get permission to take some personal belongings from home. The next day, they were transported in guarded trains to no-man's country between Germany and Poland. These people stood in front of a abyss, and although they managed to deny the unimaginable truth for a short time, they had a merciless fate with the attack of the German military power in Poland." (Verlagsinformation)
content.title_en: "... that we were out" : Eastern European Jews in the old town of Hanover in the first decades of the 20th century

content.text: Dr. Sefindliche Verwaltungskommunikation in Zeiten der Digitalisierung: Konzepte - Lösungen - Fallbeispiele. Verstellliche Kommunikation in Verwaltungen, zwischen Verwaltungen und ihrem Publikum ist ein viel und lang begebendes Desiderat. To write technical texts from administrations understandable for a lay public is highly complicated. The practice of texting up to now was mainly oriented towards administrative requirements and the requirements of the jurisprudence, which are called for example in the event of contradictions against administrative decisions. This meant a main orientation of the administrative language to the language of law, which is a technical language, not a generally understandable everyday language. The digitization of the public sector offers good possibilities to use new techniques for more effective and understandable administrative communication. Representatives of various disciplines provide practical indications of a technical and content nature, convey background knowledge and focus on the likes of successful, digitally mediated administrative communication. With contributions by Prof. Dr. Ralf Daum, Dr. Heiko Fiedler-Rauer, Prof. Dr. Rudolf Fisch, Dr. Martin Hagen, Prof. Dr. Dr. Hermann Hill, Prof. Dr.
content.title_en: Understandable administrative communication in times of digitalization : Concepts - Solutions - Case studies

content.text: YouTube is used by many students as a source of information for current political content. Consequently, in political teaching, media competence should be taught, which includes social media such as YouTube. This includes, among other things, the ability to critically deal with these sources for information acquisition and political opinion formation. This volume outlines a teaching concept for dealing with current political topics using news videos from YouTubers.
content.title_en: YouTube in Political Education

content.text: Digitalisation with work and vocational training is a sustainable way of shaping the work and vocational training. What is the significance of digitalization for the education and training of the electrical, information, metal and vehicle professions? The use of digital technology leads to a major change in the activities and workflows. At the same time, the employees of these professions are particularly involved in these changes by using and manufacturing digitally innovative products. The present collection is divided into three parts. The section on resource-focused technical work is about the design of sustainable production, service and repair processes: How can digital technology be used to work resource-efficiently and efficiently? Under the heading "Smart Learning", the authors discuss the success of didactic transformation and new teaching methods for commercial-technical schools. Furthermore, the volume deals with computer science as a cross-cutting discipline of all digitization processes: How can computer education be designed in vocational education and training, although computer science is not a binding subject?
content.title_en: Making digitalization sustainable with work and vocational training

content.text: Hegel in the wired brain. The provocative script on the topicality of Hegel. - Hegel is outdated. But precisely because IBM is the point of master thinker Slavoj Žižek IBM we can better understand the present through his lens. So instead of determining what is still current in Hegel's thinking today, Žižek turns around the question: What does our present look like when we look at it with Hegel? And it turns out: We understand it much better, precisely because Hegel could not imagine it in any way. Žižek's object is the wired brain?: What will happen if the human mind can actually wire with a machine? What will this have on our subjectivity? Will we still be able to speak of the unconscious? How can we think of mind and matter then? And what will be the result of freedom? By resorting to thinkers like Johann Gottlieb Fichte, Jacques Lacan, Ray Kurzweil or Yuval Noah Harari, and by means of numerous Hollywood films, Heck's subject is well discussed in the context of Heck's and the subject of this.
content.title_en: Hegel in the wired brain

content.text: Malé: Roman. All attempts to save the Maldives from rising sea levels have failed, package tourists have sought new destinations, and most of the population has had to leave the islands. At the same time, the run-down capital Malé has become the destination of all those seeking an alternative to life in the gentrified cities of the West. And so, for the short time until it is doomed, the island will become the projection surface for emigrants, adventurers and utopians, a place between euphoria and nightmare, where new forms of solidarity are tested and people disappear undetectable. With »Malé«, Roman Ehrlich captures the complex mood of our time and weaves the stories surrounding the longings and the failure of his characters into a reflection of all the contradictions that make life at the beginning of the 21st century.
content.title_en: Malé : Roman

content.text: Overtourism. Venice, Dubrovnik or Mallorca! Many destinations suffer from overtourism - which has a massive impact on society and nature. Andreas Kagermeier takes the phenomenon to the bottom. He illuminates triggers and drivers and shows the sustainability of a destination. From securing the Active Directory to using Kali Linux, from searching for exploits to curing web servers: A team of renowned IT security experts will show you how to sustainably secure your infrastructures and how attackers are one step ahead. content.text: Hydraulics in water management: Basics and applications. Hydraulics is the science of the forces of the dormant and the moving water. In water management planning, the results of hydraulic calculations serve to dimension the corresponding structures and systems as well as to optimize the processes that run in them. This textbook conveys the knowledge for the processing of hydraulic questions and enables them to be independently calculated by means of a graphic representation. The most important hydraulic connections for studies and practice are explained by means of calculated examples and exercises with detailed solutions. For the most important technical terms relating to hydraulics, the English translations are given, and a corresponding directory is also included. This book is primarily aimed at students of civil engineering at technical universities, universities of applied sciences and similar educational institutions. In addition to the necessary knowledge during the studies, however, it can also teach practitioners:inside it is a valuable help for the short-term refresher of hydraulic contents. In the 4th edition, the book was extended to include hydraulics in water engineering. Prof. Dr.-Ing. Robert Freimann teaches the subjects of hydraulics/water engineering, settlement water management and mathematics at the University of Applied Sciences in Munich.
content.title_en: Hydraulics in the water industry : Basics and applications

content.text: What is the future of continuing education and training: the demands of today and tomorrow. The world of continuing education is changing. It is not only becoming more digital, but is also in an increasing field of tension: on the one hand, the demands for a higher implementation success and a more sustainable effect are louder. On the other hand, the framework conditions (financially and temporally) are becoming increasingly restrictive. Entrepreneurs, managers and personnel are increasingly under pressure to find new solutions. This book also aims to provide decision-makers with experience values and orientation. It highlights trends in continuing education, examines current forecasts for the future and presents best practices, e.g. in the areas of e-learning and blended learning. Several practical examples also provide inspiration for successful implementation. content.text: Remind: the fall of the Wall from a migrant and Jewish perspective. The fall of the Wall 30 years ago meant a violent break for migrant and Jewish life in East and West. While the two were united, the others were excluded. The present book wants to make marginalized perspectives on the German-German unification visible again and to recall the struggles for participation in the 1980s, drastic experiences about the turn and self-assertion against the racism of the 1990s. Thus, the volume contains stories of civil rights and asylum struggles of former guest workers, refugees in Germany and GDR, contributions about the self-interest of contract workers, then international students, about Jewish life in East and West, as well as about the struggles of Sinti and Roma in divided Germany. With contributions by Sharon Adler, Hamze Bytyci, Max Czollek, Nuray Demir, Gülriz Egilmez, Kadriye Karcı, Andrea Caroline Keppler, Paulino Miguel, Dan Thy Nguyen, Patrice Poutrus, World.
content.title_en: Interfering with Remembrance: the Fall of the Wall from a Migratory and Jewish Perspective

content.text: Anthropocene and Sustainability: A boost to the climate crisis and to sustainable action. "What exactly is the Anthropocene and how did it come about? What forces are working in it? Where does global civilization lead? Has the Anthropocene brought about the climate crisis? Is there virtually no real sustainability anymore through the Anthropocene? What can be learned from the many crises in the Anthropocene? These questions are well-readable and vividly addressed on the current state of things. On this basis, the author presents a detailed plan for the mitigation of the climate crisis that could be realized by individual states. He also presents a concept for achieving real sustainability and explains why the Anthropocene should be proclaimed as a new age of the Earth. In this context, the author also addresses the Coronavirus pandemic. The book includes the invitation to advance the "second Enlightenment". It is necessary to use the remaining window of time of a few decades to enable the Anthropocene to become future-ready."
content.title_en: Anthropocene and sustainability: ideas for climate crisis and sustainable action

content.text: The management manual requires not only technical and economic know-how, but also skill and vision. Business administration has suitable tools for this. The authors provide an understandable guide to the classification, selection and application of the most important methods for supporting business decisions. Each method is presented in a short and precise manner. At the end of each chapter, the reader can apply the method directly and use it in a useful way in the company. In this way, complex real problems can be analysed in a structured manner, evaluated and determined as best possible solution. The book applies to students of economics and related study programmes. content.text: Mathematics in economics studies: introduction – lectures – examination. Mathematics is an important methodological component in economics studies at universities, universities and vocational academies. Finally, mathematics provides models for describing economic phenomena, so that complex relationships can be clearly presented. So mathematics in economics studies is not about the operation of pure mathematics or the leading of mathematical evidence, but it is only about its application in economics to describe economic problems and to answer economic questions. This is what this book is about. To introduce mathematics in economics studies, the basics of school mathematics are summarized, which can be discussed as contents in bridge courses at the beginning of the study. Furthermore, mathematical contents are discussed in several sections, which illustrate how mathematics can be used specifically in economic science questions and problems. These sections can be taught in lectures, exercises and tutorials in a first semester. Furthermore, using sample exams, it is shown how mathematics can be completed in economics studies with an examination.
content.title_en: Mathematics in economics : Introduction – Lectures – Examination

content.text: The avant-garde of fear. The concern for the environment, the panic about the climate catastrophe and the mobilization against it have become the new common sense of the 21st century. But where assessments and appropriate ways of reacting are no longer discussed, political action soon leaves its rational basis and shirks on emotional states of excitement, which are otherwise hardly to be had in the unenchanted world. In his philosophical---mass psychological investigation Norbert Bolz analyses the conversion of ecological problem consciousness into a collective fear religion, which has replaced the fear of the Lord with the fear of man and his action. The protest movement of our day, which results from this, is not only characterized by a fatal risk and technological hostility, it also celebrates a long forgotten cult of childish superiority in relation to truth and morality. Against this background, the question arises once again: Will ›German fear‹ become an export hit or learn from the rest of world complacency?
content.title_en: The avant-garde of fear

content.text: The neurobiologist Gerald Hüther explores the art of accepting the unforeseeability of life.With his long-standing experience in the field of fear research, in this book, neurobiologist Gerald Hüther explores how this function of fear, which protects our lives, can be reconciled with our longing for a fear-free life. His surprising answer: people can also learn to ignore legitimate fears. They can even experience that a deep fear that is deeply in them can be superimposed by another fear that is pre-determined and more controllable. To achieve certain goals, we humans are able to suppress fear and strengthen IBM not only in ourselves, but also much more powerfully in others.The shyness or appeasement of fear is thus specifically used to assert their own interests and intentions. This instrumentalization of fear makes people dependent and manipulable, it deprives them of their freedom. Accordingly, Gerald Hüther does not describe how we can free ourselves from fear, but what we can do in order not to be driven by other fear groups or groups of people who are afraid.
content.title_en: Ways out of fear : about art, the unpredictability of life

It is clearly formulated which fundamental reform approaches are required, which interventions (e.g. pay for performance) are necessary and how these can be introduced into the system without negative accompanying effects. Quality 2030 also stands for a realistic time frame for the implementation of this paradigm change; the work is the basis for the necessary reforms.

content.text: Construction site Electromobility: Social science perspectives on the transformation of (auto)mobility. Our mobility is changing. Electric cars are on the rise and are being praised as a central solution for many transport problems. However, this change in drive technology is too short, because it brings with it new social and ecological problems for raw materials policy and the global value chain. But also mobility concepts around car sharing, autonomous driving and other approaches to the traffic turnaround leave many questions open. The contributors coming from different disciplines deal with these highly topical developments and provide orientation in the examination of the transformation and future of (auto)mobility.
content.title_en: Construction site Electromobility : Social science perspectives on the transformation of (auto)mobility

content.text: Autonomous systems and delict liability: fault as an instrument of adequate liability allocation?. Terms such as "Industry 4.0", "Internet of Things" and "Big Data" have recently found their way into the general spirit of the times and are synonymous with the numerous changes in human (collaborative) life and legal evaluation initiated by digitalization and automation. In particular, the use of autonomous systems that act on the basis of artificial intelligence makes the connection points of a fault accusation disappear and thus technical innovation and traditional principle of guilt act like irreconcilable children of different times. In fact, the combination of compensation obligation and carelessness only ensures a sufficient freedom gain as well as an assignment of damage according to interests and individual cases and thus corresponds to the social justice sense. In an increasingly digitized world shaded by artificial intelligence, does it still make sense to talk of lashed-based liability? Or is a switch to an alternative on marriage of freedom?
content.title_en: Autonomous systems and delict liability : fault as an instrument of adequate allocation of liability?
