content.text: Liberalism and its enemies. Does liberalism still have a future? The democracies are in crisis worldwide. Military threats and the division of society seem to have nothing to do with them. Francis Fukuyama is putting our system under stress: Are the principles of liberalism still a contemporary basis of our actions?
content.title_en: Liberalism and its enemies

content.text: The DevOps Handbook : Redesigning Teams, Tools and Infrastructures successfully. In this second and expanded edition of the original English edition, the authors present ideas and methods from the field of DevOps philosophy. The basic idea of this term, a composition of the words Development and Operation, is the acceleration of the processes, especially of software development, by increasing efficiency at as many levels as possible of a company. The authors, whose ideas are based on years of practical experience, present, among other things, with numerous case studies in the six sections of the book, the development of DevOps methods and possible entry into working with DevOps. The book focuses on the so-called "Three Ways": Flow the acceleration of product delivery to customers, feedback on the creation of more reliable work systems as well as continuous learning and experimentation. - The selected case studies allow for an effortless completion of the theories, principles and practices described by the authors in order to implement and implement DevOps initiatives in companies.
content.title_en: DevOps Manual : Redesigning teams, tools and infrastructures successfully

content.text: Queere AI : about coming out of smart machines. Common forms of discrimination as well as the reproduction of normative stereotypes are commonplace in artificial intelligence. The contributors explain ways of reducing these faulty procedures and negotiate the ambivalent relationship between queerness and AI from an interdisciplinary perspective. In parallel, they give space to a queer-feministic understanding of knowledge that is always understood as particular, ambiguous and incomplete. This opens up possibilities for dealing with AI that can transcend reductive categorizations.
content.title_en: Queere AI : for coming out of smart machines

content.text: Nuclear democracy: a history of nuclear energy in Germany. Nuclear energy was a child of the economic miracle years in the Federal Republic. In the seventies it became the centre of a public controversy in which the major questions of open societies were negotiated: the importance and legitimacy of protest, media coverage, power of large corporations, political control and the consumer citizen's claim to cheap energy. Frank Uekötter traces this story from the beginning to the present and shows how the conflict triggered learning processes in society, politics and not least the nuclear economy itself. The nuclear phase-out, which Germany will seal by shutting down the last nuclear power plants at the end of 2022, appears here as the final chapter of a cross-generational experiment that deserves attention with a view to the energy transition, but also against the background of the current crisis of democracy.
content.title_en: Nuclear Democracy: a History of Nuclear Energy in Germany

content.text: Measure by measure: the seven units that explain our world. Foot, span and elle are old length mass, but they were only valid in a small area. However, in order to have mass for the whole world it needed a stronger unification, as is the case today in the urmeter. Likewise, there is the urkilogram and the second, which are defined with the help of the speed of light at the most. The author, he is Italian and professor of experimental physics, explains here the seven units of measurement and their history. To this end, he also presents important researchers/inventors with their personal peculiarities. Time we connect with the calendar, the clock and vibrations, the kilogram with scales and the quantification of energy, the Kelvin with the thermometer and the nuclear fusion, the ampere with the current strength and the elementary charge, the mole with the periodic system and the climate change, and Candela with the interaction of the sun and water. "So a unit system was created that is really valid for all times and all people." - The work, illustrated with individual strokes, is recommended for nature readers (2).
content.title_en: Measure by measure: the seven units that explain our world

content.text: The cross: an object history of the most famous symbol from late antiquity to modern times. The Christian cross is an omnipresent and difficult to understand symbol. It is impossible to think away from the most diverse forms of art, we encounter in pictures, carvings, book paintings, jewellery objects and relics. From the beginning, its representation formed an essential part of the controversy over the right faith and the relationship between world, people and God and is still the subject of heated political debates. In this unique art and cultural history of the cross, Kathrin Müller explains how an off-side symbol of a marginal sect could become the central sign of Western culture and allows us to understand the superimposed interpretations and instrumentalizations of the cross by means of fascinating art objects.
content.title_en: The Cross : an object history of the most famous symbol from late antiquity to modern times

content.text: Running without injury : Improve running technique, prevent injuries and treat complaints correctly. Shrimp: Every time the foot hits the ground, a tremendous energy is released. The active force corresponds to about three times the body weight and a speed of more than 300 kilometers per hour. It allows every bone to vibrate and can be felt in every tendon. An exceptionally high load has to be cushioned. In addition, often a wrong technique, inappropriate equipment or insufficient training is added. No wonder, therefore, that every year more than half of the leisure runners are injured. Chiropractist Dr. Tom Michaud presents in this illustrated standard work how to analyze and correct their own running technique by means of functional tests, find the right footwear and which exercises strengthen the tendons above all. He describes in detail the 25 most common running injuries IBM from the runner knee to the achilles tendon infection IBM and shows how properly trained to run more powerfully and stay free of injury in the future.
content.title_en: Run without injury : Improve running technique, prevent injuries and treat complaints correctly

content.text: Distracted : how we lost our concentration and how we regained it. Why did we lose our ability to concentrate? To answer these and other questions, Johann Hari has been conducting research for over three years. He has talked from Silicon Valley to a favela in Rio to an office in New Zealand with the world's leading experts and professionals and exposed twelve reasons that are responsible for the loss of attention; this book shows ways to regain our focus
content.title_en: Distracted : how we lost concentration and how we regain it

content.text: Applied geography: Fields of work, activities and methods in geographical professional practice. From retail to water management, from geoinformation systems to citizen participation: The professional possibilities of geographers are more diverse than ever. New employment opportunities are constantly emerging in business companies and civil society, public administration and politics. At all spatial scale levels, applied geography makes important contributions to current societal challenges – in the face of climate change or the traffic transition, the tense housing markets or digitalisation. Around 30 teams of authors from non-university practice and university present geographical occupational fields, their activities and methods. Interviews with experts and reading tips round off the orientation aid.
content.title_en: Applied Geography : Fields of work, activities and methods in geographical professional practice

content.text: Artificial Intelligence and Nuclear Threats: Accidental Risks of Nuclear War. The increasing complexity and reduced decision times in early warning systems for nuclear threats require the use of artificial intelligence techniques (AI). In this book, AI experts cover aspects of the safety of such AI decisions as well as the risks of nuclear war by accident. The statements are supplemented by comments from policy and military experts. The nuclear deterrent strategy includes the operation of early warning systems to detect an attack with nuclear weapons. However, there may be false alarms in which nuclear attacks are reported, although there is no threat. Such false alarms are particularly dangerous in the event of international crises and may lead to nuclear war by accident. In the past, there have been several dangerous situations where only by luck there has been no such use of nuclear weapons. New technical developments and an increasing number and diversity of objects in the airspace increase the complexity of threat situations and shorten the decision-making periods. For an analysis and evaluation of alarm messages, therefore, automatic systems using methods of artificial intelligence (AI) is required to prepare for the risks of making certain early decisions, as well as the case of these decisions are automatically addressed to the next decisions.
content.title_en: Artificial intelligence and nuclear threats : risks of nuclear war by accident

content.text: Migration-related diversity in the day care center: pedagogical work with parents, children and in the team. Morgan is not concerned with knowledge transfer, but is concerned with raising the awareness of the readers of cultural differences and encouraging them to reflect on them without any evaluation. She gives a historical overview of educational concepts regarding migration-related diversity, explains integration, inclusion and intercultural openness as well as the intercultural skills of the specialists and deals in detail with the concept of culture and cooperation with parents and professionals with migrant backgrounds. The next two chapters deal with intercultural learning of children: It is shown how to communicate with materials, books, games and similar diversity competence. With detailed case studies and checklists at the end of the chapter, which help to recapitulate the read. A completely successful, very well readable volume, which is completely convincing, both in the well-founded theory part and in the helpful case examples.
content.title_en: Migration-related diversity in the day care center : pedagogical work with parents, children and in the team

content.text: Health Economics : Structures - Methods - Practical Examples. In the 9th edition the work has been extensively revised and updated and supplemented by a new chapter on "Health Insurance". The established textbook provides a well-established overview of the field of health economics. It explains the theoretical foundations of market and competition and the problematic transferability to the health sector. The focus is on monetary and non-monetary incentives in statutory health insurance, outpatient and inpatient care and the pharmaceutical market. As examples of alternative financing and care systems, the health systems of the USA, England and the Netherlands are discussed.
content.title_en: Health Economics : Structures - Methods - Practical Examples

content.text: Media technology: Basic knowledge, concepts, procedures, applications. The textbook offers students of media technology and related study programmes a direct introduction to communication technology as the basis of media technology. It deals with the diverse possibilities of the transmission and storage of audio and video signals, i.e. of sound and image. The book deals with the methods for transmission and storage of messages as well as the implemented systems and thus contrasts the theoretical approach of practice. Furthermore, the functionalities and connections are described in detail and important technical terms are explained in detail. Numerous examples and exercises serve for better understanding and illustrate the learning material. From the content: signals and level; OSI layer model; transmission; storage; devices and components; interfaces and protocols; networks; procedures; applications: radio, television, telephony, data networks, Internet The second edition has been completely revised, brought to the latest state of the art and extended to include chapters on audiovision/data in the media area as well as applications. Ulrich Freyer was Technical Director at the Landesanstalt für Medien in Düsseldorf. He is an analyst for media technology, holds teaching events and is the author of numerous specialist books for radio technology.
content.title_en: Media technology : basic knowledge, concepts, procedures, applications

content.text: Power electronics for Bachelors: Basics and practical applications. Prof. Dr.-Ing. Uwe Probst teaches power electronics and drive technology at the Department of Electrical and Information Technology at the Technical University of Mittelhessen. This textbook for students of electrical engineering introduces the field of power electronics with its components and control procedures. It systematically provides the basic structure and functioning of modern power semiconductor components. Based on the grid-guided rectifier circuits with diodes and thyristors, the terms and mathematical procedures are introduced, with which power electronic circuits can be described and calculated. Based on this, the circuits, which form the basis of today's power supplies and drive drivers using modern switching transistors, are explained. Online, for almost all basic circuits discussed in the book, interactive simulation programs are found, with which the functioning of the circuits can be illustrated by animations and the time flows of currents and voltages are represented. They are important for the circuit-technical understanding and are very helpful for the solution of the exercise tasks. Examples, numerous illustrations and exercise tasks with solution suggestions complement the teaching material and enable an in-depth examination of power electronics.
content.title_en: Power electronics for Bachelors : Basics and practical applications

content.text: Introduction to wind energy technology. Wind energy is an important renewable energy source in power generation. Its importance will increase further in view of current developments. With this textbook you will get to know the state of the art and gain an overview of the diverse aspects of this renewable energy form: - History and international development of wind energy - The wind – from theory to practice - Aerodynamics, leaf design - Rotor blade structure, power harness, tower and foundation - Power electronics generator systems - Control and control of wind energy systems - Grid integration, Offshore wind energy The knowledge is easily conveyed and strengthened by examples and exercises. In the 3rd revised edition the chapter on the basics of wind power use was completely redesigned. With the six steps location identification, recording of wind climate, data analysis, spatial exploration, selection of wind energy plant and evaluation of energy yield, the most important planning aspects of wind park development are shown. All other chapters have been thoroughly revised and the current standards adapted. This textbook supports you in your studies and in professional training during the entry into wind energy technology.
content.title_en: Introduction to wind energy technology

content.text: Handbook on sustainability in vocational education and training: political education as a design task. Strengthening political learning through sustainability in vocational education and training: How can one tap into the guiding idea of sustainable development in vocational education and training and what is the contribution of political education? In this handbook, experts: from science, education practice, companies, politics, civil society and NGOs will follow up these questions on a theoretical level and with practical tips. All relevant protagonists come together:in vocational education and training and develop a common perspective on the challenge of sustainability. The handbook is aimed at company training staff, vocational school teachers:inside, sustainability representatives, apprentices, students and all interested parties.
content.title_en: Handbook on sustainability in vocational education and training: political education as a design task

content.text: Hydrogen technology: tasks and solutions. The task and solution book about the most common element in the world The energy supply, transport and industry of tomorrow require forward-looking technologies that enable an affordable storage of large amounts of renewable electricity, a greenhouse gas-free transport as well as sustainable industrial and chemical processes. The use of hydrogen promises the solution of many related questions. In addition to the Hydrogentechnik plant - basics, systems, application, economy, this book contains numerous exercise tasks with detailed described solutions. With this unique collection of exercise tasks you gain as an incoming engineer or technician the necessary expertise for the calculation of hydrogen-specific chemical-physical quantities and processes as well as economic framework data for hydrogen use. Since 2002 Professor in the department of Energy, Buildings, Environment at the University of Applied Sciences Münster, Abt. Steinfurt, there from 2011 to 2018 Dean in the department. From 1998 to 2002 in the gas saving of the gas and electricity grid operator EWE AG in Oldenburg in the field of gas procurement, construction and operation of gas storage and gas expansion plants. From 1982 to 1998 Engineering activities at the remote gas supplier Thyssen in Duisburg GmbH in the planning and plant of the company of the company Baugas GmbH in Duisburg.
content.title_en: Hydrogen technology : Tasks and solutions

content.text: Drivers of the authoritarian: Paths of developments at the beginning of the 21st century. Count crises among the special drivers of authoritarian developments and extreme right-wing activities in the young 21st century? To answer this question, this collection offers broad theoretical and empirical analyses. The contributions link to longer-term economic, political and social developments, but also focus on the Covid-19 crisis. They deal with the dangers of open society and liberal democracy, the central focus is on right-wing authoritarian and right-wing extremist movements and parties.
content.title_en: Drivers of the Authoritarian : Paths of Developments at the beginning of the 21st Century

content.text: Between the punishment of God and conspiracy theories: epidemics from antiquity to the present have been unusually competitive in Germany since 2020. Conspiracy theoretic and "alternative-theological" interpretations as well as negations of the Corona pandemic; in the "liberal milieu", which is convinced of the evidence of medical-scientific expertise, they provide considerable irritation. Such different perceptions are not new in times of epidemics. This collection first illuminates such interpretational conflicts in an interdisciplinary, epoch-wide perspective; the contributions ask under which conditions what interpretations of resonance and reception found, how this changed over time and how far this change correlates or collides with historical master narratives (modernization, secularization, rationalization)
content.title_en: Between God's Punishment and Conspiracy Theory : Interpretation Competitions in Epidemics from Ancient to Present

content.text: Coal Age: a global and knowledge history (1500-1900). In view of limited resources and ecological crises, the energy transition today aims at the decarbonization of economy and society, a new era in which coal no longer plays a role. This noble intention clearly demonstrates that there must have been an era in which coal was extremely important for mankind: the "coal age". Helge Wendt describes it as a global knowledge story about the material, its extraction, storage and use, connected with political questions and social structures. Starting in early modern Europe, his book sheds light on questions that were discussed in Latin America as well as in Asia and Africa of the late 19th century. Especially in the colonies of European states - so Wendt's innovative approach - it was evident how knowledge and power, practice and problem solving, fossil energy transition and economy interacted in large and small spatial constellations.
content.title_en: Coal Age : a history of global and knowledge (150-1900)

content.text: Modern lighting optics in practice: concepts, design, simulation, production with free-form optics. Light and lighting technology is everywhere: on the road in street lights and automotive headlights, in interiors and in the targeted illumination of a measuring field for sensors. Everywhere, a desired light distribution is to be generated as efficiently as possible. Knowledge of modern light sources such as LEDs and the design of suitable (free-form) optics are therefore becoming increasingly important. The book introduces the modern lighting optics: Readers: learn what sizes and light sources are important and how free-form optics can be designed, used and manufactured in lighting technology. From the content: - light technology bases - light generation - light steering - lighting-soptical applications - production of lighting optics. Examples and a multitude of exercises help to successfully apply the acquired knowledge in lighting projects.

content.text: Hidden spaces, hidden biographies: gay architects from the 18th to the 20th century. Homosexuality is still a taboo topic in architectural history. content.text: The collection of the University Library in Helmstedt, the collection of the University Library, is a virtual reconstruction of the collection of the University Library, its equipment, the collection of objects and historical documents in the library archive. The name of the unique Renaissance building reminds us of Duke Julius, founder of the University and the Hofbibliothek in Wolfenbüttel. Newly discovered architectural drawings by Georg Christoph Sturm show that the hall library, which was established in 1759, replaced older library rooms. Its spatial concepts were archived together with handwritten inventories, library regulations, catalogues and correspondence. The analysis of the documents on the knowledge organization is linked in this study with results on the materiality and use history of historical manuscripts and printed works - thus social practices are given sharper contours. When the University of Helmstedt was closed in 1810, the hall library contained about 24,000 books from estates or secularized monasteries. In addition, there were copies of evidence or purchases at auctions.
content.title_en: Scholar culture and collection practice : Architecture, actors and knowledge organization in the University Library Helmstedt (1576-1810)

content.text: The pioneer of the digital era: the history of ZEISS lithography optics. Stephan Paetrow was born in Jena in 1978 and studied Modern History, Philosophy and English Literature before specializing in technology and economic history.As co-founder of the agency timefab (Leipzig/Berlin) he has since 2013 supported a large number of medium-sized and large companies in transforming a often complex historical tradition of files and contemporary witnesses interviews into exciting stories and in opening up the company history for a wider audience.In the mid-1960s, a small team at ZEISS Oberkochen developed the first lenses for the exposure of integrated circuits, the so-called lithography optics. At that time, ZEISS was able to explore the limits of the feasible and to redefine them. Since then, the ZEISS lithography optics has played a decisive role in enabling ever-increasing computing performance in ever smaller devices. This development is also called Moore's Law. Today, ZEISS is the only company worldwide to explore the optics for the latest generation, the so-called EUV lithography, because only the mobile technology can be used to determine the boundaries of our digital devices.
content.title_en: Pioneers of the digital era : the history of ZEISS lithography optics

content.text: While sustainability is to become the overarching guideline for social trade, its means and paths are not clearly clear. From its holistic understanding sustainability must combine technical, social, economic, ecological and ethical strategies, between which there are complex interactions and often enough also conflicting objectives and priorities. In no other area can these relationships be better understood, presented and influenced than in the building sector. "Better – Less – Anders Bauen" takes up two areas of sustainability in each volume, whose interactions are particularly important and at the same time particularly well to be grasped. After introductory overviews, established methods, current developments and acute conflict fields are described, analysed and presented in detail on international case studies. This happens along with the sustainability criteria of efficiency ("better"), suffificiency ("less") and consistency ("others"). The first volume presents concepts, methods and examples of circulars in the building sector and in the economy. Urban mining and circular construction are different ways of dealing with the challenges in architecture and urban planning.

content.text: The concept of artificial intelligence -- Practical limits -- Theoretical limits -- Conceptual limits -- Prospects for hybrid AI. Artificial intelligence is a key technology that involves great expectations in both science and industry. This book discusses both the perspectives and limits of this technology. In an early phase, AI's expert systems were the focus of attention, where rules-based knowledge was processed with the help of symbolic data processing. As a result, it is argued above all for a hybrid AI that can bring the potential of both approaches to the development of scientific science. The authors Klaus Mainzer teaches as emeritus of excellence at the Technical University of Munich, as senior professor at the Carl von Weizsäcker-Center at the University of Tübingen. content.text: Diversity-sensitive teacher formation: theoretical and practical explorations. In this context, everyday theories and evaluation habits, established practices, but also institutional sorting mechanisms play a special role for the continuous remobilization of persistent forces in the system. From the relevant "abbreviations" that take actors between professional knowledge, governance and practice in everyday life, specific blockades of overdue renewals and perspective changes in and on the system arise. The volume addresses these syndromes by opening innovative perspectives on diversity sensitivity as a significant moment for the teacher training of the first and second phases. content.text: Investments: Digital Asset Management – Sustainable Portfolio Management – Alternative Investments. content.text: Loneliness and the use of the term "loneliness" is a phenomenon that is common in clinical life, even if it is not always reported spontaneously by patients. The aversive feeling of loneliness occurs when our basic human need for social relationships is not sufficiently satisfied. It is evident in those who have too few or insufficiently satisfying contacts. It is important to distinguish between temporary, situative and persistent loneliness. Because, although any kind of loneliness is painful, loneliness is not always dysfunctional. While temporary and situative loneliness is usually attributed to adaptive function, persistent loneliness is associated with high suffering pressure and a variety of mental and somatic complaints. Moreover, feelings of loneliness play a central role in the development and/or maintenance of various mental disorders. The band sensitizes professionals for the topic of the topic of "loneliness" and is intended to support the current phenomenon and to describe the context of the phenomenon.
content.title_en: Loneliness

content.text: Handbook Political Ecology: Theories, conflicts, concepts, methods. Global crises such as climate change and the Corona pandemic make political ecology an indispensable research field of the future. The contributors to the first German-language handbook on the topic present the relevant theories and, by means of concrete conflicts and struggles, show the relevance and added value of a political-ecological approach. They explain the central concepts that are important for the analysis, critique and transformation of social natural relations and present fruitful methods and working methods for political ecology.
content.title_en: Handbook Political Ecology : Theories, Conflicts, Terms, Methods

content.text: Radicalization narratives online: perspectives and lessons from science and prevention. Radicalization towards extremist milieus has also been taking place online for several years. While contact with extremist actors continues to be offline, social media plays an increasingly important role in radicalization processes. In YouTube videos and other social media platforms, young people are actively addressed by extremist actors and guided to extremist content. The investigation and disclosure of radicalization narratives online is therefore an important task for science and prevention. In the efforts to de-radicalize or inhibit or prevent radicalization, counternarratives or alternative narratives can also play a role. Counternarratives try to deconstruct radicalization narratives, to disclose false connections and contradictions and to identify alternative or legal-state, democratic interpretations of existing problems. These counternarratives can be made available online and used in youth work for prevention. The collection volume addresses this issue by bringing together important insights from science and prevention. The publisher Dr. Sybille is a researcher for crime policy, a researcher for politics and a researcher for politics and a researcher for politics.
content.title_en: Radicalization narratives online : Perspectives and lessons from science and prevention

content.text: Risk Democracy : Chemnitz between the radical right and the European Capital of Culture. The radical right-wing riots in Chemnitz in 2018 raise fundamental democratic theoretic questions: What dangers are there of right-wing? How does an entire city become a political risk area? And what does the presence of risky politicization and depoliticization mean for our democracy? The authors illustrate along ethnographical ramifications how an apolitical centre of radical right-wings repeatedly leaves the public space. The extreme right-wings spread in this vacuum and claim democratic fundamental rights for themselves in order to abolish them at the same time. As the cultural capital of 2025, Chemnitz must prove itself in dealing with this democratic risk.

content.text: Mathematical modelling in life sciences. Deep and broad insights in life sciences are only available with mathematics. In this book you will learn how classical and current mathematical models describe processes in the animated nature. Experience how simple considerations lead to mathematical models that fundamentally reshape our understanding of the phenomena in biology and medicine, and how on this basis completely new insights and progress become possible. The journey begins with questions about the spread of epidemics and vaccination strategies and leads among others on water health, one- or more-dimensional population dynamics and pharmacokinetic processes up to optimal medications in diseases. Each chapter draws on as much mathematics as you need to answer the research questions. The clear design and use of colors in the text and in the numerous illustrations facilitate reading and understanding. Task series encourage you to own activity and research. The authors Alexander Caspar is a senior scientist at ETH Zurich. He finds methods there for a low-scrowded and inviting mediation of mathematics. Norbert Hungerbühler works as a professor at ETH Zurich.
content.title_en: Mathematical Modeling in Life Sciences

content.text: More-than-human geography has established itself as an important research field in Anglo-Saxon and has gained increasing importance in German-speaking geography in recent years. The decentralization of human beings is being promoted conceptually by various approaches such as phenomenology, pragmatism, the actor-network theory, assemblage, affect and multi-representational theories, as well as by practice-theoretical, performative and visceral approaches. Despite this great heterogeneity, the multi-human geography unites that they understand humans as part of a larger overall context, approach the world from more than strictly rationally tangible experiential and meaning dimensions and thus systematically explore physical, affective, emotional and sensory practices, transactions and intra-actions. Authors introduce themselves into the development lines, broad lines and key concepts of the complex debate, thus contributing to the systematic opening of German-speaking and interested neighbouring disciplines.
content.title_en: Multi-human geography: key concepts, relationships and methodologies

content.text: Digital Turn and Historical Education Research : Inventory and Research Perspectives. content.text: Fluctuation in the German labour market: dynamics of personnel movements and their factors influencing them. Labor turnover in Germany is almost constant over time, but it is falling slightly in economic times such as the financial and economic crisis and the Corona pandemic. This is partly due to the fact that the personnel turnover is largely determined by employee-side dismissals, which follow pro-cyclical economic developments. While the economic perspective shows the function of personnel movements for a better allocation of resources, a high turnover at the company level is often seen as an expression of a low employee retention. However, only a few companies (2016 was around 9 percent) are actually concerned about the extent of their fluctuations in the coming years. Rather, personnel changes and employment development are strongly influenced by the operational environment such as competitive pressure and the respective personnel policy strategy. In contrast, the diversity of the workforce plays a more subordinate role in terms of gender, age distribution and the cultural background of employees for the dynamics of personnel movements. Given increasing skill shortages in connection with the structural changes in the ecological and digital factors, the fluctuation of the workforce could gain even more significance as a function of the influence of the German labour market.
content.title_en: Fluctuation in the German labour market: dynamics of personnel movements and their factors

content.text: The Corona crisis is the first pandemic of digital late modernism. Home office and home schooling, but also the expansion of an online range of neighbourhood aid and solidarity-providing hashtags are among the time-tested testimonies of digital crisis communication. At the same time, a global apparatus of regulation has been formed: drones for controlling quarantine, pandemic apps, thermal imaging cameras and the monitoring of individual urban districts make it clear how different societies are facing the crisis and what role technologies play in this process. The contributors reflect the situation interdisciplinaryly from the perspectives of sociology, ethics and IT.
content.title_en: Crisis technologies: the Covid-19 pandemic as a catalyst for new forms of networking

content.text: While climate research has long been considered a purely scientific undertaking, it has been increasingly used in the social sciences since the 2010s. Popularization in and outside science has not only led to new problem references, but also produced a growing complexity: there has been a need to explore disciplinary starting points, interdisciplinary connections and transdisciplinary exchange opportunities. The contributors of the volume review key social science climate research works and thus provide initial access to and orientation in the research field.
content.title_en: Key works of social science climate research

content.text: Uncertainties, but certainly! : from the competent handling of inaccurate data. All beginnings are uncertain -- On a date with data -- Correct, precise and accurate -- From appointments, population growth and nitrogen dioxide -- Uncertainty -- Knowledge creates uncertainties -- discretion of uncertainties -- Latte ripped? Compare measurement results -- Uncertainties are fertile and continue to thrive -- Cum grano salis. This book provides a general introduction to the handling of uncertainties of data and sensitises to not accept data unreflected as correct. It alerts readers to how uncertainties in data can occur in many everyday situations and be highly relevant, e.g. to make personal decisions, to participate in political elections and to assess scientific studies. Spipped with numerous examples from natural science, society and everyday life, the book conveys the necessary basic knowledge without much formulas and mathematical knowledge. It enables readers to look for uncertainties in everyday life, to identify them, to question them and to evaluate them by using the science of science.

content.text: A pandemic is changing the world: genetic engineering, data protection and an ethical dilemma. Crises are the drivers of scientific innovations - the Coronapandemic has made such an inventive spirit more necessary than ever. Genetic-produced vaccines and digital contact tracking have proved to be the most effective weapon in the fight against the virus. However, this combination of genetic engineering and digitalization also brings with it a number of ethical problems: How do big data and data protection come together? What can and can genetic engineering do? The book discuss these and other questions with vivid examples and shows the backgrounds of technology and medical history. The book is an exciting reading for all those who want to classify and understand the effects of the pandemic.
content.title_en: A Pandemic Changes the World : Genetic Engineering, Data Protection and an Ethical Dilemma

content.text: Introduce human-robot cooperation successfully: Basics, guidelines, applications. This book conveys in a vivid and pragmatic way all the necessary knowledge and necessary to introduce human-robot cooperation (HRC) and cobots legally in everyday business. A consistent guide with guidance aids! The author Prof. Dr. Markus Glück is Professor of Automation and Robotics at the Aalen University of Applied Sciences, Faculty of Optics and Mechatronics. Vice-President of EUnited Robotics. Specialities: Automation and Robotics, Image Processing, Digitalization of Production, Human-roboter Cooperation. Before that, he was Chief Innovation Officer at SCHUNK and Managing Director of Technology Centrum Westbayern GmbH at the University of Augsburg.

At the same time, understanding thermodynamics is often complicated by the fact that it is described by complex mathematics. content.text: Inequal rural spaces: contradictions, concepts and perspectives. Rural spaces have been "in" for some time now: in times of the Covid-19 pandemic, they are considered to be supposedly safer places, investors discover the country as a profitable business field and owners increasingly benefit from price increases of land. On the other hand, rural areas develop strongly: in prosperous and abandoned regions. Especially in peripheral regions, right-wing populist parties gain above average votes. The contributors of the volume provide an inventory of research on rural inequalities and offer starting points for critical land research as well as for progressive perspectives for rural spaces.
content.title_en: Inequal rural areas : contradictions, concepts and perspectives

content.text: History and theory of interior design: from modernism to today. Those who provide interior design with a social claim inevitably diagnose human coexistence. Unlike the fixed, difficult-to-change structures of our cities and houses, the design factors of interiors are more changeable. Interior design thus has the ability to react to social and cultural changes earlier than architecture can afford. The understanding of space inspires almost all scientific disciplines, each of which has found a definition for it. In this book Natascha Meuser, Professor of Interior Planning at the University of Anhalt in Dessau, tells her very personal history of spatial art and puts source texts on the theory of interior design in a historical context.
content.title_en: History and Theory of Interior Design : from Modernism to the Present

content.text: Romanische Dorfkirchen in der Region Braunschweig. "The region Braunschweig is characterized by a high density of smaller village churches, which date back to medieval foundation buildings. Over the centuries the churches have been changed in structural terms. However, in the sacral buildings, extensive remains of the Romanesque original buildings are preserved to this day. The book traces these traces. Based on plans and numerous photos, the phenomena associated with the architectural development of the village churches are explained on twelve selected examples of the region. A well-founded introduction also illuminates the topic from an architectural, social and regional historical perspective." (Verlagsinformation)
content.title_en: Romanic village churches in the region of Braunschweig

content.text: Source Book contemporary offices : architecture and interiors of exemplary workplaces. Office buildings are among the most demanding and diverse tasks of contemporary architecture. Companies and authorities have long recognized the importance of the working environment for efficiency, health and even creativity of their employees. The right office stimulates, simplifies communication, creates a working and ultimately a living environment that motivates. The designers of workplaces must take all this into account. Thus their task has long since grown beyond the creation of work-right-compliant desk arrangements and conference room optimizations. It is important to create situations in which the most valuable operational capacity can develop the employees. This volume presents 60 office buildings and interiors of the past years in word and image with numerous plans. In addition to large buildings, small offices and remodelings are also shown, which are equally exemplary. Ecological innovative constructions are addressed; as well as the arrangement of work sequences or the atmosphere through interior design. The book shows classic single, group or large-scale offices, but also the newly animated idea of the open office landscape or the still young new work worlds of business non-lotion or work-lotioners.
content.title_en: Source Book Contemporary offices : Architecture and interiors of exemplary workplaces

content.text: What a coincidence! : About unpredictability, complexity and the essence of time. How does chance come into our world? And why is so much unpredictable? Understandable, exciting and amusingly telling us, the author takes us into the world of chemistry, quantum physics and biology. Strewing astronomy and philosophy, we witness a rewarding journey of discovery. In doing so, he develops a completely new view of chance on the basis of natural laws. Here, the omnipresent non-equivalence plays an extremely decisive role, because it creates the complex structures in our world. Finally, he presents on this basis an equally simple and bribery hypothesis about the nature of the time. This book of matter provides a deep insight into the fascination of research, into the tormenting search for basic understanding and the struggle for scientific insight. The author Dr. Bernhard Weßling is a chemist and entrepreneur. He has mainly pursued chemical product and process development and also realized basic innovations since his professional life.

content.text: Digital Capital in Use : an Ethnography on the Transformation of Digital Practices in Art Education. For some time now, the education at art universities has been increasingly discussing questions about the relationship between digital and analogue practices, between technical know-how and artistic idea, as well as between university offerings and individual orientations for action. Using theses in art, design and art mediation, the authors investigate which digital practices students use, on which skills and knowledge they use and how their use is evaluated. content.text: Africa is not a country. More than 1.4 billion people, 54 countries, over 2000 languages, have been reduced to simple stories for decades: hunger, safaris, perhaps brutal dictatorships. An entire continent is simplified to horror, with disastrous consequences ... "Africa is not a country" corrects the global distortion of perception. It is the narrative manifesto against stupidity, laziness and simplicity in dealing with the multifaceted African continent. And an absolutely gorgeous intervention
content.title_en: Africa is not a country

content.text: The colonialized brain and the paths of revolt. The modern understanding of brain functions and mental illnesses is deeply influenced by the projection of colonial hierarchies on the brain: the supervision of the supposedly primitive drives and lusts is supposed to be attributed to higher brain centers and functions. Psychic diseases have long been understood as a loss of this sovereign control and the affected people were delivered power techniques that were reimported from the colonies. Andreas Heinz reconstructs the history of revolts against these racist constructions as well as counter-movements. Can traces of the internalized hierarchies of the colonialized brain still be found in current forms of careful self-discipline?
content.title_en: The Colonial Brain and the Ways of Revolt

content.text: On the way to the Cyberpolis: new forms of community, self and education. The social, cultural and political process of digitalization has made new forms of community and education conceivable, which were decisively shaped by three scenes: the cybernetic artistic backgrounds of PC culture as the basis of Silicon Valley, the popularization of the Internet in the 1990s and current developments, which are taken under the concept of digital nomadism. Martin Donner and Heidrun Allert ask against the background of the associated shifts in community understandings about practical design possibilities.
content.title_en: Towards Cyberpolis: new forms of community, self and education

content.text: Digital teaching has led to profound changes at many levels in the field of infrastructure, methodology and didactics at universities. In the past two years, digital teaching concepts have been developed, implemented in practice and much of what had been only partially integrated into teaching has become increasingly established due to the special external circumstances. In 2003, the GMW conference was already devoted to the topic of "sustainability", which shows that this topic has long shaped the media didactic discussion. Against this background, the contributions of the GMW conference 2022 address the question of whether and how, under the impression of the Pandemic, new perspectives for the sustainability of the efforts to renew education with digital media have emerged in recent years. In particular, topics such as quality in teaching, personalized teaching concepts, including educational technologies and university development are being addressed in the context of digitalization.
content.title_en: Making digital teaching sustainable

content.text: Hydraulics and pneumatics: Basics and exercises - applications and simulation. content.text: Controlling - current developments and challenges: digitalization, sustainability and special aspects. Challenges of digitalization -- sustainability and corporate social responsibility -- family and small and medium-sized enterprises. content.text: The oldest church in the world: Christian preaching places, meeting rooms and churches before Constantine. Even before Constantine there were Christian meeting places and church buildings. Using literary and archaeological sources Reiner Sörries tries to reconstruct the largely unknown church building in the first three Christian centuries.Although early Christian church construction is one of the central themes of Christian archaeology, the question of which building can actually be considered as "the oldest church in the world" has been given little attention to the churches before Constantine - following the assumption that there can only be churches in the actual sense after the constant change.The author traces the processual development of early Christian cult sites: a path from useful, temporarily used rooms over permanent worship buildings to the first, independent church buildings, which undoubtedly existed before Constantine.
content.title_en: The oldest church in the world: Christian preaching places, meeting rooms and churches before Constantine

content.text: Traces of digital articulations: interdisciplinary approaches to social media as a cultural educational space. Almost daily we post or like something on Twitter, Facebook or Instagram.As places of direct communication and interaction, social media has long since become platforms for the negotiation and dissemination of cultural expressions of our everyday life. However, when we look at them closely, the complex processes of media-mediated interactions and articulations of actors who jointly realize cultural educational spaces and processes within the framework of informal, digital everyday practices are eluded from easy access. Starting from the interdependence of technology, aisthesis and articulation, the contributors of the volume unfold from different disciplinary perspectives the attempt to (re)read traces of cultural educational and transformation processes in social media.
content.title_en: Traces of digital articulations : interdisciplinary approaches to social media as a cultural educational space

content.text: The fundamental principles of climate protection law are fundamental to the existence of the entire human civilization and form a complex multi-level law. The fundamental principles of climate protection law follow a corresponding global approach. As already in the successful preliminary edition, both the international, European and national legal levels are presented and placed in relation to each other. This creates a comprehensive picture of the individual questions in this area of law that is crucial for the future of our planet. Important text passages are visually highlighted. In addition, the core sentences are again pointed out for the recapitulation and for the quick overview at the end of each chapter. In order to meet the dynamics of the matter, users of the work have access to a digital add-on that provides further information on current developments. In addition, instructive multiple choice questions, current regulatory texts and important court decisions in the full text are included.
content.title_en: Broad lines of climate protection legislation

content.text: Crowdfunding in sport: Professional funding for clubs and individual athletes. Crowdfunding is the most active of all forms of funding and funding for sports clubs, sports organisations and sportsmen. The innovative practical book by Torsten Lührs and Francesca Poschen shows how you successfully implement sports projects with crowdfunding and sustainably develop your club with tailor-made campaigns. - Principles of crowdfunding, advantages and sports-specific features - projects, project starters and supporters, typical motifs and constellations in sport - planning and implementation of a campaign – from the project team to the communication plan to the correct timing Whether jerseys for the youth team, artificial grass courts, new floodlight or World Cup participation: 15 current case studies of successful sports crowdfunding campaigns prove impressively how you can start out passionately and professionally in the further development of your club, including funding and promotion issues.

content.text: Climate protection and violence: When activists make themselves punishable and how we really save the world. "And are you unwillingly" - The dilemma of climate protectionists -- Where does violence begin? -- Is violence allowed to protect the climate? -- Is violence suitable and necessary to protect the climate? -- Legal and better than violence – Three fresh strategies. Climate protectionists are sounding alarm: Instead of limiting global warming to a maximum of 1.5 degrees, the world is currently on a 2.7-degree path. What now? Does violence only help now? In this essential, Jochen Theurer analyses the current legal situation and shows how the 1.5-degree goal can be better achieved with the help of three fresh strategies – in time, non-violent and legal. The content The dilemma of climate protectionists Where does violence begin? Is violence allowed to protect the climate? Is violence suitable and necessary for protecting the climate? Three fresh strategies for effective climate protection The target groups All who actively want to contribute to limiting global warming to a maximum of 1.5 degrees have been employed in the law.
content.title_en: Climate protection and violence: When activists make themselves punishable and how we really save the world

content.text: The East: a West German invention. "The East has no future as long as it is understood as a source." What does it mean to be imposed on an East identity? An identity that is held responsible for the growing social division? The attributes such as populism, lack of understanding of democracy, racism, conspiracy myths and poverty are attributed? Dirk Oschmann shows in his book that the West still defines itself as a norm over thirty years after the fall of the Wall and the East as a deviation. Our media, politics, economy and science are dominated by West German perspectives. "The East appears as an ulcer on the body of the West," writes Germanist Dirk Oschmann. The former GDR is today associated with all the problems of the country: populism, racism, poverty. Responsible for these attributions: above all West German, which still dominates media and politics. A rage speech, written with sharp pen (place 9 of the Sachbuch Best List for April 2023).
content.title_en: The East: a West German invention

content.text: Java for Dummies. You want to get into Java or expand your knowledge? "Java for Dummies" is also a textbook and indispensable reference work for all Java programmers. Basic knowledge for object-oriented programming is taught just as well as the principle of reusability of program modules. You also learn when variables should be declared within or outside of methods, where the limits of arrays lie and how code is made crashproof with exceptions. This edition of "Java for Dummies" takes into account the innovations of the Java 17 version.
content.title_en: Java for Dummies

content.text: The architecture of the real: plea against the flood of images in the architectural culture. In contemporary culture, the inflationary spread of the pictorial has led to an implosion of content. That is why Bernhard Denkinger pleads for an architecture that does not originate from the pictorial. His study focuses on two different approaches to realistic currents of modernity: the early functionalists, team ten or the populists of the 1960s defined architecture over social, later tendencies such as critical regionalism or Dirty Realism emphasized the sensual experience. New approaches, on the other hand, refer to the factual. An innovative approach to the guidelines of building practice opens up new resources here.
content.title_en: The architecture of the real: plea against the flood of images in the building culture

content.text: The role of Germany in the context of the energy transition: An ethical investigation of normative conflicts of objectives, with particular regard to the lignite phase-out. How can necessary climate protection measures such as the lignite phase-out be implemented in such a way that no moral violations of rights arise both at local and at the general level of society? To answer this question, it is necessary to analyse precisely the threat of normative conflicts of objectives. This task is addressed in this work. Using the example of the lignite phase-out in the Rhine region, target conflicts with regard to the energy policy goal triangle, on emerging social hardships and on consequences such as a strengthening of right-wing populist parties are investigated. On the basis of this, possible solutions are outlined. The author Friederike Henke has completed her doctorate at the Ruhr University in Bochum at the Institute for Philosophy in the field of applied ethics. Her research focuses on climate and energy ethics. In her dissertation, she has worked on the question of the lignite exit in the Rhine district.
content.title_en: The role of Germany in the context of the energy transition: an ethical investigation of normative conflicts of interest, with particular regard to the lignite phase-out

content.text: 21.1 : a brief history of the present. Climate change and war, populism and cultural struggles, migration and pandemic - global crises are increasing and superimposing themselves as never before. Andreas Rödder presents with "21.1" the long awaited update of his historical crash course due to the basic problems of our time. How did the central conflict constellations of the present actually arise? And what options and instruments do we have to meet them? The renowned contemporary historian, Professor of Contemporary History at the University of Mainz, dissects in his book the manifold crises that challenge and threaten us, and surprises readers with unusual perspectives and new insights.
content.title_en: 21.1 : a brief history of the present

content.text: The task book is specifically tailored to the students of mechanical engineering and is intended to help them take the "fear" of the basic subject Thermodynamics to make the exam a success. content.text: Euregio Mobility in vocational education and training: go across the border & think. How can vocational education and training be developed and developed in border regions of Europe? Using the example of six vocational schools in the Euregio Rhein-Waal, the authors report:Inside on potentials and challenges of cross-border vocational education and training. The researchers accompanied exchanges in three tandem partnerships from one vocational school in Germany and the Netherlands (ROC). Part of the project were the courses of retail, educators and horticulture. The project report focuses on the structure of tandem partnerships, which ensures low-shaft participation, as well as the exchange of teachers. The use of digital tools is also analysed with a view to the Covid-19 pademie. Overall, the publication provides new perspectives on the possibilities of cross-border educational projects and arguments for a wide range of mobility, with which teachers and learners can act as multipliers in the European area.
content.title_en: Euregio Mobility in vocational education and training: go across the border & think

content.text: In the future: from dignity and justice and the Arab Spring: essays from the Middle East and North Africa. From Tunisia to Bahrain: 2011 marked a social-political gap in the Middle East and North Africa. With incredible courage, millions of women and men rose up against rulers whose power was based on violence and foreign-political convenience. But socio-economic demands were not the first in any of the uprisings. The contributors put the core of the protests at the centre: the demand for dignity! They follow the people, revolutions and developments and outline the experience and the still existing hopes of the populations in the context of the Arab Spring
content.title_en: In the future: Smell of dignity and justice and the Arab Spring : Essays from the Middle East and North Africa

content.text: Digital technology for outpatient care and therapy: challenges, solutions, applications and research perspectives. Every year 270,000 people suffer a stroke in Germany. In many cases, the affected persons can return home and continue their lives, but they need outpatient care and therapy measures. Especially in rural regions, this brings with it considerable challenges, which face new technologies and digitalization. The contributors of the volume discuss first results of the project "YourHouse 4.0 Oberpfalz" from an interdisciplinary perspective, in which the possibility of using telepresence robots to support outpatient care and therapy measures is investigated.
content.title_en: Digital technology for outpatient care and therapy: challenges, solutions, applications and research perspectives

content.text: Optimization of the self : Concepts, representations and practices. Klappentext: From gyms to sleep apps to healing stones - the pursuit of self-optimization has a fixed place in the everyday culture of the present. What is to be understood by the ubiquitous term, however, is controversially discussed. Self-optimization provokes: critics reject it as part of a neoliberal coercion, proponents interpret it as an expression of autonomy. The contributors of the interdisciplinary band differentiate the discourse about self-optimization: they question current valuation patterns, highlight ambiguities and fractures and expose the cultural complexity of the phenomenon.
content.title_en: Optimization of the self : concepts, presentations and practices

content.text: Queere's Letter in Catholicism : Criticism of Religion in the Early Work of Fernando Vallejo and Josef Winkler. How can we understand the ambivalent relationship between queer literary tradition and Catholicism? This question is addressed by the present research work, which set itself the goal of exploring the ambivalent relationship of queer literary aesthetics with the Catholic religion. This is the result of this dissertation from the early work of Fernando Vallejo and Josef Winkler, which aims to outline three main strategies of affirmative and negational religious critique.
content.title_en: Queere's Letter in Catholicism : Criticism of Religion in the Early Work of Fernando Vallejo and Josef Winkler

content.text: Artificial Intelligence : how can a trustworthy use be achieved in Germany and Europe?. The technology of artificial intelligence has arrived in everyday life of consumers. It meets us in almost all areas – whether in communication, transportation or in official contact. The present collection is dedicated to the following possibilities, risks and legal implications from various, interdisciplinary perspectives. Typical problems are addressed, which include the protection of discrimination, transparency, traceability and verifiability as well as the data selection of AI systems. Consumer protection is also addressed by creating standards, standards and certification. The picture is supplemented by the presentation of area-specific challenges. Finally, the practical problem of law enforcement in the context of consumer-prone AI systems is addressed. Artificial intelligence abroad affects our everyday life in specific areas.
content.title_en: Artificial intelligence: how can a trustworthy use be achieved in Germany and Europe?

content.text: Business Analytics: how you use data for controlling companies. Why do some companies fully exploit the potential of business analytics and others do not? The reason for this is not a lack of competence in the use of algorithms. Rather, other aspects of business analytics are not sufficiently considered! This includes the interpretation and visualization of the results of the algorithms, but also the organizational positioning of the analytics function. This book provides managers with all the essential aspects of business analytics in a compact form. The framework for this is four basic questions: For which business problems should the scarce analytics resources be used? Which resources, i.e. data, IT and personnel, are necessary to solve the problems? Which algorithms can solve the problems? How do the results of the algorithms have to be interpreted and visualized so that managers can use them correctly? A special feature of this book are the numerous practical examples. In these real examples, all aspects of business analytics are illustrated.
content.title_en: Business Analytics : how to use data for controlling companies

content.text: When monsters roar and angels sing: a little sociology of heavy metal. Formerly music of young hangovers and outlaws, heavy metal has arrived more and more in the middle of society today: probably more than 10 million Germans hear heavy metal. But why do they do that? What do they look for and what do they find in this music, which is often perceived by outsiders as pure noise? Why is heavy metal teeming with monsters and devils - and why are the gods and angels not silent? What do metal fans experience when they hear their music - and what experience does it always bring back to the concert? Why do they constantly read music magazines and don't listen to CDs? How is it to explain that 40 percent of metal fans claim that the music has saved their lives? And why is heavy metal stronger than the music industry? What is it really about in heavy metal? These questions and more answers Hartmut Rosa in this small sociology of heavy metal.
content.title_en: When monsters roar and angels sing : a little sociology of heavy metal

content.text: Religion and Gender : Concepts - Experiences - Media. In public and media debates, the connection between religion and gender plays a prominent and problematic role. Religious experiences and practices are not adequately understood without consideration of the diversity of the affected and active subjects. Nevertheless, a gender-sensitive religious science is still not self-evident. Current and historical case studies on the connection between religion and diversity take into consideration different religions such as Islam as well as western and orthodox Christianity and also deal with a variety of media, such as narratives, films, series or reality TV.
content.title_en: Religion and Gender : Concepts - Experiences - Media

content.text: Perspectives on transitions in refugees education: ruptures, passages, and re-orientations. Refugees are confronted with transitions in their lives: at an individual, social and cultural level. This book deals with various aspects of these transitions and their overlaps with educational experiences. Studies from different country contexts show the complex relationships between individuals, culture, society and institutions. The study of these relationships and experiences during transition processes is intended to contribute to a deeper understanding of the different types of transitions in connection with education, which can be used in the future to improve support structures. Refugees face transitions in their lives: at an individual, a social and a cultural level. This book covers various aspects of these transitions and their interactions with educational experiences. content.text: Digital transformation in vocational education and training: concepts, findings and challenges. With a view to social progress and economic performance, the digital gap in the German education system must be made up. Vocational education plays a key role in digital transformation due to its close links with the economy. The articles in the collection cover aspects and cross-cutting topics in which digital media opens up new possibilities for action at both content and method: organisation of training, professionalisation of teachers, digitally supported examination tasks, cooperation of learning places, changes in didactics through the use of digital media such as learning analytics dashboards, augmented reality and virtual reality, individualisation of learning processes, diagnosis of learning levels, inclusion and career participation opportunities through digital technologies, as well as forms of political socialisation and ability to act as a task of vocational education. The collection covers the future and ideas for the vocational education school 2030.
content.title_en: Digital transformation in vocational education and training: concepts, findings and challenges

content.text: Introduction to good laboratory practice : a practical manual. The book provides the reader with the principles of the GLP system and provides principles for the organisation and infrastructure of a test facility, such as the use of computer-aided systems and standard working instructions. Furthermore, the reader is informed about the process of GLP tests, the archiving of documents and the interfaces to other QM systems. Good laboratory practice (GLP) is a formal framework for non-clinical experimental testing of substances or preparations, as laid down in the Chemicals Act, the results of which are intended to enable an assessment of their potential risks to humans and the environment in a licensing, authorisation, registration, registration or notification process and is applied in the areas of chemicals, pharmaceuticals, plant protection products, food additives, dyes, packaging and explosives.
content.title_en: Introduction to good laboratory practice : a practical manual

content.text: In other times: Time discourses in transition. Klappentext: Zeit was and is omnipresent. What is closer to focusing on international and interdisciplinary research than on its research? The epoch-wide study of the topic in this volume demonstrates the great importance of the phenomenon of time for people. It also shows in what diverse questions and sometimes astonishing answers the great attraction that the topic exerts on humanity has always been. The studies in this volume range from ancient Greece to the present, from childish sense of time to philosophical conceptions of time and from ancient Chinese views to duration and transience to the importance of natural phenomena in the early modern age. In their entirety they are evidence that the scientific attitude of fundamental openness to positions and approaches enables us to pursue science in the service of all and in the sense of Comenius as "improvement of all human affairs".
content.title_en: In other times : Time Discourses in Change

content.text: Inhospitable times: Salzburg after World War II 1945-1947. Salzburg was fortunate that not the Soviet army but the US army liberated the country from Nazi rule. Nevertheless, it was initially a hard occupation. A central problem was the denazification. A radical elimination of the former National Socialists would have prevented the attempt to rebuild. Thus, the Nazis were enslaved: Great Nazis were arrested, small Nazis remained in their positions. A consciousness of the Austrian co-responsibility for the crimes of the Nazis was lacking. Responsibility for the crimes was outsourced to the Germans. The most important thing was the dreary everyday life: famine, housing, refugee crisis. Nevertheless, the US military government and the state government were slowly trying to build a democracy that should avoid the mistakes of the First Republic. The result was a consensus of the three approved parties. Nevertheless, the shadow of the First Republic continued to operate. The strong ÖVP accused the SPÖ of possessing a low Austrian consciousness, the SPÖ accused the ÖVP leaders of being responsible for Austrofascism.
content.title_en: Inhospitable times : Salzburg after the Second World War 1945-1947

content.text: Non nobis – über das Bauen in der Zukunft / Werner Sobek ; Volume 2: About the boundary conditions of the future. With volume 2 of the trilogy, Werner Sobek continues his comprehensive analysis of the relationships between building and the environment. His focus this time is on the developments that we have to expect in the coming decades and on the boundary conditions within which human action will still be possible. As in the first volume, it is about resources, emissions, energy, global warming, climate goals, population development, migration and much more. The book offers a ruthless analysis of the world of tomorrow. It is an indispensable basis for the decisions to be made today about our future way of building, living and moving forward.

content.text: Artificial intelligence: what it can & what it expects us to do. Artificial intelligence (AI) stands for machines that can do what man can: hear and see, speak, learn, solve problems. In some cases, they are not only faster, but also better than man. How do these smart machines work? Do they threaten us, make us superfluous? Journalist and AI expert Manuela Lenzen explains clearly what artificial intelligence can and what awaits us. Artificial intelligence is the new magic word of digital capitalism. Intelligent computer systems provide medical diagnostics and legal advice. They manage the stock trade and soon control our cars. They paint, dense, interpret and compose. Ever smarter robots stand on the conveyor belts, welcome us at the hotel, guide us through the museum or roast burgers and snip the salad. But besides the utopia of a beautiful new intelligent world of technology have long since entered the world of science: from artificial intelligences that monitor us at every step, who take over our jobs and replace our control. "The robot look at the scene of the world of science can be defined by the word of the word of science.
content.title_en: Artificial intelligence : what it can & what awaits us

content.text: Digitality dance! : about commoning & computing. Digital technologies are an impediment! To change this, we should not turn away from them, but rather look at their transformative power. Shintaro Miyazaki calls for the alternative rhythms of cooperative, solidarity-based coexistence (commoning) to be made operable and the digitality to dance. He makes a life conceivable in which profit and property no longer play a role, but the sustainable interaction of the needs of our living ecosystems with those of all people has top priority. Here capitalism criticism meets a critical, Marxist-informed media theory of algorithmic modelling of other futures.
content.title_en: Dance digitality! : about commoning & computing

content.text: Spectacle and opportunity space: Art and the long summer of migration. What happened in 2015 was not a sudden appearance without any preconditions and not a crisis of migration, but a crisis of the European border regime. In addition to the idiosyncratic movements of migration, this time was characterized by civil engagement and numerous art and cultural productions with, for and about refugees. Nanna Heidenreich negotiates the overlaps between art and politics, activism and artistic intervention and asks with the perspective of migration: How is the relationship between spectacle and possibility space? And what resonances can be found between post_colonial and post-migrant perspectives - especially with regard to the politics of infrastructures?
content.title_en: Spectacle and Possibilities : Art and the Long Summer of Migration

content.text: The opportunities and challenges of cooperation are being developed by youth associations. Youth associations are increasingly working together with all-day schools because children and young people are spending more (free) time there. The forms of these cooperations range from individual offers to the design of the entire day-long offer. Based on empirical case studies on the engagement of Catholic youth associations in the all-day school, Claudia Gärtner and Judith Könemann investigate the diversity, opportunities and challenges of these cooperations as well as the associated expectations and objectives. Their empirical explorations form the basis for conceptual designs, how school and church youth association work can cooperate more closely.
content.title_en: Church Youth Work in the Full-Day School : Opportunities and Challenges of Cooperation

content.text: Smart cities, digitalization and citizen participation: the vision of politics and administration. The volume deals with aspects of smart cities, digitalization and citizen participation. Digitalisation with citizen participation and citizen participation with digital instruments and formats – these are two sides of a medal. Smart cities test numerous facets of municipal digitization. Dialogue-oriented communication is necessary to find sustainable solutions for politics, administration, associations and citizens. Digital communication tools are also helpful. State governments successfully use messenger services, and municipal construction offices use social media channels. Municipal councils and mayors are open to digital formats of citizen participation, but often want more information about their possibilities and limits. The editor Dr. Frank Brettschneider is a university professor of communication science at the University of Hohenheim.
content.title_en: Smart cities, digitisation and citizen participation: the view of politics and administration

content.text: The book takes a completely new look at the climate crisis: all talk of CO2, drought, heat and floods are also consequences of massive changes in the landscape, soil sealing and disturbed water cycles. The good news: We can change something about this without waiting for the next climate conference to finally produce results. Local groups and committed communities can not reduce the CO2 content of the atmosphere, but the local temperatures are the solution. Water and vegetation are the solution: If we succeed in storing more water in the landscape and greening cities and landscapes, it can become more rain and cooler, the risk of flooding is falling. Thus we get three solutions at the price of one: climate, species and health protection. The book takes us with intact river landscapes, fields and corridors, future-proof forests as well as cities that store water like sponges instead of leading it into the sewerage.
content.title_en: Afforestation against drought: how nature can help us to end the water emergency
