content.title_en: The energy imperative: 100 percent now: how to realize the complete switch to renewable energy

content.text: The architectural argument: texts and interviews. Hans Kollhoff has not only made himself an internationally renowned acting architect with designs and buildings. The writing and speaking architect also challenges the critical consideration of his profession. More than that: Hans Kollhoff has repeatedly broken public debates on practical and architectural theoretical questions from the fence as a keyword. Concepts such as "Tectonics", "Convention" or "the stone house" have been brought back into discussion in the 1990s, even beyond the narrower professional public sphere, and become part of a theoretical, sometimes highly Polish, discussion of architecture. "Kollhoff argues with concepts such as tradition, convention or metier. These imply an individual validity, but whether such an attempt can still be asserted is unlikely... He relies on Heinrich Wölfflin's theses on architectural psychology from the end of the 19th century, which our conception of physical phenomena (especially buildings) can be traced back to the bodily organization of man. This attempt to establish a naturalization of the architect's life, however, cannot only remind the basic concept of the existence of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept.
content.title_en: The architectural argument : texts and interviews

content.text: Garden plants are wintering properly: from woody plants, perennials and roses to pond and potted plants. The guide explains all important winter protection measures for woody plants, perennials, roses, pond and potted plants and offers first-aid measures for frost damage and tips for animal winter guests. With many photos, tables and further addresses. (Kristina Kroll) According to M. Phlipfen: "Gartnertipps für Herbst und Winter" (BA 11/07) finally a guide, which deals exclusively with the so important winter protection measures, so that woody plants, perennials, roses, pond and potted plants as well as the lawn survive the cold season well. In the short introduction, among other things, the winter hardening zones for Central Europe are presented, followed by procedures and advice (cut, active winter protection, water requirement) for all plants that remain outside in winter. Special topics such as lawn, garden pond, animals in the garden is dedicated to a separate chapter. Also potted plants that are brought inside, need special locations and care. The increasingly of spring plants are not forgotten.
content.title_en: Wintering garden plants properly : from woody plants, perennials and roses to pond and pot plants

content.text: From alcohol to sugar: twelve substances that changed the world. The author is a chemist, science editor and writer. Accordingly, he is also known to us for the wide range of his works. He is known both for his novels, here most recently "Alles Fleisch ist Gras" (BA 4/10) and "Semmlers Deal" (BA 3/08), as well as for non-fiction books, here last "Forgotten Inventions" (BA 4/03). The latter deals with the history of technology. In the present book, which was nominated in Austria in the category of natural science/technology for the choice of the best science book of 2010, the author reports on the historical, economic and natural scientific backgrounds of 12 chemical substances: alcohol, ammonia, aniline, anti-babypille, gasoline, quinine, caffeine, DDT, rubber, penicillin, soda and sugar. It is to be seen whether all these substances can really be counted among the "12 of the most important substances" (cloth text). The fact is that the extremely interesting, informative and exciting to read and impressively understandable for us, our students, have changed our chemical stories very impressively.
content.title_en: From alcohol to sugar: twelve substances that changed the world

content.text: Sven Hofestedt seeks money for enlightenment : stories. In his second volume with stories, the author, born in Kalkar am Niederrhein in 1966, deals with events and experiences that make reality fragile for his characters and profoundly change their perception of the world
content.title_en: Sven Hofestedt seeks money for enlightenment : Stories

content.text: We still have to plant weeds: [Schloss Ippenburg - Geschichte einer Passion]. Viktoria Freifrau von dem Bussche is one of the most famous gardeners in Germany - and it is out of passion and with all her heart. Since 1998 she organizes the annual Schloss- und Gartenfestival on the grounds of her family property. This year, the Schlosspark offers the Landesgartenschau Niedersachsen a beautiful environment. In this book Viktoria von dem Bussche reports easily and easily about the emergence of her various gardens, the castle history and her very special passion for gardening. Many large-format pictures, sketches and plans underscore this unique history and make the book a very special Schöker for flower and garden fans! (Source: www.buchhandel.de 03.05.2010)
content.title_en: We still have to plant weeds : [Castle Ippenburg - History of a Passion]

content.text: The end of patience: consistently against juvenile violent criminals. The violent offenders become younger, more brutal, less ruthless and society with this problem helpless. The Berlin youth judge Krästen Heisig was not prepared to accept this. Thus, she did not want to accept that among young people between crime and court proceedings many months pass and developed the Neuköllner model. Here, after simple offences of young people, the trial takes place within three weeks. The fast penalties have a greater effect on perpetrators and victims. She explains the model and its enforcement path, describes the life courses of young criminals, describes crimes and procedures, calls the situations at schools, youth offices and the police. Heisig also provides facts, however, as well as suggestions for solutions, such as the networking of police, prosecutor, youth office, schools, authorities, institutions and parents should work. Here she also casts a comparative glance at European abroad. (buchhandel.de) The author committed suicide at the beginning of July. Her book acts like a contempt before this background and is already a deadlock to the nine mirror.
content.title_en: The End of Patience: Consistent Against Young Violence-Puggers

content.text: Freedom of will in theology and neurosciences : a historical-systematic guide. The fact that theology and neuroscience are not necessarily opposed to the central and controversial topic of "freedom of will" is shown in this book, which describes important parallels between theological and neuroscientific concepts. The author first introduces the history of the theological and philosophical concept of will and outlines the most important developments and accentuations from antiquity to the age of the Reformation. This historical part is complemented by a systematic part in which the theological ideas of freedom of will are typified and compared with central positions of psychology and neuroscience. The result is a ›dynamic-personal model of freedom of will‹, which combines theological and neuroscientific perspectives and models in a productive and illuminating way.
content.title_en: Freedom of will in theology and neurosciences : a historical-systematic guide

content.text: Mobility in rural areas, with special attention to demand-driven modes of operation of public transport. In the transport policy discussion, demand-driven forms of public transport (ÖPNV) are often considered as a suitable complement to traditional public transport, thinning out in demand-driven spaces, in order to respond to the quality disadvantage compared to motorised individual transport (MIV), demographic change and the flexibilisation of mobility demand. The present study evaluates literature on the contribution of demand-driven modes of operation of public transport to maintain a basic range of mobility in rural areas. As the greatest obstacle to the introduction of demand-driven modes of operation is the low level of cost coverage. Costs per passenger are partly related to the cost of taxi use. Since the occupation rate per journey is usually hardly higher than in the MIV, this form of public transport has no ecological advantage. Due to the limited potential of demand-driven modes of operation, the study will examine further approaches beyond the traditional and demand-driven public transport system (Verlag Verlag: ÖPNV).
content.title_en: Mobility in rural areas, with special attention to the need-driven modes of operation of public transport

content.text: Industrial architecture in Saxony : Reserved by new use. Summary: Many factory buildings in Saxony can no longer be used industrially, but some of these old plants are architecturally so attractive that they were tried to preserve them. In this volume more than 50 of the most beautiful buildings are presented: One of the most famous is the oriental-looking cigarette factory 'Yenidze' in Dresden. The old consumer center and the cotton spinning mill in Leipzig are just two more examples of the industrial monuments that were restored in old splendor, whose uniqueness this volume shows
content.title_en: Industrial architecture in Saxony : Receiving through new use

content.text: 55 reasons to become an engineer. The author, CEO of ThyssenKrupp AG, breaks a lance for the engineering profession, which in his opinion is "the most beautiful of the world" and leads to a shadowy existence in the public sphere. Not least, demographic change, but also the professional image (difficult study, dry work) and the peripherality of technical knowledge in school education have led to a noticeable lack of future career prospects. The author emphasizes the creative and useful side of the job and brings tangible examples of applications and necessary conditions. He describes entertaining, full-bodied, sometimes provocative and promotes many future career generations. Reader for a broad audience, with drawings, without registers or further literature. He does not replace a study guide. In addition to "Career and Career Planner Technology" (BA 11/09). (2)
content.title_en: 55 Reasons to Become an Engineer

content.text: The social state: Origin and development in an international comparison. Gerhard A. Ritter's standard work on the emergence and development of the social state since the early modern times is more topical than ever. The public debates on social transfers, health costs and the appropriate level of Hartz-IV services are a source of high waves - not only in Germany. The author gives an overview of the formation of the modern social state in the area of tension between industrialization, social change and changing social and political forces. Differences in the systems of social security and labour relations in Germany, Great Britain, France, Scandinavia, the United States and Japan are thus clear and comprehensible. The new edition of the volume is extended by an essay that presents the current problems of the social state, triggered by demographic development, the change of the working world, the globalization and Europeanization as well as the costs of German unity, and the position of the German social state in an international comparison.
content.title_en: The welfare state: Origin and development in an international comparison

content.text: The Unfinished : Germany between unity and duality. The fall of the Wall fought by the East Germans and cheered by all. Twenty years of unification, but the Day of German Unity still seems like a retort. May the state unity be completed, which is not the case for people. False promises of flourishing landscapes and unilateral accession without the participation of the people caused disappointment and discord. Polls still show a dark picture. "It can't please you," says even Angela Merkel, but it doesn't change much. So it must not remain. A strong country needs an inner unity and the diversity of people, it needs reconciliation at last. That's what can happen.
content.title_en: The Unfinished : Germany between Unity and Unity

content.text: Atlas of World Images. Visuality has a fundamental meaning for our understanding of the world. It has produced the most diverse world images, but is more than just a repetition of vision. The world images give us a visual image of the world and of the cosmos. They are powerful instruments for practical and theoretical action in the world, which in various ways design our ideas of the world and shape our world view. The richly illustrated Atlas of World Images is the result of a three-year research work by the interdisciplinary working group ?Die Welt als Bild? of the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences, which has devoted itself to the research of the practices of visual world production in the form of images. The publication provides insight into a wide spectrum of world images and outlines a temporal framework that begins with ancient Egyptian world concepts and ends with current satellite images of Google Earth.
content.title_en: Atlas of World Images

content.text: Natural science meets religion : opponents, strangers, partners?. Barbour is dedicated to the fascinating topics that arise at the interface of the material and spiritual dimensions of life. What happened at the beginning of the world, what does quantum physics say about what we perceive as reality, is evolution of God's kind of creation and what do the genes have to do with our will? These and other questions find an answer here. Ian G. Barbour dives into the world of neuroscience, genetics, the nature of man, evolution, quantum physics and reflects their meanings for our world picture, for our God image, for our interpretation of creation narratives. Through these interfaces the author gives a clearly understandable, simply written introduction to the relationship between religion and natural science.
content.title_en: Science meets religion : opponents, strangers, partners?

content.text: The group is a collective work of renowned fall prevention experts led by Dr. C. Becker, head of the Federal Initiative for Fall Prevention and Chief Physician of a Geriatric Rehabilitation Clinic. The target groups of these programs are both older people with already limited mobility and those who want to become preventively active. The title of A. Pierobon (Thieme; BA 2/08) is aimed primarily at people working in the care sector and does not include exercises. The elaborate title of F. Ziganek-Soehlke (ID 26/08) is widely used for the benefit of the barbarian and the majority of the group. The group is also highly recommended for the benefit of the barbarian and the majority of the group.
content.title_en: Fall prevention training : [Equilibrium & Strength training, no fear of falls, working aid for trainers, exercise hours]

content.text: The new band of the series "Here moves something" (lastly "You're looking into the tube", BA 9/10) contains a collection of imaginative game ideas, songs, craft ideas and movement stories on the topic of environmental protection. The well-explained and relatively easy to implement proposals are suitable for use in kindergarten as well as in school and club. The games are complemented by suggestions for participation actions such as the children's tournament for children from 3 to 12. Can be used for school children.
content.title_en: Keeping our environment fit

content.text: Children and young people find and create daring tasks in the niches of our movement culture, which serve them to try out themselves and to give them self-representation and satisfy their need for exciting and captivating experiences. They climb, jump, swing, balance or drive daring maneuvers with the skateboard or bike. These special test and probation actions are also to be made possible for the pupils in school sports. Under the educational perspective they should learn something and be responsible for the appropriate handling of daring sports activities and also be supported in their personality development. The book aims to motivate teachers to engage in the risk perspective in sport and give them certainty of action. In addition to educational orientation, three didactic topics are therefore at the centre: the experience and the management of ventures, the experience and the handling of fear as well as the experience of trust and reliability.
content.title_en: Something dare and be responsible in school sports : didactic impulses and practical aids

content.text: Mashup : Praise the copy. Because she incorporated passages from blogs into her book, Helene Hegemann triggered a controversy. When Danger Mouse released an album on which he mixed Beatles songs with Jay Z's (to mash), he was celebrated as a fighter against the creative industry. The debates about copyright and new forms like mashups are extremely confusing. It is certain that copying has lost its innocence in the online age. In this cultural history of the copy Dirk von Gehlen brings order into the discussion and variants of the liquefying distinction between original and copy into play.
content.title_en: Mashup : Praise of the copy

content.text: The physical internship : Handbook 2010 for students of physics; with 21 tables. The Handbook 2010 is the "Guide" to the basic internship for students of physics at the Georg-August-University of Göttingen. It describes the experiments and their basics that have to be carried out in the Göttingen physical internship from the second to the fourth semester.
content.title_en: The physical internship : Handbook 2010 for students of physics ; with 21 tables

content.text: The genetic key to music: why music belongs to humanity. Stone age people carved flutes, Greenlanders solved disputes by rap duels and football fans in seconds become choir singers. Singing strengthens our immune system, Mozart demonstrably reduces the stress of intensive patients and piano playing can sometimes even improve math notes. Christian Lehmann's entertaining trajectory revealed by the evolution and cultural history of humanity: music is in our genes, shapes the profile of every culture, influences body, psyche and spirit - is thus an indispensable part of our human nature. --- Dr. phil. Christian Lehmann, born in 1966, studied musicology, biology, Germanic and singing, researches in the field of the evolution of music and teaches at the University of Munich. He has been working as a voice designer for several years at the Regensburg Cathedral Patts, appears himself as a vocal soloist and works in internationally renowned professional choirs such as the Collegium Vocale Gent.
content.title_en: The genetic key to music: why music belongs to humanity

content.text: Insurrection of the headscarf girls: German Muslims defend themselves against Islamism. Lale Akgün has made a career in German politics, has written bestsellers, is at home in Cologne and professes their faith in Islam. They and countless other women are held liable for Islamism. They are defamed as headscarf girls and laughed at as relics of an archaic society because they do not bother to distinguish between Islam and Islamism. Lale Akgün demands a new Islam, one that acknowledges the Western values, the values of the French Revolution and the Enlightenment but it is precisely in this struggle abandoned by those who allegedly so vehemently advocate the rights of Muslim women Lale Akgün has made a career in German politics, has written bestsellers, is at home in Cologne - and confesses to the Islamic faith. They and countless other women are taken into account for Islamism. They are defamed as headscarfs and as relics of an archaic society, because one does not bother to fight between Islam and Islam, but the other is accused of the rights of Islam.
content.title_en: Uprising of the headscarf girls: German Muslims fight Islamism

content.text: ECDL: the European Computer Guide Certificate; the complete course book for Microsoft Office 2007 and Windows 7, certified according to Syllabus 5.0; [DLGI-approached learning material ECDL 5.0, approved learning material ECDL Core Syllabus 5.0]. The training book for the preparation for the examination for the "European Computer Guide Certificate" (ECDL) also takes into account the current operating system Windows 7 and Internet Explorer 8. (LK/HB: Isigkeit) In preparation for the examination for the "European Computer Guide Certificate" (ECDL), the two authors repeatedly present revisions of their course book (last version BA 2/09). Compared to the previous edition, new passages to Windows 7 were inserted in the module Operating Systems. Also adapted were the statements to Internet Explorer, as now version 8 is based on the basis. Until these two exceptions, the entire remaining text remained unchanged. The acquisition of a current edition is not necessary, but an exchange is not necessary. Since a new Office version has been published in the meantime, it may be assumed that a further version of the revised version is not available for the new edition.
content.title_en: ECDL : the European Computer Guide; the complete course book for Microsoft Office 2007 and Windows 7, certified according to Syllabus 5.0; [DLGI-approved learning material ECDL 5.0, approved learning material ECDL Core Syllabus 5.0]

content.text: Paperback of process engineering : with 49 tables. Compact, practice-oriented teaching and reference work with basic explanations on important processes and applications. In addition to the classical sub-areas (mechanical, thermal, chemical reaction engineering), biological process engineering (new sub-area) and biotechnological aspects are included and are suitable for repetition of the teaching material and for exam preparation for students. Updated from the 1st edition 2000 (BA 2/01) (work market situation) and revised in the guidelines. The old edition can be used up, should be supplemented with this new one. (2)
content.title_en: Paperback of process engineering : with 49 tables

content.text: The study of the processes of propagation in physics, known as diffusion, and in various areas of the natural and human sciences. (Michael Mücke) The special field of the author and professor of physics is diffusion, which is also the subject of this work. Known from physics lessons is the "Brownian movement", the seemingly unregulated movement of small particles in a liquid. No less than Albert Einstein has investigated the causes and mathematically described the movements. But diffusion phenomena are by no means limited to physics, because by means of the diffusion laws one can also trace the seemingly random paths of moving particles, living beings, even ideas. Thus, G. Vogl here describes, among other things, the diffusion of Greek culture and Buddhism, the spread of Rosskatanienminiermotte and Ragweed (an immigrated type of foot), the plague and the diffusion of European and pre-Asian languages, and perhaps even the diffusion of Greek culture and Buddhism, the spread of Rosskatanienminiermotte and of the Ragweed, can be a fruitful way of working.
content.title_en: Ways of chance : dance of atoms, invasion of new species, spread of diseases and languages

content.text: Positions on the reconstruction of lost buildings and spaces: a project of the Federal Ministry of Transport, Building and Urban Development's "Experimental Housing and Urban Development" research programme (BMVBS), supervised by the Federal Institute for Building, Urban and Spatial Research (BBSR) at the Federal Office for Building and Spatial Planning (BBR). Urban development is often the result of conflicting interests, ideas and attitudes. In this respect, the reconstruction debate is not only conducted by experts. What has changed in society that for some years now more frequent reconstructions have been considered? Are they embedded in a general need for historicality or merely an expression of a specific concept of beauty, a certain desire for a particular image of the city? What roles do the various actors take in the debate?
content.title_en: Positions on the reconstruction of lost buildings and spaces : a project of the research programme "Experimental Housing and Urban Development" of the Federal Ministry of Transport, Building and Urban Development (BMVBS), supervised by the Federal Institute for Building, Urban and Spatial Research (BBSR) at the Federal Office for Building and Spatial Planning (BBR)

content.text: Algorithms and data structures. Knowledge of data structures and algorithms is one of the basics of computer science. Detailed descriptions can be found in standard textbooks on computer science, e.g. Th. Ottmann (ID-G 13/12). A good introduction to the topic, based on a preliminary course for prospective computer science students, Heinrich Müller (ID-B 11/13). This book is aimed at the beginning semester of computer science. It takes another interesting path. The reader accompanies the computer science practitioner Algatha Data Strukt (without any prior knowledge) in the programming of the software for managing all branch data of an expanding company and learns from their growing insights (and also backlashes). The book is structured according to the algorithmic ideas behind the different data structures and algorithms. An application reference is taken into account and consequences resulting from the ideas for different application cases are well worked out. For all algorithms a Java implementation is given. Many instructive illustrations and exercises (with solutions). (2)
content.title_en: Algorithms and data structures

content.text: The prohibition of killing in war: an intervention attempt. War is the use of force. This is an equally banal statement as in its consequence difficult. On the one hand, the war is subject to rules which are intended to prevent its demarcation. On the other hand, its appearance has changed. From the classic enemy constellation, which extends to few war parties, it has become an immediate international matter with numerous actors. Based on resolutions of the UN Security Council, government leaders are being eliminated and societies remodelled - the world is to be made more peaceful. That this happens with military violence is increasingly proving to be a problem. Whether in Gaza, Sri Lanka, Iraq or Afghanistan - in the affected populations grow rage and bitterness. Above all, the uninvolved civilians killed in combat actions are no longer unrecognizable with the concept of collateral damage. And in the states that are part of the intervention missions and face an asymmetrical opponent, there are always pressing questions about the meaning and purpose of ongoing missions. Which violence is acceptable, which is legally prohibited? When the unacceptable situation is not being protected?
content.title_en: The War Prohibition of Killing: An Intervention Try
