The well-known computer author has summarized his almost identical introductions "Office 2010", "Office Home & Student 2010" (both BA 9/10 - can continue) and changed to a continuously colored layout. Beginners with low Windows knowledge get very well understandable explanations for the professional or private use of the "Home & Business" version with Word, Excel, Outlook, OneNote and PowerPoint under Windows 7/8. Focus on the most important program functions and application possibilities of the individual modules as well as cross-programme work. Keyboard and touch operation, installation and individual adaptation are explained and offered in a short time to solve problems. With detailed step-by-step instructions, vivid screenshots, information boxes for the target group.

content.text: Control data quality successfully: Practical solutions for business intelligence projects. More and more companies are understanding good data quality management as a decisive competitive advantage: IT costs are reduced, projects are accelerated, changes in the market or legal requirements can be reacted faster and more flexibly. Data integration across system, department and company boundaries are facilitated and wrong decisions are prevented based on poor data. Practical examples show you how to improve the quality of your data in a targeted and sustainable manner. Analyze the causes and effects of poor data quality and find out what investments are really worthwhile. Learn the basics of data quality management, the technical implementation with custom tools and the practical implementation in a complete cycle of BI project. With this comprehensive knowledge, the authors provide you with a valuable guide to successful data quality management. The 3rd edition has been completely revised. Big Data has been included as a new topic, as it represents a new evolutionary stage for the world of business intelligence and thus has an impact on data quality management.
content.title_en: Control data quality successfully : Practical solutions for business intelligence projects

content.text: Network policy: Freedom and legal protection on the Internet. Key issues of network policy are: What does freedom mean on the Internet? What can the law do to minimize the risks of electronic networking and protect individual rights? How can democracy develop under the influence of new technologies and the demand for greater transparency? What importance does data protection have and how should it be shaped in the future? The author – legal scientist, who was also the first Federal Commissioner for Data Protection and, at times, the Minister of the Interior of a federal state – not only poses questions, but also provides answers: Based on risk analysis, he deals with the various problem areas and gives concrete solutions. He deals primarily with the fears and concerns of those who distrust the new technologies and their suppliers and users, and pleads for targeted, effective legal regulations that contribute to reducing risks.
content.title_en: Network policy: Freedom and legal protection on the Internet

content.text: Dropbox : save safely and work effectively in the cloud. The author gives an overview in the preface of the possibilities that Dropbox offers as a cloud storage medium. Of course, the cloud is not really to be seen as a cloud in the sky, but as one of many servers of the company, many safely in the USA. The advantages of having at least 3 GB of storage space on these servers for free are completely enough for some users. Those who want more, have to pay or use other providers additionally. How to use Dropbox is described in detail and illustrated with many colored screenshots. It is practical that one can release own folders and thus make them accessible to other employees. Thus projects can be conveniently processed everywhere. Dropbox is also a good backup solution. Also the current security concerns take Schilling forward looking. He not only recommends Truecrypt as a good encryption medium, but also describes the installation. Since smartphones and other cloud media are also treated in the last chapter, the band has succeeded perfectly. - More can not be demanded. (1)
content.title_en: Dropbox : Save securely and work effectively in the cloud

Both for practitioners and application-oriented scientists and students. Impassetly with double-packing.

content.text: Less politics! : pleas for a freedom-oriented conception of state and law. In recent times politicians are increasingly trying to create "justice" by means of law. They are a "social mischief" and demand more redistribution. This book takes the opposite position. Not (even) more politics is indicated, but less politics. The community is at the service of people - not the other way around. Not supposedly world-improving politicians are to make decisions for the citizens, but these themselves. The author conceives the legal system as an infrastructure for exercising freedoms. The guideline of the legislation should therefore be to enable people to implement decisions that are made in their own right. Winners of the German Economic Book Prize 2013
content.title_en: Less policy! : plea for a freedom-oriented conception of state and law

This book offers first the basics, and indeed relatively wide-ranging, since many neighboring areas are important (in addition to electric drive motors e.g. also the power electronics, control technology, charging and battery technology etc.); also questions of accident prevention in the recovery of an e-car are discussed. There are still not so many books on the topic. Also an introduction offers the bird learning program "Hybrid and electric drives in the car" (last ID-B 35/11; possibly also BA 3/10); "E-Autos" (ID-A 31/10) is rather an overview: "Hybrid" (ID 38/07) and K. content.text: The agreed objectives of a European market as a whole are based on differentiated starting conditions in border regions. The volume describes selected framework conditions - socio-economic and ecological starting conditions, cross-border regional policy and cooperation - and shows on this basis experience in the implementation. It is evident that a dual approach is important in the implementation, whereby a vertical orientation for the temporary implementation of the common objective concept of medium to long-term development goals should be agreed as time horizons. This vertical orientation in development stages should be assigned horizontally as graduated action levels project groups. Despite notable progress, the current institutional infrastructure for cross-border cooperation is not yet sufficiently tailored to the political needs of border regions. By establishing consortia with the participation of the various actors, an informal information and dialogue network could be built up.
content.title_en: Environmentally-friendly development of border regions through cooperative action

content.text: Energy : Physical foundations of their production, transformation and use. In this volume, scientific and physical background information on the topic of energy is provided to the reader in order to provide objective evaluation criteria for the globally highly topical discussion of the future of our energy supply. In particular, it is a central concern to prepare an assessment of all sources with regard to the influence of their extraction and use on the environment and to make the respective risk in relation to each other. After defining the concept of energy and its manifestations, global boundary conditions of the use of energy are shown. These marginal conditions are then narrowed down for Germany as a typical industrial country. The range of potential sources, fossil, renewable and nuclear, is then presented in detail. The yield of resources and other possibilities and limits of use are discussed; all energy sources are then compared according to the definition of an energy harvesting factor. The storage and transport possibilities and - closely linked herewith - the playrooms of rational dealing with the various forms of energy form form form form another focus.
content.title_en: Energy : Physical foundations of their production, transformation and use

content.text: The Lenbachhaus-Book : History, Architecture, Collections. Lenbachhaus Buch unites for the first time all the collection areas of the Städtische Galerie in the Lenbachhaus in a representative volume. Founded as a smaller museum for works with direct reference to Munich, the former villa of the painter-prince Franz von Lenbach (1836-1904) is now world-famous for the overwhelmingly rich collection of paintings by the 'Blue Rider', but also for its equally important and idiosyncratic collection on contemporary art. Essays on the new and remodeling of the museum by the architectural office Foster + Partners. The golden cube, designed by Norman Foster and his team, elegantly attached to the historical building stock, not only provides the house with additional exhibition space, it also enriches the Munich art area with a spectacular architectural accent.
content.title_en: The Lenbachhaus Book : History, Architecture, Collections

content.text: The American nuclear arsenal and the illusion of security are a true story. Best-selling author Eric Schlosser reveals in this contemporary thriller an accident in a nuclear weapons silo of the USA that would have destroyed several American cities by one hair. This true, hitherto unknown story forms the framework for unusual insights into the American nuclear armament. The brilliantly written book makes a danger aware of which we are exposed to today daily. Arkansas, September 18, 1980, evening: In routine work on a fencing-ready Titan II rocket slips a wrench from a worker's hand. "O man, that is not good," is his first thought. The mishaps lead to a chain reaction that the largest ever built nuclear bombhead threatens to explode- Eric Schlosser reconstructs on the basis of secret documents of the Defense Ministry and interviews with eyewitnesses as America was on the verge of a nuclear disaster. In this crime mystery of an even-timed rescue he is able to expose the story of American nuclear equipment to the ground. He does not use the weapons and weapons to fire the thousands of the people in the world.
content.title_en: Command and control: the US nuclear arsenals and the illusion of security; a true story

content.text: The exception: October 1943: how the Danish Jews escaped destruction with the help of their fellow citizens. How the Danish Jews escaped from the National Socialist deportation - by means of family fates, the events in Denmark during the German occupation. (Petra Friedmann) What happened exactly 70 years ago in Denmark is historically significant, because Germany's small northern neighbour formed the title-giving famous exception: In no other European country did it manage to save the Jews there almost completely from deportation to the concentration camp, using population, church, government and king. The historian, diplomat, politician, writer and journalist B. Lidegaard describes with personal contemporary witnesses reports how the Danish government and King Christian X through skillful tacturing kept a great independence and through a kind of trust relationship to a German diplomat the information about the imminent deportation, which enabled the unprecedented rescue action. The time witness reports gathered in the volume described fear and horrors and were intended to be remembered only for perönlich.
content.title_en: The exception : October 1943: how the Danish Jews escaped destruction with the help of their fellow citizens

content.text: The author presents in detailed portraits the planning and execution of 10 small gardens of different styles. (Georg Braun) On the subject of "Small Gardens" numerous good non-fiction books have been published, most recently H. Louwerse (ID-B 17/12) and Andrew Wilson (ID-G 17/13). Nevertheless, this book has its justification, because it has been optically ais also very successful in terms of content. The author, a well-known garden designer, presents 10 small but very interesting, individual gardens of different styles. The individual projects are divided into the areas of planning, execution and monthly care work. The reader finds detailed plans, material and plant lists as well as detailed instructions and helpful practical tips. appealing photos complement the clearly structured text. The book is suitable as a guide with instructions for ambitious homeworkers as well as as as as a basis for a specialist. A recommended purchase, to supplement the inventory perfectly suitable! (2) (Georg Braun)

content.text: The monster: Roman. Forts. of "The Lonest Man on the Continent". Darius Kopp, the failed IT specialist, is now only a wreck of a man. Flora, his beloved wife, whom he believed to know, took his life a year ago. In deep sadness and desolation, Darius went to the apartment without leaving. The urn was not yet buried, Darius finally went on a journey to find his wife's final resting place. He took Flora's laptop and dived into foreign countries like Albania, Turkey or Greece, as well as Flora's past, her distress, her double life. (Cornelia Jetter) Work and sleep, sleep and work: from this life, IT expert Darius Kopp was torn away as he lost his job. Little later, his wife died. He did not leave the apartment for months - then he made a journey to Hungary to join the urn. A touching love story (Cornelia Jetter)

content.text: Biogas plants in agriculture. Biogas production in Germany is booming. For many farmers, this branch of the farm is now an important pillar of income. The volume provides detailed information on basics of production and planning, on technical requirements up to economic operation. All changes to the 2012 Act on Renewable Energies (EEG) are taken into account. The focus is on, among other things, key figures on gas yield of various substrates, the possibilities of meaningful heat use and the correct storage of the available biomass types. Further emphasis is on changes in the EEG, e.g. the current regulations on electricity compensation and the possibility of direct marketing on electricity exchanges (source: aid).
content.title_en: Biogas plants in agriculture

content.text: After migration: post-migrant perspectives beyond the parallel society. Migration creates a variety of forms of mobility that combine different places, ways of life and visions. People who migrate create spaces that are different from those who left them and from those who have been re-acquired. Thus, structures, cultures and forms of communication are created that would be hardly conceivable without impulses through migration. Life practice shows that people have several homelands and belongings, can create diverse cultural and social networks and that they can deal creatively and subversively with negative attributions from outside. In this way, post-migrant, multi-local, hybrid and transcultural everyday practices develop, which have so far been hardly appreciated. The contributions of this volume therefore understand themselves as a plea for a different view of things and as a rejection of the precipitous mistrust with which migration-related phenomena are frequently encountered.
content.title_en: After migration : post-migrant perspectives beyond the parallel society

content.text: Complex trauma disorder: diagnosis and treatment of consequences of severe violence and neglect. Complex trauma disorder can be safely diagnosed and specifically treated. Experiences of severe violence and neglect, especially in childhood and adolescence, can lead to a variety of psychological and psychosomatic symptoms. Typical consequences are problems with affect regulation, self-acceptance, feelings of shame and guilt, as well as difficulties in the interpersonal area. Not infrequently, sufferers also suffer from physical complaints without sufficient organic cause, anxiety disorders, dissociative disorders or addiction diseases. The broad spectrum of complaints can be summarised under the term complex trauma disorder. The variety of symptoms available at the same time and the high impairment of patients present a challenge for diagnosis and therapy. This work also provides a comprehensive and practical overview of the entire range of consequences of severe and prolonged trauma disorder and its treatment. Basic chapters describe diagnosis, differential diagnosis and treatment strategies. In addition, the authors also address the special requirements of the treatment of children and adolescents, elderly people, victims of organized violence and patients with a successful trauma disorder.
content.title_en: Complex trauma disorder : diagnosis and treatment of consequences of severe violence and neglect

"The current time diagnosis of the "economization" of society has long since reached science and universities. The collection discusses the reorganization of universities according to the concept of "entrepreneurial university". Increasing business and market-economy principles change working and career conditions, organizations and professions, equality policies the production and mediation of scientific (gender) knowledge. Coming gender-based, segregating practices possibly in motion and what (new) gender-based effects does the implementation of current reforms and initiatives produce? How do business affect known requirements for mobility and flexibility, which are increasingly directed towards scientific subjects whose work and everyday practice? How are gender equality strategies such as gender mainstreaming and diversity management translated by university actors and what does this mean for gender equality policy? content.text: Who cares about the elderly? : on the way to a caring society. Like Heidelberg's age researcher Andreas Kruse (BA 8/07; BA 2/10) and Swiss sociologist Peter Gross (ID-A 38/13), the Freiburg social expert is one of the leading gerontologists who are committed to humane socio-political guidelines on age and care. Starting from the higher life expectancy via the horror scenario "care case", which is managed by the family "as the largest care center of the nation", through the care industry to the "exit of death aid?", Klie presents the state of the current "age care" and at the same time questions the situation. His model of shared responsibility of a caring society could be developed in the future, practical examples are available (see Wolfgang Frey: ID-A 5/14), many other approaches are listed by the author. From these housing communities in old age, citizen associations for care provision of care locally, housing groups for people with dementia in the district develop with the involvement of the creative elderly social networks and thus a sustainable care policy.

content.text: The very beautifully designed small, narrow ribbons are used in 8 short chapters by Brazilian architect Oscar Niemeyer (1907-2012). The co-founder of modern architecture was a convinced Marxist and has been committed to a more just society throughout his life. In the contributions he deals with art, beauty and fantasy, but also with politics and society, and reports on encounters with personal role models such as Sartre, Fidel Castro or Che Guevara. Italian journalist Alberto Riva wrote this booklet, which emerged from personal conversations with Oscar Niemeyer in his home country. He also gives an interesting account of the work of the important architect. content.text: Introduction to the design of school buildings : Results of international school building research ; new developments in school building ; communication problems between planners and users ; a textbook and training book. Teachers and pupils spend a substantial part of their lives in school buildings. Therefore, school buildings should not only be experienced in a dignified and pleasant way, but also in a way that promotes learning, and should not be repugnant, unfriendly or hostile. In well-designed and aesthetically sound school buildings better school achievements succeed, the willingness of users to destroy decreases and their vulnerability to diseases decreases. Therefore, it is all the more surprising that school buildings are still being built, which are being experienced by those for whom they were built as life-threatening, ugly and threatening. The book provides fundamental insights into international school building research, it lists numerous evaluation criteria from the point of view of school students and it shows opportunities for a targeted understanding between architects, designers and users. Numerous figures point to good examples, but also to serious and typical errors in the previous school building planning.

content.text: The city is strengthened by the robustness of urban life. With urban strenghtening, the urban environment is being sought from different perspectives for the robustness of urban life and the opportunities to sustainably strengthen cities. In view of increasing uncertainties and rapid social change, attention must be paid to the creative interplay of individual aspects and the whole of the city. Instead of taking familiar paths, we must think and act in alternatives. Volume 17 highlights the city's strengths in order to re-examine the particular living and quality of life in cities. Strengthening European cities is in promoting their urbanity and density. Austere resource flow and reurbanisation are future tasks that require careful urban design. In various contributions, new ideas on the diversity of use in the confined space are sought as well as strengthening governance and generating productive uncertainties that lead to new alliances.
content.title_en: Strengthening the city: the robustness of the urban environment

content.text: Therapeutic chaos: an introduction to the world of chaos theory and complexity sciences. The fact that human behavior is complex and surprising even for those who act is not a secret and will not be seriously denied by anyone. But what does this mean for therapeutic action? How do psychotherapeutic changes work? - This book deals with chaos, the abysses of complexity, but also its beauty, diversity and ability to change. It wants to explore the limits of predictability, the plan and influenceability of human behavior and show how therapeutic action opens up new possibilities for these limits. The volume provides an introduction to the world of chaos theory and complexity sciences. It offers a scientifically sound answer to the question of the organized complexity of human behavior. Psychotherapy based on modern complexity research accepts the nonpredictability of human behavior, but is not helpless to it.
content.title_en: Therapeutic Chaos: an Introduction to the World of Chaos Theory and Complexity Sciences

content.text: Rock gardens, garden caves, art mountains : motifs of nature in architecture and garden; [... in the context of the project "Zur Ikonographie der Alpenlandschaft: Kunstberge und Kunsthöhlen (1830 - 1918)"]. Rocks, grottos and mountains are recurring motifs in garden art and architecture. This book presents their varied manifestations and constructions from the 16th century to the present day with a wealth of images. - - From prominent examples, such as the Venus cave of King Ludwig II in the castle park of Linderhof, to hardly known installations, the spectrum of artificial rock structures ranges. Magnificent, with shells, snails and rocks, castles of pleasure from Renaissance and Rococo reflect the competition of the arts with nature. Täuschend real imitations of mountain formations prevail, however, since the Enlightenment according to the motto "Back to nature". Since the discovery of the Swiss Alps, a comprehensive mountain and grotto construction has been observed, which experienced a climax in the 19th century, and not least in works of art and films until today.
content.title_en: Rock gardens, garden grottos, art mountains : motifs of nature in architecture and garden ; [... within the framework of the project "Zur Ikonographie der Alpenlandschaft: Kunstberge und Kunsthöhlen (1830 - 1918)"]

Chronologically by eras from the beginnings until 1945 ordered catalogue of German aircraft, which have remained until today in museums or elsewhere. Each model is presented with an informative text, photos and references on locations. (Rolf Raschka) The weighty volume has been continuously updated compared to the 2nd edition 1998 (BA 5/99) and extended by about 80 pages. It presents chronologically by eras like "Pionierzeit bis 1914" or "1939 - 1945" ordered German aircraft, which have remained until today and found their place in museums or other facilities (including replicas!). There are also special chapters on rockets, airships and balloons. Each model is portrayed with a fairly informative text illustrated by photos and references on locations. Thus there are famous "Ju 52" still available everywhere in the world. Other models are rare. The number of 3,100 aircraft mentioned in the subtitle refers to specimens, not to different types! In its kind a standard work, which is at least used for old aircraft.

content.text: Basic knowledge IT security: the most important for the protection of systems and data. As the security situation and the technology used are constantly changing, the author has revised his textbook once again (2nd edition: BA 9/10). In addition to updating some sections (e.g. further protocols and algorithms, security of embedded systems), the topics of smartphones and apptors are now also taken into account. Some new technical terms have also been introduced (e.g. security awareness). While the font gröe has significantly reduced, apparently to limit the volume of the book, the table of contents is available in an improved preparation. Book structure and a cleverly designed didactic concept (labelling essential contents, summaries, glossary, examples, tips and hints, cross-references) support the learning process. content.text: Trace metals in groundwater East Frisia : regional thematic report; data analysis 1993 to 2012. The hydrochemistry of groundwater distinguishes between trace elements with concentrations < 1 mg/l, secondary components with concentrations between 1 and 5 mg/l and main components with concentrations > 5 mg/l (Merkel and Sperling, 1998). For metals, the elements iron, manganese and aluminium can be classified in the group of secondary components under the largely reducing conditions in groundwater East Frisia. They play a significant role in the preparation of raw water to drinking water and are removed by oxidation and precipitation. The present data analysis is devoted to metals and semi-metals, which can be found in traces in groundwater East Frisia and are hereinafter referred to as trace metals (Alloway and Ayres, 1996). Trace metals can have both an essential character, such as copper and zinc, where the absence of trace metals can be found in groundwater East Frisia, or they have toxic properties such as the presence of mercury or the presence of both elements.
content.title_en: Trace metals in groundwater East Frisia : regional thematic report ; data analysis 1993 to 2012

content.text: New types of continuing vocational training in enterprises: labour assistance for works councils and staff councils. Vocational training has grown steadily in importance over the last two decades. However, the character of continuing vocational training in enterprises is also changing. Other open forms of vocational qualification ("learning in the process of work") are being used to side with traditional continuing vocational training in courses or seminars. For works councils/staff councils, these developments both create new possibilities of influence and new requirements, because continuing vocational training is also increasingly approaching the everyday business life. The present work for works councils and staff councils is intended to provide guidance that draws attention to these new developments in training policy and in companies. Using practical examples from different sectors, current trends in continuing vocational training in enterprises are explained in order to achieve both a better understanding of the problem and to show new participation and design options of works councils in the field of continuing vocational training.

content.text: The German health system has a comparatively high level of health expenditure. WHO has assessed the output and performance (ratio of input and output) of the German health system as only average. The quality indicators of the OECD also show a very wide range of different factors. However, the reasons for over-, under- and miscare - and therefore also for the existence of significant efficiency, effectiveness and quality reserves in the German health system - are not always the same. Above all, sector-specific budgets and collective bargaining do not leave much room for the realisation of efficiency reserves. Against this background, the authors of this study propose to strengthen the contract competition on the performance side. The GKV-WSG provides for some measures to strengthen contract competition, but there are also measures that are in conflict with this goal. In particular, a semi-closed competition concept is still not recognizable. The measures adopted in the GKV-WSG are therefore only very limited in their capacity to increase the performance of the German health system.
content.title_en: Efficiency, efficiency and quality reserves in the German health system

content.text: The canteen at the park in Weimar is one of the last individually planned and almost completely preserved menses of the late East-Modern. - - - The building was planned in 1982 in the then GDR by professors, employees and students of the University of Architecture and Building (today Bauhaus-Universitaet Weimar) and built with the help of work-inserts. - - When the demolition of the canteen at the park in January 2010 was discussed to make room for a new Bauhaus museum, this was just 28 years old. content.text: After the first catastrophe: Germany, Europe and the First World War. The First World War has pre- and post-history. It shapes the development of power relations, states, cultures and societies, of historical delusions and distortions to this day. The present book traces central developments in German and European history, at the end of which the First World War is a great switcher. The presentation takes its outcome in the respective situation before the outbreak of the war and traces the course of events and consequences to the edge of our present day: Why was Austria's connection to Germany in 1918/19 an important topic of European politics, however, not 1945? Why was there no oral negotiations between Germany and its opponents in the Versailles Treaty in 1919, but a conceivable dense communication of the parties involved in the negotiation of the "Two plus Four" Treaty in 1990? How was Germany positioned before 1914, in the 1920s and since the founding of the Federal Republic in 1949 world economicly? Why was the Weimar Republic far more militarized than the old Federal Republic, despite a much smaller army? "Peter March describes in his book "After the first catastrophe. Germany, Europe and the First World War" however, it is not a subjectively perspective of war.

content.text: The disintegration of the audience: News usage between newspaper and Internet. E-paper, website, blog and of course newspaper publishers today provide journalistic information about many channels. But how do readers and users inform themselves? Only little is known about whether they have different topics in the web than in the daily newspaper or whether an attractive online appearance can attract new readers and introduce them to the newspaper. Manuel Thomä describes how journalistic information offers are used in print and online media. He shows the change of the news system between newspaper and Internet and what consequences he has for the media reception of the readers. Various approaches are presented, which are concerned with these developments in communication and media research. The empirical basis is a long-standing research project of the Institute for Practical Journalism Research. To analyse the specific use of individual channels, 30 problem-centered interviews were conducted, 1,239 regular readers interviewed by telephone and for the first time periodically interviewed online through a panel investigation of about 350 readers and users. The results show how frequently and why the interviewed readers access individual media offers, how they evaluate and why they do not do so.
content.title_en: The disintegration of the public : use of news between newspaper and internet

The pilot study is based on qualitative interviews with owners and managers of family enterprises and an economic association.? Dr. phil. Lars Schatilow is a scientist as well as an expert in political communication strategies and innovation management. In Berlin and Brussels, about 22,000 lobbyists represent the interests of public societies. But about 90 percent of German economy, the family companies, so far renounce strategic political communication: they interact intensively with politics at regional level. The successful, personal political communication culture there is not feasible at a regional level: too many issues and stakeholders require consensus and professionalization. content.text: Basic services Education: on the threat of social cohesion by thinning out the continuing education structure. This book describes the effects of migration processes and counter-control measures through education based on a model case. The design forces of further education for regional development processes, the creation of social-regional anchor points and the provision of general interest for people are analysed. content.text: Social Work as a State Practice in Urban Space. Starting from the thesis of a lack of political-scientific contextualization of social work, social work is conceived with Foucault as a state-spatial practice. Using little-received texts from Foucault on the connections between state, city and space, order strategies as well as territorial inclusion and exclusion processes are discussed and related to social work. Using a qualitative research approach that combines discourse, program and practice analysis, the Praterstern station uses a contrasting analysis of public-parliamentary and public-media discourse sections and a case study on practices of seeking social work. In this context, seek-out social work can be characterized as a spatial-relational practice that is integrated into a state-private ensemble of punishing and leading strategies, and thereby organizes aid services and directs territorial orders. The content of social work and state • social work, space and state • transformation perspectives on state and society • state, space and social work with Foucault • The empirical-qualitative research process and its methods • The public discourse on the Vienna Prastern University of Practice.

content.text: Participative media cultures: Positions and investigations on changed forms of public participation. With the Internet, especially the so-called Web 2.0, the coordinates of social, cultural and political participation seem to have shifted significantly in comparatively short time. The contributions of the collection cover from various technical perspectives the question of how this change can be adequately described and evaluated. The considerations not only take into account the implications for political participation, but also address cultural articulations in the net and new forms of participation of children and young people in educational and educational contexts. content.text: Public mobility: perspectives for sustainable transport development. Public transport is a child of the 19th century. While it has lost more and more importance in the 20th century in favour of the automobile, public transport is now in crisis. At the same time, however, great hopes are placed in public transport, which is still considered as a guarantee of sustainable transport development. In contrast, the social analysis concludes that public collective transport does not meet the individual mobility needs of modern societies. The thesis is that if public transport is not to disappoint the hopes placed in it, structural reform is needed. Introduced and discussed are approaches aimed at a strategy of individualisation of public collective transport and the publication of private individual transport. The content - context analysis - inventory analysis - potential analysis The target groups · lecturers and students of transport and mobility research · representatives of consumer associations and public transport as well as transport policy makers and administrative employees from the transport and environment departments The editor Dr. Oliver Schwedes has been a scientific assistant at the department of Integrated Transport Planning at the Technical University Berlin since 2008.

content.text: Excessive Internet use of young people in a family context: analyses of the social class, family climate and parental employment status. content.text: The future of the hospitality industry: employment prospects in the German hospitality industry. This study examines market and structural developments in the hospitality industry over the last ten years, their impact on employment and working conditions and gives an outlook on the industry development until 2017. For this purpose, the developments in the three sub-sectors hospitality, catering and catering industry are analysed. While the turnover in the catering industry and catering industry has grown, the food and drink-based catering industry has had to suffer from a decline in turnover in recent years. This has led to a decline in overall turnover in the hospitality industry. Nevertheless, in recent years, after the large declines in employment in the catering industry in the 1990s, employment has been restored for the first time. However, this employment growth is characterised by a strong increase in mini-jobs and part-time employees. The hospitality industry already counts with 1.96 million employees among the most employment-intensive sectors in Germany. Almost every second employee is employed slightly. 70 percent of the employees in the hospitality industry since 2007 are employed by a large number of employees.
content.title_en: The future of the hospitality industry: employment prospects in the German hospitality industry

content.text: Dragon and Pen Snake : Europe's grip on America and China 1519/20. In a comparison of the colonialist European access to Latin America on the one hand and the failed incorporation of China on the other, the French historian tries to reach a new global view of this epoch of colonial history in the 16th century. Review: The French historian, who has identified himself as "The Aztecs" (1993) as a specialist in Latin American history and European expansion, broadens his view of Europe's colonial history here by comparing the conquest and colonization of the Latin American peoples with the failed attempt to expand Europe's sphere of power in this way, even in the Far East, in China. His presentation is deliberately not a chronological event story, but an attempt to interpret the different historical sources in order to arrive at a new view of the epoch, which corresponds better to the situation of the non-European peoples in the context of a global history. The author is concerned with asking new questions and "slowing" the historical history of the Eurocentristism. In a demanding way, the book thus addresses those readers, who also want to have a deeper understanding of the fundamental colonial history and who already possess a new knowledge of the history.

content.text: Free radicals - why scientists do not adhere to rules. Science is generally regarded as objective and rational. But that the human factor plays a decisive role in revolutionizing innovations, shows fateful moments in the life of Galileo, Newton, Einstein and many other brilliant contemporaries. If intuition and analysis alone do not lead to the goal, it is sometimes mystical experiences, drug use, fraud and radical self-experiments in which unconditional devotion to research is fulfilled. Michael Brooks proves the thesis that research success is often coupled with ruthless persistence and can unscrupulously exceed boundaries. Many of the anecdotes and evidences cited above make it seem to be sneezing and show the shadow side of academic life. They show the reader the weaknesses and human sides of the great spirits. Surprisingly, it is that no more reference is made to Thomas Kuhn ("The Structure of Scientific Revolutions", ID 37/94). The book market currently offers little comparable. The title should be offered far beyond the university environment. (2)

This third volume of the Hamburg city guide deals with the at least architecturally most important part of Hamburg city center. It is the Kontorhaus district with Fritz Höger's masterpiece, the Chilehaus, and the expressionist ballinhaus, now Messberghof. However, Hamburg architecture was not invented by Höger, but rather, the Hamburg cityscape was shaped by architects such as Martin Haller or Albert Erbe. Hamburg city centre is still architecturally an image of the late 19th century, although the expressionism of the 1920s led to an outstanding architectural climax. The buildings built afterwards never again reached the quality of the 1920s, at least not in this density and thus in the shape of the city, as the northern section on Altstädter Straße, which was mainly preserved from the 1930s, shows.

content.text: The environmental impact of climate change is a major change in the environment. In order to mitigate biodiversity losses, adaptation strategies for nature conservation are necessary, e.g. to ensure the permeability of the landscape and (re)networking of protected areas. In order to enable the implementation of these adaptation strategies, an appropriate legal framework must be provided for this purpose. content.text: Controlling for engineers. Controlling represents a goal-, use- and close-pass oriented management concept with which the company can be successfully managed in the short, medium and long term. The goals are recorded in plannings that contain measurable target values. If the actual actual values are measured, the deviations from the plan values can be determined. These deviations trigger a control by adaptation measures to achieve the target or correct the target values. It is distinguished between strategic and operational controlling. The strategic controlling serves to safeguard the existence by determining the long-term goals based on the findings about future market opportunities and risks taking into account the company's own possibilities and strengths. The task of the operational controlling is to ensure the viability of the company (liquidity), an appropriate remuneration of the capital used (returnability) and an optimal cost and performance ratio (economicity). Strategic and operational controlling are explained for all functions of the company. The content - essence of the controlling - plans for the target - tasks of the strategic and operative controlling - controlling in the individual functional areas The target groups - engineer and MBA management.
content.title_en: Controlling for engineers

content.text: The Scrum principle: build and design agile organizations. Faster, more flexible, solution-oriented. In rugby, Scrum is the standard situation to restart the game after a minor rule-into-rule or after a break. From project management to organizations, Scrum can be the decisive move to more agility, especially in management. Scrum reduces the heaviness of classical management approaches by accepting that many developments are not predictable. In practice, this means that self-organized teams achieve above-average results with the help of fewer, but very clear rules and methods in a short time. Consistently solution orientation, clear responsibilities, flexible plan adaptation and very flat hierarchies characterize the methodology. The practical guide shows how Scrum can be integrated into organizations step by step profitably. (publishing text)
content.title_en: Scrum principle: Build and shape agile organizations

content.text: Do it! : The ultimate physics of weight loss. Apolin is a physicist and sports scientist and has written several unconventional physics schoolbooks. In his "ultimative physics of weight loss" (subtitle) he explains humorously and entertainingly, supported by drawings and tables, the natural laws that apply to humans and weight loss. First and foremost, it is about the energy conservation sentence. Whoever wants to lose weight must ensure that the input (food) is less and the output (movement) more. Many nutritional myths, also claims that one can get along with light food, are exposed as lies. Nature scientists interested in the explanations of physics and the calculations may have their fun. [...]
content.title_en: Do this! : The ultimate physics of weight loss

content.text: English garden icons: the creators of the English garden style and their gardens. An exclusive insight into the life and gardens of the driving forces of the English garden scene from the 1960s to today. England is the measure of all things in terms of garden design. Here the great garden designers live and work, here in the last decades a large garden movement has been founded, which with its ideas and visions influences the whole world. In this book the Grande Dames of the contemporary English garden style are presented, from Vita Sackville-West to Beth Chatto to Beatrix Havergal find here the greats of the English garden style, from Vita Sackville-West to Beth Chatto to Beatrix Havergal
content.title_en: English Garden Icons : the creators of the English Garden Style and their Gardens

content.text: Greenpeace: from the hippie movement to the eco-group. F. Uekötter had noted a lack of history of ecological movements ("At the End of Certainties", ID-A 46/11). The American (Environmental) historian Zelko has convincingly worked against this with a historical analysis of Greenpeace. He combines the beginnings, development and internationalization of Greenpeace with the social, political and ecological movements since the 1970s (USA, Canada). The German edition contains a chapter on the beginnings of Greenpeace Germany. "Make It a Green Peace!" (original) refers to the first activists who attached to radical pacifism. Influences of counterculture, the New Left, the ecology movement were added. The fluidly written, material-rich book is full of stories about the violence-free direct actions, but also, on the basis of interviews, about the "couragated characters, intrigues, affections and internal struggles" of the elite cadre (cf. D. MacTaggart: "Rainbow Warrior structured here).
content.title_en: Greenpeace : from the hippie movement to the eco-group

content.text: The "Social Media" generation: how digital communication changes the lives, relationships and learning of young people. The Swiss Gymnasial Teacher and publicist Philippe Wampfler is intensively concerned with the relationship triangle social media, youth and school, besides his blog he already published several books on the topic. The view on the "digital generation" and its (concealed) weaknesses and strengths is often clouded by his own (analog-influenced) experiences and expectations, which make it difficult to objectively evaluate. Wampfler pleads that youth media behaviour is not to be judged from an adult perspective, but based on the needs and criteria of young people. Possible connections between media use and youth development is illustrated by scientific studies, whereby it is often apparent that social media have an influence on developments, but rarely their triggers. Even before Internet times there has been mobbing and people have not only been inclined to "outsource" knowledge since Google. School must prepare young people more strongly for using social media in the sense of sustainable learning. Indications under which youth can be heard three years of play are discussed in the context of the school.
content.title_en: Generation "Social Media": how digital communication changes the lives, relationships and learning of young people

content.text: Architecture as a quote: Forms, motifs and strategies of contemplation. "According to Wolfgang Schenkluhn, the architectural quotation describes "a procedure in which an architecture located in another place is remembered by quoting or adopting certain structures and motifs." Based on this definition, internationally recognized experts investigate the question of the specific appropriation of "pre-shaped forms" in a new architectural context. No specific epoch focus is given, rather, the phenomenon is considered over the centuries. In addition to theoretical reflections on the methodology, the thematic range ranges from early Christian and pre-Romanesque to Gothic architecture, especially the "Halle Churches" and late medieval Saint-Grab buildings, to expressionist architecture and the Gothic reception outside Europe, as in South America and China."
content.title_en: Architecture as quote : Forms, motives and strategies of perception

Creating a psychological diagnosis is part of a more comprehensive intervention in which planning, changing, decision-making and judging play an essential role.
content.title_en: Psychological diagnostics : Basics and fields of application

content.text: Functional safety in the automotive industry: ISO 26262, system engineering based on a safety life cycle and proven management systems. Functional safety (FuSi) in the automotive industry was first described in the standard ISO 26262, published in November 11. In order to meet the growing complexity of functions in the automotive industry and also the increasing requirements for the interdisciplinary project teams, the system engineering approach and the approaches of proven management systems had to be redefined or supplemented accordingly. The present book shows what results from this for the developer. In addition, the way safety mechanisms in hardware and software are implemented is also described. The entire process of system development, starting with the basic requirements in quality management, is presented through the actual system engineering up to the approval of a vehicle and its components for road traffic. The process is also addressed to necessary risk analyses, safety concepts and architectural development. Chapters on product realization in mechanics, electronics and software as well as the subsequent test phase enable the developer to implement the FuSi in practice and meet all standard requirements. Hans-Leo Ross Malvenweg 1246 Dick Germany, Germany Lorves AG.
content.title_en: Functional safety in the automobile: ISO 26262, system engineering based on a safety lifecycle and proven management systems

Engelhardt (ID-B 15/14 - photo and video) and M. Weigend (ID-B 51/13 - programming with Python). All these books do not require any special prior knowledge from the reader and are actually introductions for beginners. The present book goes beyond this and conveys knowledge necessary for more sophisticated electronic crafting. The book starts with hacks (one should say more like: tips and tricks) for commissioning the Raspberry Pi. Most of the following altogether over 60 hacks then focus on using the Raspberry in the house (print server, telephone system, web browser), and the Pirower outside (the micro-mounting of a multimedia.

content.text: The book on Raspberry Pi with Linux. This title is another work on the numerous introductions for beginners to the single-platinum computer Raspberry Pi, which takes a little more into account the operating system Linux, but also gives in step-by-step instructions on the construction of interesting applications with the focus on media servers. The book here is not comparable to the cookbook of M. Simon (in this no.) and does not go as far as E.F. Engelhardt (in this no.). For absolute beginners who do not come from the MINT range, the book is very suitable. A screenshot on the left side is contrasted with the explanatory text on the right side; this facilitates the work. The author starts with basics and a short overview of various Linux distributions and then comes to the media server very helpful at the end with necessary additional purchases (SD card, power supply, keyboard, ...) and a more detailed presentation of the distribution Raspbian and working with Linux. Very helpful at the end hints on Raspi communities (2).

content.text: Developmental psychology of genetic syndromes. The book presents various genetic syndromes associated with learning or mental disability. It describes the specificities in development and behaviour in children with Prader-Willi, Williams-Beuren, Fragilem-X, Sotos, Apert, Cornelia-de-Lange, Cri-du-Chat, Rett and Angelman syndrome. For the new edition, current research findings on the specific development and behavioural characteristics of the individual syndromes were included and a chapter on Down syndrome was added. Thus, the volume contains the most important information on the most common genetic syndromes, which are important for clinical practice and the pedagogical-psychological accompaniment.
content.title_en: Developmental psychology of genetic syndromes

content.text: Disability and Migration: Inclusion, Diversity, Intersectionality. In the social science discourses on the construction of social inequality relations, questions of intersectionality traditionally touch on the triad of ethnicity, gender and class. Disability, however, has not yet been taken into account as a category of difference. Thus, only a few scientific papers on the question of how the difference between disability and other differences in the context of migration and the consequent differentiation along national, ethnic-cultural origins are individually and socially intertwined. However, these interfaces are increasingly focused on the context of the current educational and social perspectives of inclusion (disability) and integration (migration) as well as the recognition of diversity. The present collection contains theoretical perspectives and empirical results of educational and social sciences, social work, health sciences and legal science (disability) and professors. The content · Inclusion, diversity and intersectionality · Life situations and social space · Occupational education and working life of the university.
content.title_en: Disability and migration : inclusion, diversity, intersectionality

content.text: Computer-controlled game partners: forms of media practice between triviality and personality. The examination of computer games offers more than just an occupation with supposed Vexi games between fictionality and reality. Computer games invite us to think about human and artificial intelligence and they encourage us to explore the diagnosis of a "computer society". Not least, the computer-controlled game partners presented in them call for a sociological social theory to work on which can also adapt to non-human entities. But the view on the sociological research state is disillusioned: games in general and computer games in particular hardly receive the attention they receive in the discourses of the mass media. Jonathan Harth therefore devotes himself to media practice in dealing with computer-controlled game partners. It becomes clear that human computer players expect triviality from computer-controlled game partners to a different extent. The content of computer games and their uses is therefore used by computer-controlled game partners as a means of dealing with computer-controlled game partners.
content.title_en: Computerized game partners : Forms of media practice between triviality and personality

content.text: Franz Krause : 1897-1979 : Architect, artist, poet. The architect Franz Krause (1897-1979), who is now almost forgotten, was often at the centre of the avant-garde: whether in 1927 as the construction director of the Stuttgart Werkbundsiedlung at the Weißenhof, during the Third Reich in the Wuppertal working group together with Bauhaus master Oskar Schlemmer and painter Willi Baumeister, after the end of the war as an architect of the Villa Waldfrieden of Wuppertal's paint factory Kurt Herberts, or as a teacher of the local Werkkunstschule and staff of Werner Ruhnau at the Gelsenkirchener Musiktheater - he inspired community projects everywhere through his systematic and at the same time playful way of working. His small styrofoam sculptures, his move play "Vepada" - they are the results of his examination of space and movement, loud poems and speech plays, expressing his experimental reflection. - - This monograph shows for the first time the great spectrum of his artistic, architectural and poetic work.
content.title_en: Franz Krause : 1897-1979 : Architect, artist, poet

content.text: Active imagination: creatively live from inner images. Imagining, the production of inner images, is something that happens constantly as a psychic activity of imagination. In the field of mysticism and religion as well as in shamanic healing practices, there have been imaginary paths of experience for centuries. As a therapeutic means as well as as as a way of self-experience and personality development (individuation), forms of imagination are of particular importance today and are used in all important psychotherapeutic school directions. C. G. Jung has tested the active imagination himself and developed it as a method within his analytical therapies, in which the imagination is not directed by the therapist's guidelines. Seven of the most experienced German-speaking psychoanalysts and psychoanalysts, who are experienced in active imagination, describe this method from a theoretical and application-oriented perspective and thus make it usable for psychotherapeutic practice.
content.title_en: Active imagination : creatively living from inner images

content.text: Reform of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) 2013 and achievement of biodiversity and environmental objectives. The protection and conservation of biodiversity is a social task. The agricultural area covers about half of the area of Germany and the European Union. How it is managed has a decisive influence on the biodiversity of the agricultural landscape. Therefore, agricultural policy and agricultural support are important factors for achieving the biodiversity and environmental objectives as a whole.
content.title_en: Reform of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) 2013 and achievement of biodiversity and environmental objectives

content.text: Net vegetables : raising and caring for the generation Internet. Quitting panic and worries, here comes the only book that parents need to feel no more like digital illiterates in the subjects of Internet, social networks, video games, smartphones and all the other modern stuff. As parents of two adolescents, the authors, both long-standing internet and family dispute experts and Grimme Prize-winners in one of the two areas, can sing a song of suffering when attracting the digital generation. But they promise: After reading »net vegetables«, parents will love the cultural space Internet more than their children do. And they will therefore be able to relax and enjoy their way through the ubiquitous online worlds. The book "is a speculation about digital contemporary culture and Zeitgeist, about education and family, a pleasant reading and a clear recommendation" (blog.dgi-info.de)
content.title_en: Net vegetables : Generation Internet rearing and maintenance

content.text: Mobile spaces: textile buildings - textile buildings. The book shows the development and realization of novel pavilion object buildings as textile multifunctional spaces, designed by Markus Heinsdorff. During the presentation of Germany in India 2012/2013, 16 different buildings were presented on a tour through five Indian megacities and served as mobile exhibition, presentation, conference, concert and event rooms. The pavilion facades show crystalline shapes of ground gemstones by using textile fabric materials. The membranes with corresponding fire protection are translucent and in different colours double or single-walled for different climate regions. All pavilions are screwed or connected with clamping belts and reflect their mobile and environmentally friendly character by the simple repair and recyclability. Furthermore, experiments with universities and engineers are shown to be "environmental membranes", statics in extreme lightweight construction as well as scientific accompaniment of the topic textile construction or membrane construction as temporary, mobile and also permanent buildings.
content.title_en: Mobile spaces : textile buildings - textile buildings

content.text: The second I for the music industry: Talks with musicians about image and career in the media society. Never before has the reputation of artistic personalities been so dependent on media attention as today. Images arise and consolidate themselves in merciless tempo - through PR campaigns, media reports or comments in social networks. How much "Authens" do artists sacrifice in this process of transformation? Can you control their public perceptions at all and how? What relationship do they develop with their audience or with Journa-lists? content.text: Manual CoScience : Research and publishing together with the network. The everyday work of scientists has changed dramatically in recent years. Research, writing and publishing are now strongly influenced by network-based applications. However, the digital age has not only created new technical tools, but has also opened up new ways to generate and disseminate knowledge. This applies both within the academic world and beyond. Working with the network challenges our established scientific practices. Research is increasingly networked, collaborative, multimedia, trans- and interdisciplinary. The present handbook describes these emerging scientific practices. The authors' aim was to write a practical and easy-to-understand manual.
content.title_en: Manual CoScience : Research and publish together with the network

content.text: More or less? : on the sociology of ecological growth criticism and sustainable development. "More or less?" Ecological growth criticism is directed against destructive dynamics of modern industrial and affluent societies that endanger a good life. Concepts of sustainable development also often hold to modern multi-promises too optimistically. However, the mere turning to less offers no better answers. Rather, sustainable development requires the continuous search for coordinated means and purposes. Stephan Lorenz shows that opportunities for this lie in the democratisation of the search processes. The task of the social sciences is to contribute to the improvement of appropriate negotiation procedures. It is about the question: Who and what must be considered how?
content.title_en: More or less? : on the sociology of ecological growth criticism and sustainable development

content.text: The building balance is optimized by means of an optimal thermal insulation by means of insulation, which offers a clear increase in the comfort of living: it saves heating costs and ensures a pleasant living environment. content.text: The crisis of European socialization?: sociological perspectives. European integration has led to a fundamental transformation of social relations and the living situation of people in Europe, especially since the 1990s. While people's lives in the post-war period were primarily carried out within the framework of nation states, the opening of national-state spaces has been accompanied by an increasing cross-border interdependence and a stronger transnational integration of social interactions, attitudes and interpretations. Not only politics and the economy, but also European societies have grown very closely together in recent decades. This transnational socialization pattern is one of the causes of the specific form of the financial and monetary crisis that has shaken Europe since 2008. In this volume, 12 of the most distinguished European researchers from Germany and abroad present their current work on the crisis within Europe and develop independent sociological perspectives.
content.title_en: Crisis of European socialization?: sociological perspectives

content.text: Mediatization research is concerned with the question of how everyday life and institutions, culture and society change by the fact that people are increasingly acting and communicating with and in relation to the media: This process is called mediatization here, because communication is increasingly taking place in media-mediated and mediatised form. For the empirical study, the concept of "social worlds" is used in the various areas of life such as work and family, entertainment and television, everyday life and social relations, politics and learning are all affected by this, but in different ways. In the DFG-funded focus program "Mediatized Worlds", scientists from different disciplines have been studying these issues for several years. In this volume, the research is now not primarily empirical findings but comprehensive theoretical considerations that arise from considerations and empirical results from different projects and disciplines.
content.title_en: The Mediatization of Social Worlds : Synergies of Empirical Research

content.text: Performance Measurement in procurement: a concept comparison. Procurement management is faced with the challenge of changing tasks. These are due, among other things, to new technologies and resource shortages. The modern key performance systems used for success measurement, which are called performance measurement systems, take into account monetary as well as non-monetary measures and link performance measurement with the internal and external requirements of the company. Anja Distelzweig examines possibilities for performance measurement of procurement processes taking into account the most complex range of key performance indicators. In the light of empirical studies, she creates a requirement framework for assessing performance measurement systems in the procurement sector. Here, her focus is on the classic concepts of performance pyramid, quantum performance measurement and balanced scorecard.
content.title_en: Performance Measurement in Procurement : a Concept Comparison

content.text: 24/7: sleepless in late capitalism. The global infrastructure of uninterrupted shopping, working and communicating 24 hours a day and seven days a week is already keeping the entire human race awake. Antislaughter is the new lifestyle product to remain permanently efficient. The night sky is no longer dark. Sleep, while the other basic needs such as hunger, thirst and sex were exploited financially early, remained the only non-controllable retreat from the constraints of capitalism for a long time. Still a hundred years ago, people regularly spent ten hours sleeping. Today's ubiquitous lack of sleep is a symptom of an accelerated life in which personal thoughts and feelings are pushed to the edge. From bed, the author opens his eyes, therefore, asks us to feel at least free in the fields of pause and supposed void. For it is the empty time that is particularly precious.
content.title_en: 24/7 : sleepless in late capitalism

content.text: Digital dictatorship: Total surveillance, data abuse, cyber war. Being monitored by one's own state at every step is a horror vision for many people. Since Edward Snowden's revelations, we know that this has long been a reality. NSA has been secretly becoming the top world surveillance authority, and soon it will intercept, analyze and store all human communication. This is also possible through the spy in the pocket. Smartphones communicate constantly with state listeners without wanting to and noticing it.
content.title_en: Digital dictatorship : Total surveillance, data abuse, cyber war

content.text: The eerie ecologists: are too many people the problem?. This book is against the mixing of ecology and population politics. It represents the ultimately anti-humanist thinking traditions of the population-politically oriented ecologists. Already in the 18th century Thomas R. Malthus saw mankind standing on the abyss - by the uncontrolled increase of the poor. At the beginning of the 20th century Eugenics and immigration critics in the USA and Europe saw their societies degenerate, the spectre was called 'Race Suicide'. In the 1970s, biologist Paul Ehrlich burst the population bomb, a book that in turn stood the Ecopop association godfather, which today wants to reduce the immigration into Switzerland with ecological justification (even more radical than the recently adopted Swiss people) and at the same time demands that a fixed portion of the development aid for family planning be used. These 'unsecret ecologists' are confronted with an understanding of ecology, which represents the people and their fundamental rights into the center. It asks the marginality of the ethnicity of the population and the marginality of the population.
content.title_en: The eerie ecologists : are too many people the problem?

content.text: Perspectives of political opinion research: Demoscopic results in the field of tension between theory, practice and public opinion. Who would you choose if the election of the Bundestag were to take place next Sunday? - In view of the declining bond between parties and voters, Anne Jessen is concerned with the future of this so-called 'Sunday question'. The areas involved in the ‘production' of the demographic results are considered: theory, practice and public opinion. Is the theory on which the Sunday question is based still contemporary? Does the methods used correspond to the scientific standards? How are the results published? In the examination of these questions, the author models a separate approach: the heuristic choice. Based on the question of which voters will use which heuristics for election decision-making, the volatilized decision-making moment of the voter is to be captured. Taking into account the surprising results, a quality improvement of political opinion research can be derived from the content theory of political opinion research.
content.title_en: Perspectives of political opinion research : Demoscopic results in the field of tension between theory, practice and public opinion

content.text: The Kronberger Kreis, scientific advisory board of the Foundation for Market Economy, demands a resumption of energy policy in Germany. If the status quo is continued, the three energy policy objectives - environmental and climate protection, security of supply and cost efficiency - are to be far from being missed. However, the German special route in energy policy would be rather a deterrent example as an international model in the fight against climate change. As a superior climate policy instrument, the Kronberger Kreis recommends strengthening and extending the international CO2 emissions trading and abolishing the EEG. If the policy does not find the power to do so, alternative, market-compliant reforms must be addressed in view of the system-immanent shortcomings of the EEG. To this end, the Kronberger Kreis recommends a certificate-based green electricity quota model according to the Swedish model. In order to induce efficient location decisions for power plants and to promote efficient grid expansion, geographically differentiated prices should also be introduced in electricity wholesale or geographically differentiated grid charges on the producer side.
content.title_en: Restart in energy policy now!

content.text: The results of this study show that tobacco smoke is 79% prevalence for prisoners and 28% for staff. Three quarters of inmates and 68% of staff say they are exposed to the smoke of other tobacco users. Non-smokers take up smoke from a cigarette in the JVAs every day due to passive smoking. Nevertheless, smoking bans, which include detention rooms, are largely rejected by both groups of respondents. The detention often involves the entry into tobacco consumption. Every second currently smoking prisoner has already attempted to try to abstinence during detention. Appropriate assistance is offered in the JVAs, however, the costs have to be borne by the prisoners themselves. As a result, this is particularly mentioned in terms of stress and boredom. While the JVAs are trying not to accommodate nonsmokers together with smokers in a detention room, non-smoking stations have so far been scarcely existential. Based on the results of this study, a large number of recommendations have been formulated and bundled into a package of measures.
content.title_en: Tobacco prevention in prisons

content.text: French and Italian architects at the Dresden court. Through their architectural and artistic mastery, these drawings illustrate the importance of Dresden in the Augustean era. - - The Dresden architecture of this epoch was coined alongside natives mainly by Italian and French builders. During August the strong man with fondness engaged French artists, his son August III became known for Italian art. August the strong man called among others the French architects Zacharias Longuelune and Jean de Bodt as the Kursächsische Oberlandbaumeister. Gaetano Chiaveri brought forms of the Roman late Baroque to Dresden. His main work, the Catholic Court Church, still sets one of the most important accents in the Dresden town silhouette. Giuseppe Galli Bibiena is considered a fuller of baroque theatre construction art, appreciated at many European courts.

At the same time, unveiling platforms à la WikiLeaks offer currently secret and confidential data to a wide public. And more and more companies and political parties want to profit from the data flood on the web. content.text: The efficient person: the dynamics of space and time in mediated working environments.
