content.text: The following are the main reasons for the union mergers of IG BCE and ver.di. Since the late 1980s, the structure of the German trade union system has undergone a sustained change. The number of individual trade unions in the DGB has decreased from 17 to 8 in a decade. As a result, the differences in membership strength have increased considerably, heterogeneous "multi-branch unions" are confronted with smaller industrial unions and professional-oriented associations.The concentration and polarisation process is the result of union mergers. These claim to give an answer to the union recruitment and financial problems and to make organizations "future-capable" in view of the structural change in working life.The work examines in a comparative perspective the causes and motives of the union's activities and the consequences for the unions most important unions in terms of industrial unions in mining, chemistry, energy (IG BCE) and the United Service Union (ver.di). The work examines the causes and the results of the two merger processes. The question of effectiveness of the actors is usually considered to be positive.
content.title_en: With united forces : causes, course and consequences of trade union mergers between IG BCE and ver.di

content.text: If Mother is not happy: the phenomenon of Regretting Motherhood. As long as Mother becomes a natural phenomenon, the claim to happiness did not belong to the mother myth, which still burdened women today and produced "the phenomenon of Regretting Motherhood". Often, however, it was about frustration and ambivalence of mothers, never about regret, too big a taboo. In her study, the author (lastly "Regretting Motherhood", 2015) presents 18 mothers between 25 and 62 with children between 6 months and 39 years. Unlike in G. Gschwend: "Mouth without Love" (BA 12/09), they love their children, but not their role in which they "are no longer themselves, only function as expected of them". Hardly one could imagine beforehand how demanding and paralysing it is to be "7 days a week of 24 hours a mom". They report on tormenting competition among mothers (see C. Kister: "Mouth, your enemy is female, BA/female, and paralysing) of their own identity, BA.
content.title_en: When Mother Don't Make Happy : the Phenomena Regretting Motherhood

content.text: Competition presentations : manual and planning assistance. "Based on global projects from 2009 to 2015, this manual shows the design methods and presentation techniques of internationally renowned architects. Explanations of the technical and formal framework conditions in the presentation of competition contributions as well as questions of expenditure in relation to fees and prize money complement this collection."--
content.title_en: Competition presentations : Manual and planning assistance

content.text: Who survives? : Education decides on the future of humanity. It is not climate, not raw materials, but education that is the key factor for the survival of humanity. Societies in which broad-based education is promoted are now opposed to non-educational, partly fundamentalist, who have no answers to the social and technological challenges of our time. Reiner Klingholz and Wolfgang Lutz make it clear: The line of conflict of the 21st century runs between the educated and the uneducated. "We are in the midst of a struggle of educational cultures," say the experts for population development. And this affects us all, because poverty, despair and terror do not stop at borders. It is time to invest globally in education.
content.title_en: Who survives? : Education decides on the future of humanity

content.text: The defence of paradise : novel. He wants to be a good person. But Heinz lives in a world that no longer allows humanity. Germany is contaminated and devastated, mutants roam around, drones are circling out of control in the sky. Together with his best friend, an electric fox, the Fennek, Heinz grows up in a small group of survivors in the mountains. He takes the chances to preserve the lost civilization, collects forgotten words and writes the history of the last people. But what use does Heinz knowledge and art now? There is suddenly the rumor that far in the West a refugee camp exists. And the group sets off to a murderous march into the supposed paradise. "With his new novel, Thomas von Steinaecker looks into a post-apocalyptic future. However, the world after its demise resembles the world before its demise in a disturbing way.
content.title_en: The Defense of Paradise : Roman

content.text: Huge machines : gigantic transporters, cranes and construction machines. Large format, with color photos and technical data text picture tape about very large, spectacular working machines (mould tippers, big excavators, cranes etc.) from all over the world. (2)
content.title_en: Huge machines : gigantic transporters, cranes and construction machines

content.text: Energetic building renovation: requirements for a fast-effective programme for the environment and work. Nikolaus Richter examines which measures can be effectively accelerated at both the federal and local levels in the implementation of the Federal Government's building renovation programme and how the European building efficiency directive can be used efficiently. This requires networking and interlinking of the various actors: this concerns the design of the legal framework, the funding conditions of the Kreditanstalt für Wiederaufbau (KfW), the financing consulting of credit institutions, the information and advice of owners, the continuous qualification of craftsmen, as well as the planners and architects.If they optimally network in an alliance for work and the environment at the federal, state and local level, the process can be accelerated.The proposals are directed at the relevant actors in politics, business, crafts and trade unions. For reasons of climate protection and to create quickly new jobs, the suggestions should be taken up.
content.title_en: Energetic building renovation: requirements for a fast-acting programme for the environment and work

content.text: The ecological modernization of the company: renewable energies in Lower Saxony; opportunities for new, sustainable jobs. For Lower Saxony, renewable energies have become a sustainable driver of innovation and employment with a total employment effect of 13,000 jobs in 2002 alone. In the Federal Republic of Germany, more than 130,000 people are now employed in this sector. The average growth rates in recent years have been between 20 - 50%. Over the entire value chain, especially in structurally weak sectors such as the steel, shipyard and metal industry, but also in the craft sector, in services including science, research and further education, new jobs are created, existing jobs are secured. Until now, the wind power industry has been driving development in Lower Saxony, primarily with plants for locations in the inland. In the meantime, new, more powerful plants are being developed for wind parks off-shore near the coast. Biomass use with its great potential in the agriculturally shaped land of Lower Saxony is only emerging, photovoltaics, solar, geothermal energy is still little developed.
content.title_en: Ecological modernisation : renewable energies in Lower Saxony; opportunities for new, sustainable jobs

content.text: Reform options for the statutory pension insurance: the effects of the pension reform 2001 and the distribution of the conversion costs; a study by Prognos AG Basel. The pension reform of the Federal Government was finally adopted in May 2001. Key elements of the reform are a new pension adjustment formula and the entry into a publicly funded private pension scheme. The study by Prognos AG examines the long-term effects of the new pension reform. The new pension adjustment formula significantly slows down the expenditure dynamics of the statutory pension insurance and reduces the future increase in the contribution rate. Compared to a development in which pension adjustments follow the net wage dynamics, however, supply gaps are created that need to be closed by private pension schemes. The additional costs for private pension schemes are offset by the lower contribution rate to the GRV. The overall effect of the contribution payments varies depending on age. While younger birth years will benefit from the pension reform, the entry into the funded pension scheme is linked to the transitional costs due to the older ones.
content.title_en: Reform options for statutory pension insurance: impact of the 2001 pension reform and distribution of the changeover costs; a study by Prognos AG Basel

content.text: The subjection of the world: the global history of European expansion 1415-2015. They came, saw and conquered – for 600 years Europeans explored, subjected and exploited the world. But at the same time they have given and received countless impulses for the emergence of our present world. European expansion was not a one-way street, but a process of interaction for centuries. In Wolfgang Reinhard's monumental work, the prehistory of globalization has found a unique overall representation. The renowned historian describes from the early beginnings of European expansion in antiquity and the Middle Ages to the lengthy decolonizations of the 20th century a world-historical process of enormous temporal and spatial dimensions. Whether he reports on the trading systems in Asia or about the artificial world of plantations with their slaves, on ecological consequences or conflict-prone political aftermath of European expansion, his impressive knowledge-rich history is always exciting to read and shaped by interest not only in the Europeans, but also in – the other.
content.title_en: The Subjugation of the World : Global History of European Expansion 1415-2015

content.text: The village of "Unterleuten" somewhere in Brandenburg. Those who take a glimpse of the village by surprise are enchanted by the ancient names of the neighbouring communities, by the quirky originals that shape the place after the turn, by the unspoilt nature with the rare bird species, by the small houses that city refugees from Berlin like to buy themselves to fulfill the dream of an innocent and undefiled life outside the capital hectic. But when an investment company wants to build a wind park in the immediate vicinity of the village, disputes break up again, which were suppressed for a long time. Because there is not only the contrast between the newly attracted Berlin-excellent, who with metropolitan self-righteousness and arrogance and little sensitivity enter into all fat-weaks of the province. There is also the still submissive swarming conflict between the turners and the turners. No wonder that in the village soon the hell is loosed. "Julie Zeh's face-uppologging does not seem to be a ble, the question of the law.
content.title_en: The House of Commons : Roman

content.text: Climate policy : goals, conflicts, solutions. Heat dead in Pakistan, floods in Russia, droughts in California, melting glaciers, crop losses and a century-old wine in Rheingau 2015: The effects of climate change can already be observed on all continents and in all oceans. International climate policy has created a unique body in the World Climate Council, which is fundamental to the agenda of politics. Still, humanity has little experience with the just and efficient use of global common goods. Therefore, climate policy is of particular importance, because it has a role model for international cooperation in many fields.
content.title_en: Climate policy : objectives, conflicts, solutions

content.text: Breakfast power : the perfect start to the day. Collection with over 160 breakfast ideas from the cereal bowl, each consisting of fruit or vegetables, cereals, protein, topping and "dressing" (milk, yogurt or similar). The ingredients are healthy, natural and varied; variants with meat and fish, but also vegetarian and vegan ideas
content.title_en: Breakfast power : the perfect start to the day

content.text: Before the garden is finished, the garden owners will present 15 examples of modern garden design. Review (ekz): The creative garden architect and designer M. Sauer has already convinced with several garden books (see last "Young Garden Design", 2014). In this book, he shows by his own designs how old gardens can be transformed into modern design gardens. Before - after: He describes the initial situation, the wishes of the builders and the individual steps of the realization. He explains his original plans, points to special details and explains the execution of individual works. The result are 15 perfect leisure gardens. Before - after: The photos of the renowned garden photographers J. Becker and V. Michael show the transformation process particularly clearly and stage the extremely successful examples of modern garden design in an atmospheric way. (2)
content.title_en: Before After Gardens : modern garden design plan correctly

content.text: Tell us math! : Learning mathematics in kindergarten and at the beginning of school. The team of authors (mainly professors) wants to raise awareness of everyday situations in day-to-day day care, which have the potential to acquire and practice mathematical skills. First, it differentiates between arithmetic and geometric awareness (numbers and operations, or space and form with measurements and comparisons). Chapter 2 shows what skills and knowledge are required to verbalize mathematics, i.e. writing with technical words, using prepositions and adverbs, narrating math experiences, explaining and experimenting. Finally, the learning possibilities are shown in the building corner, reading picture books, using rules and traditional games. (2S)
content.title_en: Tell me math! : Learning mathematics in kindergarten and at school

content.text: The potential and risks of imported tree species: tree species portraits with a nature conservation assessment. Sustainable, multifunctional forestry has the aim of maintaining and exploiting forests in such a way that their productivity, rejuvenation capacity, vitality and biodiversity are preserved. In the past, it has been shown that neither in the keel water of the raw wood production nor in that of nature conservation all forest functions are adequately fulfilled. The integration of imported tree species into a forest building on ecological foundations therefore requires compromises which can be found on the basis of scientific knowledge. Specifically, this means that the cultivation of non-invasive imported tree species is accepted to some extent by nature conservation, as well as by forestry of natural protection interests are taken into account by respecting a spatial order of cultivation and by reducing existing occurrences of invasive tree species. Against this background, the aim is to highlight the potential and risks of 15 imported tree species on the basis of scientific literature and long-term research work on experimental areas of the various research facilities and cultivation areas of the forest farms in order to discuss the potential and risks of imported tree species.
content.title_en: Potentials and risks of imported tree species : tree species portraits with nature conservation assessment

content.text: Risk. The concept of risk, which is theoretically based on society, assumes that "risk" belongs to the class of problems of modern society, which is "cross" to its functional systems: risks cannot then be concentrated on a special functional system (economic, scientific or political), they are structurally linked to the system of modern society. As outlined in the volume focusing on system-theoretical risk research, research problems are essentially related to the possibility of understanding between decision-makers and those concerned, to the "rationalizability" of risky decisions and to the importance of non-dissolvable knowledge. In the ecological context, these aspects culminate in the insoluble problem of "self-hazardment of society".
content.title_en: Risk

content.text: Media, systems, networks: elements of a theory of cyber networks. Everyone talks about networks and networks. What has been lacking so far in media science is an empirically resilient and theoretically sufficiently complex theory of threads, nodes, networks and networks. Media epistemologist Stefan Weber is facing this task with this book. Is the Internet a medium or merely technical infrastructure? Is the World Wide Web an autopoietic system? Are networks systems? - Questions of this kind dominate the net scientific debate and testify to conceptual confusion in the face of the new media. Weber's text is the attempt to clean up the corridor. Empirically, the theory proposal leads to a structured observation of micro- to macro-trends of net medialization: 'viralization', self-referenceialization, human/machine dedifferentiation, dedualization of classical communication relations and the re-dualization of binary social structures. »The first attempt at a coherent theory of networks, a long overdue book that combines current media and system theory.« Peter Weibel, media theorists and artists.
content.title_en: Media, Systems, Networks : Elements of a Theory of Cyber Networks

content.text: The self-sense of consciousness: the person - the psyche - the signature. It is no secret that what we call person, consciousness, psyche, individual, etc., seems to evaporate in the advanced theories of sociology and philosophy. It is becoming increasingly clear that the consciousness to which tradition had attributed an own value is overformed by social processes. It cannot observe itself without discovering itself as an individual generality. Peter Fuchs' instructive essay deals with this problem. Explores the terrain of the question of consciousness - in connection with important concepts of proximity such as person, psyche, individual - at the level and with the means of system theory, i.e. one of the theories that seem to be massively threatening the self-value of consciousness. The concept of individual signature and its counter-drawing is used in all its preliminality to open up the space of discussion of the problem.
content.title_en: The self-sense of consciousness: the person - the psyche - the signature

content.text: Micrology: literary and philosophical figures of the small. Micrology - these are the little things, the little things. They often appear as insignificant, cute, exposed to the sight of the small. But does their logos exhaust themselves in this (apparent) weakness? The present essays discover other potentials of the small. In literature and philosophy, the basic, the disturbing, the density, the fantastic world-tenancy are detected. The authors put an historical space on exemplary objects from the 17th to the 21st century and explore the small as a motivating, formal, epistemical and poetic instance. The micrological research shows that the germ-like, monadic and atomic relation to the big and the whole has enormously provoked the literary and philosophical imagination. The volume deals with works by Walter Benjamin, Adalbert Stifter, Samuel Beckett, Franz Kafka, Heinrich von Kleist and Virginia Woolf.
content.title_en: Micrology : literary and philosophical figures of the little one

content.text: Optical magic: the history of visual media in the early modern era. »Optical magic« is the title of a series of publications written in the 17th century by Jesuit scholars to represent the field of optics by means of art-ready stagings. Novel media such as the Laterna magica or the anamorphosis created illusions with which an audience should be entertained and formed. This particular approach to visual techniques by authors such as Schott and Kircher is examined in the present study in terms of media and cultural history and is defined as part of a baroque culture of appearance that has moved between representation, manipulation and lust for show.
content.title_en: Optical magic : about the history of visual media in the early modern era

content.text: Analog/Digital - Opposition or Continuum? : on the theory and history of a distinction. The opposition of the 'new digital' to the 'old analog' media is found in advertising, pop culture, business, politics and science. Apparently, the distinction analog/digital has developed into the paradigmatic leading difference of the late 20th and early 21st century. But what exactly does 'analog' or 'digital' mean in different contexts and are there not also transitions between both forms? When does the distinction appear and in what context? By addressing these and other questions from different perspectives, it eliminates a considerable research deficit not only in the media sciences.
content.title_en: Analog/Digital - Opposition or Continuum? : on the theory and history of a distinction

content.text: Innovation. How does a catchword transform into a scientific concept? The volume by Holger Braun-Thürmann looks at this question and develops a »sociology of innovation«. The systematically structured text provides information on how innovations can be understood as phenomena of social change. For this purpose, the author integrates the basic concepts of innovation studies into a sociology of innovation. The volume examines the complexity of the phenomenon of innovation, which is usually only considered from the point of view of the competitive advantage and the increase in productivity.
content.title_en: Innovation

content.text: At@elier and Poetszimmer in neuen Medienwelten : About the current situation of artists' and literary houses. In the course of the historical and media change at the end of the 20th century, the location, space and architecture of the exhibition and the process of exhibiting have radically changed. The extensive illustrated volume provides insight into current exhibition aesthetics of artists' and literary houses. Contributions from theory and practice reflect multifacetedly the new forms and possibilities of staging and exhibiting art and literature, of image and text, as well as artistic biographies and life forms in the media age.
content.title_en: At@elier and Poets' Room in New Media Worlds : On the Current Situation of Artists' and Literature Houses

content.text: Perception - Cognition - Aesthetics : Neurobiology and Media Science. Perception, cognition and aesthetics can be understood as different forms of processing and expression of a basic biological equipment of man. Whether these are stable or whether they are culturally overformed or even transformed, forms the central media anthropological question of the volume. In this process, it is examined what kind of reciprocal impulses are, which can lead to cultural and biological changes, what effect they have and what duration they have. These questions are not directed solely at processes of perception, cognitive or aesthetic habituation, but rather at the physiological conditions. With the participation of proven researchers from the fields of biology, medicine and brain research, this volume opens up Neuland in the border area of natural and cultural sciences.
content.title_en: Perception - Cognition - Aesthetics : Neurobiology and Media Studies

content.text: In this book, renowned economic geographers look at these changes and design alternatives to dominant neoclassical-inspired positions. In dialogue with the philosophy of science, cultural studies, heterodox economics and organizational sociology, central topics such as cultural economy, networks and evolution are negotiated. The volume thus becomes a plea for pluralistic, transdisciplinary access to the frequently broken geography of a globalized economy. With contributions by Ash Amin, Trevor Barnes, Gernot Grabher and Ron Martin.
content.title_en: Reflections on a different geography of economy

content.text: Apples and pears: illegitimate comparisons in cultural studies. Pluralism of objects and methods is considered to be a characteristic of cultural research. Nevertheless, comparative studies are concerned, which disregard cultural and media historical differences, to throw together the accusation of apples and pears. The contributions gathered here make this offense a topic. They test forms, problems and possibilities of illegitimate comparisons by confronting phenomena from historically distant cultural contexts as well as representations in different media. Elisabeth Bronfen opens the volume with the presentation of the reading process developed by her, the cross-mapping. Further contributions by Jörn Ahrens, Silke Förschler, Steffen Greschonig, Julia B. Köhne, Karsten Lichau, Iulia-Karin Patrut, Markus Rautzenberg, Tilo Renz, Wiebke-Marie Stock, Alexandra Tacke, Daniel Tyradellis and Horst Wenzel.
content.title_en: Apples and pears : illegitimate comparisons in cultural studies

content.text: The ununderstood culture: Perspectives of a critical theory of media society. Ununderstood culture is the search for the set-up of a cultural theory of media society - with the aim of renewing a critical communication science. In a time that is characterized as never before by the omnipresentity and abundance of mass media communication, we need a critical understanding of the culture that emerges from it. The book aims to contribute to conceptually and conceptually grasping this media culture. In search of an illumination of our current media society, the text follows historical and current socio-cultural debates.
content.title_en: The Ununderstood Culture : Perspectives of a Critical Theory of Media Society

content.text: Does nature disappear? : the actor-network theory in the environmental sociological discussion. Modern societies, according to the common thesis of the main actors of the actor-network theory (ANT), develop a program of strict distinction between the areas of nature and society, which excludes the area of nature from social responsibility. But now it turns out that this limitation has always been fiction, the border between nature and society begins to blur, nature seems to disappear as a separate area from the social one. What consequences does this have with regard to ecological problems? What does this mean for environmental sociology? What potential does the ANT open up in this regard?
content.title_en: Does nature disappear? : the actor-network theory in the environmental sociological discussion

content.text: Evolution and Race : Theoretical and institutional change in Victorian anthropology. How did the evolution-theoretical transformation of racial theories take place in the context of the so-called Darwinian revolution? This question is only answered at first glance by the large number of ideological-historical works, for they leave the concrete conditions of this change in the dark. Thomas Gondermann subverts the social formations in Darwin's environment, their racial-theoretical approaches and scientific-political campaigns of a meticulous investigation. This shows the interplay of the social and cognitive dimension of the evolution-theoretical change of racial theories and sets out its close social relationship to the establishment of evolutionary theories in the natural sciences.
content.title_en: Evolution and race : Theoretical and institutional change in Victorian anthropology

content.text: »Gender and science«: Perspectives in the natural and engineering sciences. The book offers an introduction to the broad spectrum of gender research in the most diverse scientific disciplines. It aims to stimulate a broad, university-wide dialogue and to show ways of effectively integrating the perspective of equal opportunities into the quality management of the university through the consideration of gender aspects in research and teaching. Scientists, especially from the natural and engineering sciences, present their concepts and projects and provide an insight into the diverse aspects and interrelationships of »science and gender«. The publication is aimed at a broad-defined audience of students and scientists from different scientific disciplines.
content.title_en: »Gender and science«: Perspectives in the Natural and Engineering Sciences

content.text: Doing Time : The temporal aesthetics of food, drink and lifestyles. This study represents an attempt to capture practices of eating and drinking in an original way in the temporal dimension. By linking elements of a social theory of time with approaches from lifestyle research, meals can be understood as episodes of everyday life. The coupling of meal times and time styles is illustrated and currently followed by the example of "time pioneers" and "flexible people". Empirical findings meet with demanding theoretical foundations.
content.title_en: Doing Time : The temporal aesthetics of food, drink and lifestyles

content.text: Interface Art - Mediation : Model project 2005/2006. Seven art schools in Lower Saxony carried out projects along the interface between art production and educational work in 2005 and 2006. They dealt with strategies of contemporary art based on process, cooperation and intervention. The book offers a reflection and theorisation of these project experiences and shows both the problems and the potential of work in the space between art and education. It wants to give new impulses for art mediation, to stimulate own experiments and to further think about it. The participatory research process proves that it is possible to analyze and describe the complexity of the processes in such projects and to understand the participation of the actors as a constituent for the process of knowledge.
content.title_en: Interface Art - Communication : Model project 2005/2006

content.text: Places of tourism : A spatial and social theoretical study. Why space? What significance do spatial forms and spatial semantics have for the construction, stabilization and change of social structures? Using the example of modern (city) tourism, the book poses these questions and shows that space serves as a medium for the formation of expectations, among other things. At the same time, the social and spatial theoretical analysis pursues the goal of using the potentials of system theory for the sharpening of a social theory of space.
content.title_en: Places of tourism : A spatial and social theoretical study

content.text: Aesthetics of objectivity: genesis and function of a scientific and artistic style in the 19th century. Objectivity is a style characteristic - strategically used and historically changeable. Cultural and historical research has increasingly made the history of objectivity a topic, but only a little attention has been paid to the lines of contact between art and natural science. In fact, the art historians, medical scientists, writers and artists of the 19th century had a common theme: the search for the "true image". What is artistic truth and what constitutes a scientific process was discussed in all its breadth in both art and science. The two cultural figures of the "artist" and the "scientist" were configured in parallel with a contemporary gender discourse, which was incorporated into the new definition of objectivity. The volume deals with the prehistory of today's separation of art and science, and is also a contribution to the history of visual objectivity.
content.title_en: Aesthetics of Objectivity : genesis and function of a scientific and artistic style in the 19th century

content.text: Media in space and time : dimensional relationships of the media. Media has always helped to re-order relationships between space and time. At the latest since the 19th century they have penetrated our daily work, leisure and science, so that the question of the change of space-time configurations arises historically. In view of the media-based insights into the micro- and macro-space of our life-worldly environment, the perception of the subject is influenced by itself in particular. The aim of the book is to narrow the cultural process of this self-reflection multiperspectively.
content.title_en: Media in space and time : Media dimensions

content.text: Virtual worlds as basic technology for art and culture? : an inventory. What role do virtual worlds play for art and culture? content.text: Retablissement : Prussian urban architecture in Poland and Germany. The cityscape of numerous cities formerly situated in Prussia is still today characterized by the systematic urban reconstruction carried out by the Prussian bureaucracy in the 18th and early 19th century. "Retablissement" was called the contemporary key concept of this particular form of urban development. This meant the reconstruction of the city, which was mainly bureaucratically directed and centrally organized, planned, or the gradual improvement of the structural situation of cities. The objectives of this urban reconstruction consisted in improving fire safety, hygiene, but also legal certainty, commercial regulation and the production of a well-ordered prospective, thus uniformly arranged street and square space. Urban architecture, legal and economic principles were applied to each other in the narrowest possible way. The bilingual volume gathers contributions from Polish and German art historians who cover the foundations of the Prussian urban reconstruction as well as exemplary case studies of the diverse urban construction measures.
content.title_en: Retablissement : Prussian urban design in Poland and Germany

content.text: Tambora and the year without summer: how a volcano plunged the world into crisis. In 1816 the climate was crazy. Winter brought extreme cold; floods caused enormous floods in Asia. In Western Europe as in North America the "year without summer" was experienced. No one knew the cause at that time: it was the eruption of the volcano Tambora in today's Indonesia - the largest volcanic eruption in human history. In his book, renowned climate historian Wolfgang Behringer tells for the first time the global history of this climate catastrophe, which plunged the world into political and social crises for years. Through miserly harvests in 1817 became the "year of hunger". There followed plagues, the entire regions paralyzed, huge waves of emigration, political unrest and assassinations, which caused a pre-revolutionary mood. In Germany the Jews were made to the sin bol of misery, in South Africa the witches, and in China the world undermined the authority of the state. Never before all these events were related to their common origin, the Tambora outbreak, and the situation of the Islamic civilization, the situation of the Islamic Republic, and the situation of the Islamic Republic of India dramatically.

content.text: The ideal tool for quoting digital sources and project materials -- The Internet and electronic media are of course everyday things for scientists, lecturers and students. It is only logical that the new media and the possibilities for their use are reflected in scientific work. However, the basic rules of scientific source work are still based on paper. Many questions about working with the Internet and electronic sources have not yet been answered by uniform standards. -- The dual degree programmes, with their project-oriented final papers, represent a new, third form of scientific work alongside purely theoretical literature work and empirical research work. However, the basic rules of source work have never been developed for the publications of companies or even for internal documents. Here, too, there is a gap between grown rules and the requirements of dual final papers. -- In this book, the scientific source work will be presented to you with special consideration of Internet, electronic and company-internal sources. content.text: The condom : on the history of sexuality from the Empire to the present. Scientific monograph on the condom - an object which not only served the protection against venereal diseases and the regulation of births, but was subject to moral evaluation to the highest degree. König examines the development and interpretation of the condom as a material means and as a symbolic expression of sexual behaviour in four political systems: the Empire, the Weimar Republic, National Socialism and the Federal Republic. In the officient moral of the Empire, the condom was still considered an embodiment of fornication. Since the interwar period it has been increasingly integrated into sexual life. Only in the post-war period, however, it has become an accepted everyday subject, promoted by liberalisations of sexual morality and sexual criminal law as well as the fight against AIDS. - The study covers various aspects of the condom between technology and society - from rubber-technical improvements, advertising campaigns and distribution channels to moral positions and legal regulations. - The prostitution in the Helenstraße in Bremen is dealt with on pages 73-80.
content.title_en: The condom : about the history of sexuality from the Empire to the present

content.text: The weather experiment: from sky observers and the pioneers of meteorology. At the beginning of the 19th century a storm was still considered a judgment of God, and those who wanted to know how the weather became were happy to keep frogs in their glass. Superstition and religious dogmas stood in the way of meteorology progress. But with the fearless curiosity of enlightened spirits a generation of science pioneers made themselves aware of the secrets of the atmosphere. They classified clouds, described the strength of the wind, explored icy heights in the hot air balloon, discovered how electricity could be used to transmit weather warnings, and deciphered the mysterious vortexes of the air currents. Some paid a high price for it - existences were ruined, reputations destroyed, competitors cleared out of the way. Lively and knowledgeful Peter Moore tells the changeable story of the stormy beginnings of one of the most natural things in the world: the weather forecast
content.title_en: The Weather Experiment : by Himmelsbeowatchers and the Pioneers of Meteorology

content.text: History without Epochs? : an essay. Publisher's info: The famous medieval expert Jacques Le Goff concludes at the end of his life: Throw the outdated epoch division overboard! In his last work he formulates his sensational thesis on historiography. And he shows that there was more continuity than break between the Middle Ages and the Renaissance. Jacques Le Goff, the most famous international medieval expert, returns at the end of his life to the fundamental questions of his guild. Why do we divide history into epochs at all? Is the Renaissance really the birth hour for modern people for bright, luminous thinking for us, or, thanks to the new knowledge about the achievements of the Middle Ages, one must not rather see both historical phases in context? Le Goff shows us not only the instruments of the epoch division, but also with its help he examines the various spiritual, technical and economic changes until the French Revolution. But this also brings us back to the questions which our own standards of historical progress and change are. A fundamental contribution to history and to the presentation of history is thus successful.
content.title_en: History without Epochs? : an Essay

content.text: Artificial Intelligence - When do the machines take over?. Everyone knows them. Smartphones that talk to us, wristwatches that record our health data, workflows that automatically organize themselves, cars, aircraft and drones that control themselves, traffic and energy systems with autonomous logistics or robots that explore distant planets are technical examples of a networked world of intelligent systems. They show us that our everyday life is already determined by AI functions. Also biological organisms are examples of intelligent systems that have emerged in evolution and can solve more or less independently problems efficiently. Occasionally, however, nature is a model for technical developments. Often, however, computer science and engineering science find solutions that are even better and more efficient than in nature. Since their creation, AI research has been linked to great visions about the future of mankind. Does the "artificial intelligence" thus solve people? This book is a plea for engineering: AI must be a service in society. What is AI? -- A brief history of AI -- Logical thinking become automatically -- systems become experts - Robots learn - Robots - Evolution - Robots learn - Robots - Robots become a factory

content.text: Gardeners do not wage wars: Prussia's Arkadien and the German division. The Prussian castles and gardens along the Havel River became one of the locations of the Cold War after August 13, 1961. Today's UNESCO World Heritage Site was located in the middle of the German-German border area. Walls, border fences and death strips destroyed more than 30 hectares of a unique cultural landscape. Lenné's grandiose idea of the visual axes was turned into negatives, because Grenzer wanted to free field of vision and fire to prevent escapes. Paths and hills were removed, park architectures destroyed and large areas devased with plant poison. After the reunification of divided Germany, the destruction of the gardens followed the elaborate restoration of the German territory. Today, the dream world of the Prussian Arkadien between Potsdam and Berlin is once again a visitor magnet for tourists from all over the world.
content.title_en: Gardeners do not wage wars : Prussia's Arcadia and the German division

content.text: The message of the last heroes against Hitler : 18 encounters. Whether resistance fighters or Holocaust survivors - the life paths of these special people impress especially in our so troubled today. Because to stand up against Hitler, to survive his reign of terror and yet not to struggle with fate, but to stand up again and again, to meet life positively and with a great yes, makes courage for the handling of terror and war, escape and expulsion - topics that today are again of oppressive topicality. Tim Preöse has accompanied some of these last witnesses over many years and tells in 18 portraits of their life and their message: a plea of the unfit for more tolerance and against forgetting
content.title_en: The message of the last heroes against Hitler : 18 meetings

content.text: Writing digitally : how the Internet changes our everyday communication : with 21 pictures. Writing on the Internet has long been a major part of our everyday communication. We maintain our contacts with it, organize our appointments, we inform friends about where we are and what we do exactly, or we simply spend the time waiting for the bus or sitting on the train. All this is possible only because most of us are equipped with a small device and so practically always and everywhere 'online'. Can the communication outside the Internet be completely unaffected by it? The answer is certainly: no. How exactly writing on the Internet has changed our everyday communication and further changes, this essay wants to clarify
content.title_en: Writing digitally : how the Internet changes our everyday communication : with 21 illustrations

content.text: Mobile hacking: a compact introduction to penetration testing of mobile applications - iOS, Android and Windows Mobile. The widespread spread of mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets is increasingly causing security problems. This topic has already been addressed by B. Hauser or A. Hoog. The present book deals with many examples of how data is protected in mobile data transmission and how it is associated with security issues in the event of theft or loss of a device. The remarks take into account the common operating systems. The author begins with a short introduction to the operating systems and their applications and shows how to set up work environments for an app analysis. Subsequently, the final chapter on data attacks on the transport route (Man - in the - Middle-attack, SSL-Strip-attack, ...) is briefly discussed. In the main part, many analysis and defense tools are presented.
content.title_en: Mobile hacking: a compact entry into penetration testing of mobile applications - iOS, Android and Windows Mobile

content.text: Along the world : the magic of the poet's landscapes. Guests at the places of life and longing of Friederike Mayröcker, Yuri Andruchovytsch, Marica Bodrožić, Karl-Markus Gauss, Ludwig Hartinger - Aleš Šteger, Monika Helfer - Michael Köhlmeier, Bodo Hell, Hubert von Goisern, Alfred Komarek, Brigitte Kronauer, Robert Menasse, Adolf Muschg, Martin Pollack, Ilma Rakusa, Jaroslav Rudiš, Ilija Trojanow
content.title_en: Along the world : the magic of the poet's landscapes

content.text: The "Neue Frankfurt" was a cultural stronghold of the Weimar Republic. Under the term "Neue Frankfurt", a period of history of architecture and culture began to pioneer. The editors and authors are looking for links and cooperations between politics and culture, between urban planning, architecture, art, graphic use, literature and music. In four introductory essays and about 150 individual biographies, the book presents known and unknown actors of the departure in the Frankfurt of the Weimar Republic.
content.title_en: Actors of the New Frankfurt

content.text: The book is particularly interesting for those who are concerned with corruption, Latin America and development. Through this, local translations of global strategies include potential to continue to emancipate from the dominant development discourse. It is interesting for those who are concerned with corruption, Latin America and development work. Through this, local translations of global strategies are able to continue to emancipate from the dominant development discourse.
content.title_en: Fighting corruption in Paraguay and Chile : exploring the local embedding of the international anti-corruption discourse from a post-development perspective

content.text: AgroCity - the city for Africa. Publishing info: The cities are growing as fast as on the African continent today. Since independence, i.e. since the 1960s, eight new million cities have been built almost out of nowhere - from Lilongwe (Malawi) and Dodoma (Tansania) to Abuja (Nigeria) and Yamoussoukro (Elfenbein Coast). In these chaotic megacities European modernism dominates. An "African" architecture, indeed an African urbanity, must first emerge. "AgroCity" is a contribution to this. Reports from different urban suburbs show the difference between townships, mining cities and slums. Essays deal with questions such as: When will a city become a city? How could an African city once look and be worth living? How can farmers and farmers become people with urban orientation? Because the growth of cities in Africa is also the result of a mass-fledged, overused and exuberant soils on the one hand, and how can this long-termed, over-repeassurance of a social backdrop present to the city in the same.
content.title_en: AgroCity - the city for Africa

content.text: From Poland to Germany and back: labour migration and its challenges for Europe. This book deals with labour migration from Poland to Germany after the enlargement of the EU in May 2004. Individual contributions deal with the new legal situation and the related shift of migration flows towards the countries that opened up their labour markets. Furthermore, the authors focus on the different migrant groups and discuss the structure and forms of the new migration as well as the role of migration networks. The focus is on the transnational practices of migrants and their social positioning. Subsequently, the consequences of labour migration in an open European area as well as the challenges of transnational migration for the understanding of social integration in Europe are discussed.
content.title_en: From Poland to Germany and back: labour migration and its challenges for Europe

content.text: Freedom and control: the history of the slave who was not released to the end. Klappentext: One of the defining experiences of the present day is that the eternal discord between freedom and control is raising with new sharpness: individuals and society are confronted with an unprecedented diversity of freedom options. On the other hand, however, the technical possibilities and the widely felt need for more and more control - be it of their own body, borders or the whole world. Starting from the concrete manifestations of this dialectic in recent debates about digital surveillance and self-tracking, big data and bureaucracy, Markus Metz and Georg Seeßlen ask to what extent the today blatant contradictions between freedom and control ultimately insoluble and where they are merely ideology.
content.title_en: Freedom and Control: the History of the Slave Unfinished

content.text: Science and technology studies: classical positions and current perspectives. In recent decades, the Science and Technology Studies (STS) has created a research field that is fundamentally re-orienting the relationship between science, technology and society. This volume for the first time gathers central texts of the STS in German, including Bruno Latour, David Bloor, Michel Callon, Donna Haraway and Karen Barad, and also provides overviews of all important research areas and theoretical positions. This has resulted in a fundamental introduction to this innovative research direction, which also draws an interim review of the development of the STS and explores current challenges and debates.
content.title_en: Science and technology studies : classic positions and current perspectives

content.text: Polycentral metropolitan regions. "The focus of the volume is traditionally polycentral urban regions, whose complex spatial structures and interdependencies, development processes and governance arrangements are examined internationally in cross-sectional contributions and thirteen case studies."--
content.title_en: Polycentral metropolitan regions

content.text: Farewell to the myth : six decades of Cuban revolution : a critical review. The history of Cuba since the revolution in 1958, which is presented here, is at the same time the story of the failure of a socialist utopia. Review: While biographies of Castro are not lacking (most recently J. Sanchez: 2015), monographs on Cuba have been surprisingly rare in recent years. The former hope country has been struggling with a disastrous economic situation since the end of the USSR and the economic decline of Venezuela at least. Bahrmann, who has previously been engaged in journalistic research on the change ("Chronicle of the Turn", 2010), but also studied Latin American studies in Rostock, is here a reference to the country's history since the revolution in 1958 as a history of failure of a socialist utopia, which, according to his assessment, has ended in a dictatorship. His judgment on Che Guevara, who is still considered an icon of the revolution, is particularly negative. Bahrmann's argumentation is generally conclusive, he has used the sources, which he could have been able to make public in the form of a literature list.
content.title_en: Farewell to the myth : six decades of Cuban revolution : a critical assessment

content.text: Police Communitarism : a practical research of urban crime prevention. In urban agglomerations, population groups, scenes and milieu meet with different practices and values. Local conditions and security situations become more confusing. Here the police are called upon to provide a remedy with knowledge, trust and relationship work. In addition to their core business, the persecution of crimes and the prevention of danger, they establish the prevention work. Different forms of this specific police work are presented in the volume through ethnographic practice research. (Verlagswerbung)
content.title_en: Police Communitarism: a Practical Research on Urban Crime Prevention

content.text: The stones of Venice. Ruskin thought about the survival of Venice. Concerned that many buildings could be irrevocably lost in future due to the increasing industrialization, he produced hundreds of drawings, portrayed details of facades and entire houses, drew churches and basilicas, and thus tried to capture in image and description the dying beauty of the Serenissima. With the »The Stones of Venice« John Ruskin made important contributions to the theory of architecture. »The Stones of Venice« is characterized by an idealized representation of the Gothic in Venice, including its social circumstances. Moreover, the »Stones« contain precise representations and descriptions of Venetian architecture and painting, especially of Tintoretto, which are of great interest for structural analysis to this day. This new edition of the »Stones of Venice« also contains the daguerotypes, which were discovered and restored in 2006. They are shown for the first time in a German book publication: »Two collectors have discovered unknown daguerotypes of John Ruskin. The recordings of the Venetian Alps are now presented in Frankfurt.« The »Senscape of the Alps« and the Stones of Venice.
content.title_en: The Stones of Venice

content.text: Understanding autism : External and internal views. The topic of autism has experienced a considerable economic boom in recent years. Not least, a wealth of autobiographical reports by those affected about autistic perception, thinking and acting has called into question the widespread clinical-pathologising view of autism. The book aims to understand the views of autistic persons and to compare them with scientific findings, especially from the field of neuroscience. Neuroscientific findings shed a completely new light on the abilities and intelligence of people in the autism spectrum. The characteristics developed here are then examined by autistic persons themselves - in a sense from the 'inner view': perception particularities, unusual learning behaviour, focused thinking, difficulties in communication and social interaction, etc. Professor Dr. Georg Theunissen has the chair of mental-disability education and pedagogy in autism at Halle-Wittenberg University.
content.title_en: Understanding autism : external and internal views

content.text: Behind the wall - small town houses on and on the city walls. With the series of writings EINBLICKE the view over the recognizable "outer" architecture is directed to the interior of the small town houses, whose spatial conditions are an expression of the former prevailing living conditions and social structures. In this volume so-called wall houses are in the center. They formed a considerable part of the building stock in some cities. The background of their creation, the builders and residents, their structural shape and internal division as well as the reasons for their largely forgotten are reported in detail on selected cities of North-West Germany. The narrow, almost without exception desolatingly built houses on the inside of the city walls were indeed "small houses", but legally in general they were citizen houses. In another focus of the volume it is again on the topic of "behelfsheime".
content.title_en: Behind the Wall - small town houses on and on the city wall

content.text: Manual Industrie 4.0 / Birgit Vogel-Heuser, Thomas Bauernhansl, Michael ten Hompel, Editor ; Vol. 1: Production. The reissue of the successful work will continue the history of the fourth industrial revolution and take into account the dynamics with which this vision has been further developed and realized over the past two to three years. Experts from science and technology will illuminate various facets of Industry 4.0 and also create an overview of the state of the art and the vision itself. This will succeed not least with a good mix of scientific findings, practical examples and overview contributions. Thematically, the spectrum of basic technologies (e.g. cyber-physical systems) and integration and migration approaches to business models and services will be addressed. In addition to data security, legal aspects will also be addressed. The second edition has been edited and expanded, now appears in 4 volumes. This first volume covers the new and renewed contributions to Industry 4.0 in production. (Verlagstext)
content.title_en: Manual Industry 4.0 / Birgit Vogel-Heuser, Thomas Bauernhansl, Michael ten Hompel, Editor ; Vol. 1: Production

content.text: Migration, inclusion and integration: sociological observations of sport. Sports are involved in three ways in the social changes caused by migration, inclusion and integration: not only are they affected and responsible, but are also considered problem solvers. The resulting complexity is also increased by the fact that sport has corresponding structural features as a self-conspicuous social subsystem. These are carefully involved in scientific analyses as well as social debates, if one does not want to run the risk of making premature and simplifying statements. This collection presents itself with this challenge by combining different observations on migration, inclusion and integration in sport in a sociological overview and allowing differentiated insights into these subject areas.
content.title_en: Migration, inclusion and integration : sociological observations of sport

content.text: The practical manual Library construction covers all topics relating to the construction and equipment of libraries: From planning to the selection of locations, the outdoor facilities, space programmes, competition procedures, financing models, laws and norms, library facilities, technical infrastructure, transport systems, training rooms, accessibility etc. to moving and evaluation according to reference. The volume contains an extensive bibliography on the topic of the Green Library. Ecological sustainability in library construction and equipmentLocation selection; outdoor space typologies at libraries; process steps for the realization of an innovative building project. The example of the common library building of University and University Osnabrück on the Westerberg campus; the youth library. Experience and communication location The children's library ; Makerspaces -- library rooms for makers; the future-capable bib office; accessibility -- a challenge? ; environment condition: light ; floor coverings for libraries ; participative design ; space requirements of university libraries Building libraries in stock ; library construction - or: the love of the existing library.
content.title_en: Practical manual for library construction : planning – design – operation

content.text: City of the Commonists : new urban spaces of the do it yourself. It is no longer to be overlooked: a new generation of do-it-yourself activists uses the post-Fordist city as a laboratory for social, political, ecological and aesthetic experiments. Whether in the community garden or in FabLab, whether in open-air workshops
content.title_en: City of the Commonists : new urban spaces of the do it yourself

content.text: Test planning : Optimizing products and processes. "Every new or further development of products and manufacturing processes undergoes a variety of experiments. But experiments cost time and money, and some results are not reproducible. Test planning (also called DOE=Design of Experiments) helps to obtain reproducible results with as little effort as possible. This book shows practitioners in development, construction and manufacturing, as well as students how test planning can optimize products and processes."
content.title_en: Experimental planning : Optimizing products and processes

content.text: The study and the study of the subject are not carried out in a systematic and graphic way. The most drawings do this because of lack of or insufficient form and position tolerance and thus cause quality defects, rework or scrap. This teaching and manual explains the form, position and dimension tolerance in a systematic and descriptive way. Essentially - the formation of reference systems on which the toleration builds - the linking of tolerances in dimensional chains and by the maximum material condition as well as the connection with the quality system. The book supports the handling of tolerances by 200 guiding rules as well as many practical examples. It can be used as a textbook, but also as a reference work and is excellently suitable for self-study.
content.title_en: Form and position tolerances : Manual for study and practice

content.text: Plastics technology: Introduction and basics. A book not only for the student of plastics technology, but also for the beginner in this exciting industry: - The entire plastic technology is presented in a coherent manner. The main core of the book are the three chapters: Materials technology, processing technology and product development. - New insights into the relationships believed to be known are explained: The book shows, for example, that 'elastic' is often said when 'extensive' is meant. That there is actually no 'swim/tough transition'. It is not called 'wall thickness', but 'wall thickness' and there is no 'polymer processing', since polymers are not plastics. - Due to many requests from listeners of lecture events and lectures, a chapter 'plastic and environment' is included. - QR codes link to videos that illustrate the presented content and represent a better learning/mechanism. Now in 2nd edition! Univ.-Prof. Dr.-Ing. Christian Bonten leads the Institute of Plastics Technology in Stuttgart, one of the leading fields of plastics technology, the Institute of plastics technology.
content.title_en: Plastics technology : Introduction and basics

content.text: The digital caliphate: the secret power of the Islamic State. The "Islamic State" is based on two pillars: on its territory and on a digital infrastructure with which it is highly efficiently organized. Abdel Bari Atwan, who has travelled the IS area and conducted countless interviews with jihadists, offers insights into the digital institutions and command structures of the IS for the first time in his book and presents its leading minds. Many computer games fascinate by the connection of medieval ambience and high-tech. This is precisely where for many jihadists lies the fascination of IS, which maintains an "medieval" order with the help of the Internet. The tax system is oriented towards the Koran, but is digitally organized. The financial system is based on the prohibition of interest, but manages the state budget and revenues from oil exports, antiques trading and abduction with electronic crypto currencies. Education ensures Koranic reading, but also digitally competent young people - IS also female. The propaganda apparatus relies on the staging of violence and employs an entire army of photographers, video filmers and game developers. Atwans always want to be defiant of the cyber-alarms.
content.title_en: The digital caliphate: the secret power of the Islamic State

content.text: The book describes the transformation of the world and the world through the Reformation. On 31 October 2017, the publication of the 95 theses that Martin Luther published at the door of the castle church in Wittenberg is a 500th anniversary. On this occasion, the scientific advisory board "Reformation Jubilee 2017" reminds us of the role that the Reformation played in the emergence of modernity. Because the impulses that Wittenberg had in the 16th century changed Germany, Europe and the world sustainably. The authors, all members of the advisory board, show in their contributions how Protestantism has shaped law, constitution and other worldly institutions of modernity. "Nevertheless, we should not do so, Di Fabio, as if the reformers had set freedom, equality and democracy on a straight track of modernization and enlightenment" (165). That one may now hold a place of worship or not be indispensable in the face of the appeal of the Reformation.
content.title_en: World impact of the Reformation: how Protestantism has changed our world

content.text: Building-integrated solar technology: Architecture with photovoltaic and solar thermal systems. Despite falling feed-in tariffs, renewable energies are still on the rise in the building sector. The increasingly cost-effective photovoltaic systems and battery storage systems contribute to this. But the legislator also has big plans: By 2050 the German building stock should be almost climate-neutral. -- The technologies for a successful, decentralized energy transition are largely available today. But how do they use them meaningfully? And how can the design challenges in integrating photovoltaic and solar thermal systems into buildings be solved? This book gives answers. It was written by an interdisciplinary team of architects, civil engineers, physicists and environmental engineers and deals with all the knowledge about the available solar energy systems, their standardisation and approval, the integration into the building technology as well as the integration into the building envelope.
content.title_en: Building integrated solar technology : Design architecture with photovoltaics and solar thermals

content.text: Diversity instead of demarcation: where does Germany steer in the struggle for immigration and refugees?. In 10 chapters authors from various social areas shed light on the situation in Germany with regard to the refugee and immigration situation and how this makes the mood between selfless engagement and right propaganda ominously fluctuate
content.title_en: Diversity instead of demarcation: where does Germany steer in the struggle for immigration and refugees?

content.text: Mathematical Methods of Physics. "The work introduces mathematical concepts and their applications and is ideally suited to both lecture-accompanying and self-study due to the many examples of this work". "This work introduces classical mathematical concepts and their applications and is designed to parallel a lecture course. Numerous examples also make it an ideal comparison for self-study"--
content.title_en: Mathematical Methods of Physics

content.text: Metamorphoses of Death : Funeral Cultures and Beyond Conceptions in Change - from Ancient Egypt to the Friedwald of the Present. Verlagsinfo: The question of how to deal with dead bodies is as old as humanity itself. Funeral rites have a long shelf life and are deeply rooted in one's own culture. When they have changed for what reasons and with what consequences, the main question of this collection volume is
content.title_en: Metamorphoses of Death : Funeral Cultures and Beyond Concepts in Change - from Ancient Egypt to the Friedwald of the Present

content.text: Sustainable urban development: Infrastructures, actors, discourses. Urban development and policy have been under the postulate of sustainable development since the 1990s at the latest. But what does it mean for cities to realize a "Local Agenda 21"? The volume combines contributions from an interdisciplinary research group, supplemented by comments from other scientists. (Verlagstext)
content.title_en: Sustainable urban development : Infrastructures, actors, discourses

content.text: On the occasion of Stephen Hawking's 75th birthday on 08.01.2017, the small book will be published in pocket format. It contains excerpts from the well-known books of S. Hawking: "My Short Story", "Einstein's Dream" and "The Great Design". In addition, two previously unpublished works by Stephen Hawking and Bernd Schuh about "Black Holes" are included. The author is gladly read and can present the difficult questions of theoretical physics and cosmology in a popular scientific way. (2)
content.title_en: "A wonderful time to live"

content.text: The origin of Islam : the first hundred years : from Mohammed to the world empire of the Caliphs. Within only a hundred years the Islam and the world empire of the Caliphs arose and profoundly changed the political and cultural coordinates of the world. Lutz Berger explains this "miracle" from the change of the late Antiquity societies and describes how Islam formed hand in hand with the Arab conquests. Much speculation has been made about the sudden appearance of Islam in the 7th century: Was it originally a Christian or Jewish sect? Which sources is the Koran going back to? Lutz Berger shows on the basis of recent research, how in the competition of monotheistic religions of salvation from Mecca spread out an Arab game with its own prophet and holy book and the fragmented Arabian peninsula satisfied. This was the prerequisite for vast conquests, which went surprisingly smoothly everywhere where one wanted to escape the access of the Byzantine or Sassanid Great Empire. By the inclusion of the Persian heritage a completely new culture emerged, while the civilization of the north-west was culturally preserved - the origin of the ancient Europe - the first hundred years : the origin of Islam was: the first century : the world empire of the calips.
content.title_en: The Origin of Islam : the First Hundred Years : from Mohammed to the World Empire of the Caliphs

content.text: Open Spaces - spaces of religious and spiritual diversity. There are numerous examples of the encounter between different religions in modern civil society. In the design of multi-religious spaces, the encounter gives expression and concrete form. In airports, hospitals, former churches or universities, in landscape parks, parliament buildings and schools, they can be found. This volume presents the variety of such spaces based on the images of an exhibition. In the contributions from different perspectives of theology, art and religious sciences, architecture, photography and sociology, various aspects are reflected which are important for the design. The book describes facts and illustrates the current state of affairs. Meetings and projects succeed and fail, good and sustainable concepts are needed. The volume provides a comprehensive basis for those who plan to create such a space.
content.title_en: Open Spaces - Spaces of Religious and Spiritual Diversity

content.text: Homogeneous areas : from soil classes are homogenous areas - technical and legal impacts on VOB Part C 2016. "The book explains the new classification of soils in civil engineering, their impact and risks, so that engineers can make the right assumptions for planning and tendering. First experiences, assessments and examples from practice in the tendering process and the application show how to deal with the new homogenous areas."-
content.title_en: Homogeneous areas : from soil classes are homogenous areas - technical and legal impacts on VOB Part C 2016

content.text: Introduction to IT management: basics, implementation, best practice. The tasks in IT management are exciting and responsible, but often enough confusing for beginners. Olaf Resch shows you how prospective IT managers master their demanding subject with analytical and goal-oriented procedures: - basics and correlations of IT management - presentation of a generic IT management model - selected best practices and pragmatics - IT governance - as a comprehensive practical example - With many exercises, interactively networked via an accompanying wiki New consideration was given to the increasingly important area of cyber security and the management of complex corporate architectures in the 4th edition of the popular introduction work. In addition to COBIT 5 and ITIL, TOGAF and IT basic protection are now also being treated.
content.title_en: Introduction to IT management : basics, implementation, best practice

content.text: The Amok puzzle: psychological explanations and perpetrator profiles. Publisher's info: What drives a amok runner to kill a seemingly arbitrary selection of people? Why are most perpetrators male? And are there differences between adult and juvenile perpetrators? Christoph Paulus presents the results of one of the largest German amok studies. The sample comprises a total of 58 cases, 46 amok runners and 12 so-called "riding-board drivers", which, although pronounced amok threats, did not seriously consider them. A network of conditions and circumstances emerge, all of which provide clues on whether and why not all people who had a hard childhood or played first person shooters become amok runners. The solution of the amok puzzle is not as easy as the pose of these questions. The author gives the first comprehensive analysis framework to the examination.
content.title_en: The Amok Puzzle : psychological explanations and perpetrator profiles

content.text: Exploratory authoring of interactive content in a live environment. Visualisations are essentially based on two approaches. On the one hand, standard diagrams can be quickly created with little effort. On the other hand, there is the possibility of programming individual and interactive visualizations. However, this is associated with a significantly higher effort. Flower enables the rapid creation of individual and interactive visualizations by greatly simplifying the development process and directly supporting users in the individual activities such as importing and processing data, their mapping on visual elements and the integration of interactivity.
content.title_en: Exploratory authoring of interactive content in a live environment

content.text: Aseptic production. "This second edition of the DIN pocket book contains essential standards for the aseptic production of products for health care. ... The aseptic process is divided into basic operations (e.g. sterilization of product or product components including sterile filtration, assembly of components, handling and storage of sterilized products). It is necessary that possible sources of contamination of materials, components, product, personnel, equipment, equipment and devices are considered and minimized."--
content.title_en: Aseptic production

content.text: "Thoughts travel, ideas arrive": the world of note. "Losing a passport was the least of all evils – losing a notebook was a catastrophe," writes probably the most famous notebook aficionado, the British novelist Bruce Chatwin in his bestseller »Traumpfade«. Even in the digital age, the analog keeping of handwritten records on various writing materials, preferably in self-fabricated or varied notebooks in trade, seems indispensable to the writers. The »transportable writing laboratories« are easy to carry with them, need no electricity and even survive wind and weather. They are quickly drawn when, as the title quote says, thoughts travel and ideas arrive. Notebooks contain excerpts or work notes, serve as memory memories or as a discrete recording instrument of a participating observer, even as a medium of knowledge. In the current volume, the curtain opens for notes among others by Johann Nestroy, Josef Strauss, Theodoro Fontane, Heimito of Dharmo, and his own Babel, and his own note by Ludwig Hohl.
content.title_en: "Thoughts travel, ideas arrive" : the world of note

content.text: The 6th edition of the bicycle technology specialist gives the necessary technical knowledge, which are listed in the training framework plan for the company training and in the framework curriculum for the training in the basic and specialized level of the vocational school. It is the standard work of the general bicycle technology and is also indispensable as reference work in two-wheeled enterprises. The contents comply with the applicable technical rules, the statutory regulations as well as the technical regulations, in particular the DIN standards. Questions of environmental protection and occupational safety are adequately taken into account. In 2015 the DIN EN ISO 4210 safety technical requirements for bicycles came into force. In many places in the technical book important decisions and test procedures are included. They make clear to the two-wheeled mechatronics specialists what importance safety requirements have in the use of bicycles. All components of the bicycle are described in detail. New bicycle construction methods and lightweight constructions, the use of new materials, the increased requirements to product safety, service and customer wishes are taken into account. In addition, knowledge on ergonomics, the adaptation of the human being taught to the bicycle machine.
content.title_en: Technical knowledge Bicycle technology

metadata.authors: Artmann, Ulrich; Brust, Ernst; Leiner, Jens; Hertel, Dietmar; Bellersheim, Rüdiger; Herkendell, Franz; Gressmann, Michael

content.text: Criticism of the political economy today: Contemporary Marx. In 2017, the first volume of Karl Marx's main work "Capital" is about 150 years old. And a year later, his author would have become 200 years old. Reason enough to ask why Marx's works are still and increasingly point of reference for capitalist analyses after such a long time. However, those who speak of political economy today must beware of misunderstandings. What was still common in the 19th century, what still shaped the style of scientific discussion with economics in Germany and the USA, is no longer playing a role today. Neoclassics is understood by its protagonists above all as non-political science. Whoever today speaks of political economy, must expect it to be a rebel, a Marxist or – even worse – a sociologist, and to be despised by the "real" economists. Therefore, today, the criticism of the unpolitical economy is factually about this: ruthless criticism of the dogmas and pseudo theories, the credibility of the recent crisis of Marx's major time-time system.
content.title_en: Criticism of the political economy today : Contemporary Marx

content.text: EU enlargement and labour migration: ways of gradually approaching labour markets. The study "EU enlargement and labour migration" was prepared by the ifo Institute for Economic Research, Munich, in the research area Social Policy and Employment Markets and completed in December 2000. The study was commissioned by the Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs. The study focuses on the impact of the planned EU enlargement on labour markets and public finances in the Federal Republic of Germany. To reduce the migration potential after the EU enlargement, the ifo Institute has been working on ecometrically based simulation calculations relating to the five population s - the strongest candidate countries. The European legal aspects of the issue were dealt with by employees of the Max Planck Institute for Foreign and International Social Law, Munich, with which the ifo Institute cooperated in the preparation of the study. The content responsibility of the authors of the Max Planck Institute extends to chapters 3 and 5.
content.title_en: EU enlargement and labour migration: ways to progressively bring labour markets closer together

content.text: American steel grades : Guide for comparing American steel grades with EN or DIN standards. "This pocket allows a rapid comparison of American steel grades with similar steel grades according to EN and DIN and is intended as a guide for finding the corresponding steel grades. The majority of steel designations were taken from the ASTM standards, followed by SAE, API, AMS steels, AWS welding additives and UNS steel designations."
content.title_en: American steel grades : Guide to comparing American steel grades with EN or DIN standards
